tasks.title: messaging: quiet hours in both zones, area-code table, night exceptions

tasks.title: messaging: outbox that never sends twice, sender directory

tasks.goal: Inbound texts and delivery-status callbacks are de-duplicated by Twilio's message ID, and every text's status (queued, delivered, failed, undelivered) is recorded from the callbacks (TXT-012, TXT-013).

tasks.title: messaging: sole-word opt-out in English and Spanish, one confirmation, no text after
tasks.goal: A text that is only an opt-out word (English or Spanish, any case) or contains a listed revocation phrase opts the number out of every text at once with exactly one confirmation within 5 minutes; nothing else goes to it until START, 21610 failures are never retried, every revocation channel feeds one suppression list, and the provider's Advanced Opt-Out matches the app's words (CON-008 to CON-011, CON-013 to CON-017, CON-030, CON-032, CON-035). tasks.title: messaging: HELP, INFO, AYUDA and START replies
tasks.goal: HELP, INFO or AYUDA gets the CON-018 reply within 5 minutes at any hour, even from an opted-out number, with the help email, askhava.com/help, the reply-time line from the settings and the LIST and roaming lines, and START re-subscribes (CON-018).

tasks.title: jobs: the twelve statuses, allowed moves and status history
tasks.goal: Every job has exactly one of the twelve statuses and moves only along the architecture's arrows, any other move refused and logged as a bug; every change writes an audit row; every waiting status has a timeout; and timers live in the database, survive a restart and do nothing if the job has moved on (JOB-001 to JOB-003, JOB-005, JOB-006).

tasks.goal: Every waiting status has its timer on the business clock or the emergency clock: Open to No quotes yet at 6 p.m. the next day, No quotes yet and Quotes ready closing after 5 and 3 days with their texts, Awaiting confirm and Payment pending returning to Quotes ready, Connected moving on DONE or closing after the check-ins, and `jobs::api::all_windows_ended`, the entry point `quotes` calls once every card's quote window has ended, which sends the all-quotes-in text and closes a job with no choosable quote left (the trigger is T046's, D-491) (JOB-007 to JOB-015, JOB-025, JOB-026, TXT-042).

tasks.title: jobs: same-moment collisions resolved by row lock and expected status

tasks.title: licensing: agency-licensed categories and boundary job types
tasks.goal: `licensing::rules` routes agency-licensed categories only to their licensees (Department of Agriculture pest licensees by attestation, alarm, camera, inspection and septic boards) and no-license categories only to businesses matching the city list, and splits the boundary job types (dryer vents, holiday lights, appliances, pools) between no-license, handyman and licensed work (LIC-011 to LIC-016, LIC-028 to LIC-031, LIC-047).

tasks.goal: Handyman quotes for construction work of $1,000 or more (top of any range) are refused with the limit explained, gas, hardwired smoke-alarm, sprinkler and permit-type jobs never reach a handyman whatever the AI says, the split-job check blocks a second job at the same address within 30 days, and every handyman quote carries the certification box and the disclaimer line (AI-012, LIC-019 to LIC-025, LIC-036). tasks.goal: Quote cards show the license line with its check date and link (ROC or other agency), the license-since year from the state record, the city-license line for no-license businesses and business-reported insurance where it applies, and never a rating, review count or ranking from Ask Hava (LIC-026, LIC-032, LIC-034, LIC-037, LIC-038, WORD-016). With matching in place, this task also adds to intake's `routing.rs` (T043's, extended here) the INT-017 count line, N counted through `quotes::api` as CARD-001 would send it then, and its Not covered branch when no active business in the town covers the job, and INT-032's SPLIT offer when no business's license covers every candidate job type, with SPLIT or DIVIDIR making two requests (TD-INT-25, TD-INT-29, D-491).

(FEE-045, TD-CARD-07, moved from TD-FEE-28, D-491). (D-493)

tasks.title: quotes: original wording beside any summary, quote facts, and the business lines on each quote card

tasks.title: quotes: first-quote text, update texts at most every 3 hours

tasks.title: intake: 24-hour reminder, 72-hour close, AI outage message, everyone hears back
tasks.goal: An Intake job with no reply gets one reminder at 24 hours and closes at 72 hours with the INT-019 text; and every new request hears back within 24 hours by text, email or a call-back alert to Casey (INT-019, INT-021, INT-023). tasks.goal: The homeowner's quote page, reached by an unguessable salted 128-bit token that stops working 30 days after close, shows every eligible quote numbered in arrival order with the WORD-005 lines, adds quotes as they arrive with a Pick button from the first one, marks an ineligible business's quote "no longer available", and shows no names, phones or addresses (PICK-008 to PICK-012, WORD-005, SEC-037). tasks.title: Accessibility suite: axe at 320/768/1280 on every route, structure, reflow, targets

tasks.title: CI for the Rust workspace: pinned Postgres service, cache, coverage floors, sqlx prepare check, one boundary build
tasks.goal: Ci pins the Postgres service image by digest, caches the Cargo registry and target with Swatinem/rust-cache pinned by commit SHA (keyed on Cargo.lock and the toolchain, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, dev profile debug = line-tables-only), installs cargo-audit, cargo-deny, sqlx-cli and cargo-llvm-cov from pinned prebuilt binaries, runs `sqlx migrate run` then `cargo sqlx prepare --workspace --check -- --all-targets --all-features` so stale offline query data fails, measures branch coverage in its own parallel job on a nightly pinned by date against tests/coverage_floor.json (this task writes the file with the measured total and the 95% floors for app/payments, app/catalog fee rules, app/privacy and app/licensing), fails any PR that lowers a floor, and keeps `cargo build -p askhava-server --locked` as the one boundary build (no per-crate clippy runs) (D-453, D-479, D-481). tasks.title: adapters and payments: a refund is recorded as Stripe reports it (pending, succeeded, failed, canceled), never as done on a 200
tasks.goal: `PaymentsAdapter::create_refund` returns only the `re_…` ID (`app/adapters/src/payments.rs`), so `refunds::finish` treats any answer as `Refunded`, sets the row `succeeded` and appends the ledger `refund` entry, and `reconcile::own_refund` counts any answer as refunded, even when Stripe answered `pending`, `requires_action`, `failed` or `canceled` (external audit A03, D-1753; D-1545 (2) already recorded the ledger side). (1) The typed refund is additive for production callers (this task is a `harness` task because four DONE tasks' test fakes gain one trait impl each): `app/payments/src/refund_stripe.rs` defines a payments-owned trait `RefundStripe: PaymentsAdapter` (the `IntentStripe` and `ReconcileStripe` pattern) with `refund(idempotency, payment_intent) -> Refund` and `fetch_refund(id) -> Refund`, where `Refund { id, state, amount_cents, currency, payment_intent }` and `RefundState::{Pending, RequiresAction, Succeeded, Failed, Canceled}`; an unknown state string is an error, never a success, and the refund must name the PaymentIntent asked for. It is implemented for `StripeHttp` there, over two new inherent HTTP calls on `StripeHttp` in `app/adapters/src/payments.rs` (the `PaymentsAdapter` trait and its `create_refund` stay unchanged until T132 retires `create_refund`). `refunds::finish`, the retry and `reconcile::own_refund` take `&impl RefundStripe`, and so do the public functions that reach them: `request_refund`, `run_refund_retry` and `early_fraud_warning` (`app/payments/src/refunds.rs:78`–`:135`), `reconcile` and `run_reconcile` (`app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:125`, `:424`) and T064's `run_late_refund` (`app/payments/src/late.rs:112`). The fakes in `tests/integration/tests/disputes.rs`, `late_success.rs`, `reconcile.rs` and `ledger_1000_jobs.rs` each gain one `impl RefundStripe` whose `refund` answers `Succeeded` with the ID their `create_refund` already returns and whose `fetch_refund` answers the same; nothing else in those files changes (no blanket impl over `PaymentsAdapter`, which would conflict with the `StripeHttp` impl). (2) A second case pins the other branch: a listener that accepts the connection and closes it without answering gives `Err(AdapterError::OutcomeUnknown)` (TD-SEC-59). Acceptance: both cases pass 200 times in a row under `cargo test -p askhava-adapters` with the crate's other tests in parallel (stand-ins included); no other test changes and no assertion is weakened. tasks.title: jobs: each job keeps its category code and remaining candidate job type codes as append-only narrowing rows, for the fee at the pick
tasks.goal: Seventh audit N7-01 (D-2330; INT-018, FEE-005, FEE-045; D-2210): no table stores a job's category or job types (`jobs.job` has no such column), so the pick's fee uses defaults (D-2210's known gap). `migrations/0164_jobs_job_facts.sql` adds `jobs.job_facts`, append-only narrowing rows: job ID, a per-job sequence number (primary key with the job), the catalog category code, the remaining candidate job type codes as a non-empty text array, set at; app role SELECT and INSERT only, so no row is ever changed or deleted. `app/jobs/src/job_facts.rs`, through `jobs::api`, offers `record_job_facts(tx, job, category, job_types)` and `job_facts(conn, job)`. The first row is written at card send. A later row may only narrow: the same category and a candidate set that is a subset of the latest row's; the same set again writes nothing (idempotent); anything else (another category, a set with a code not in the latest row, an empty set) is refused and writes nothing. `record_job_facts` locks the job's `jobs.job` row first, so two narrowings at once are applied one after the other. `job_facts` returns the latest row (highest sequence number), or none. Codes only: every fact derived from them (fee-free, visit tier, one-time or recurring) is resolved from catalog data at the pick (T340), never stored here (national-ready). Callers: T251's card sender writes the first row in the transaction that sends the cards, on the approval and the emergency path; T162's intake order writes a narrowing row whenever a later answer settles or narrows the job type (on the emergency path the trade questions come after the cards, INT-029). Tests in `tests/integration/tests/job_facts.rs` (TD-JOB-17). Update the `jobs` `CLAUDE.md`, add the new table's line to the `jobs` part of the module notes in `docs/architecture.md` (found by grep, never loaded whole; D-3079) and `docs/decisions.md`; the module table of section 3 is locked in `kit/plan.lock` and a build task cannot rewrite the lock, so the next plan change adds `jobs.job_facts` to its `jobs` row (D-3112, as T334's hand-in left its new table).

tasks.title: payments: a Confirm needs the current card-authorization wording accepted, and the version a Confirm needs is never below the wording's
tasks.goal: Brand rename prep (D-3347; FEE-007, FEE-015, D-072). A Confirm is allowed only when the business's highest accepted `payments.card_authorization.version` is at least `payments.fee_terms.authorization_version` (`service.rs` `may_confirm`, about line 363); a fee-mode switch raises that stored number by one (`rules.rs` `FeeTerms::switched`, `service.rs` `switch_fee_mode`); saving a card stores `AUTHORIZATION_VERSION` with `AUTHORIZATION_TEXT` (`insert_card`), and `accept_authorization` stores the terms' version with the text it is given. One number therefore stands for two things, the fee mode and the wording, and a version check alone misses a wording change: with the wording at version 2, a mode switch to 3 and then a wording change to 3, every business that accepted the switch already holds 3, so nobody accepts the new wording. Each acceptance row stores its `text`, so the wording is checked by its text, with no migration or schema change. (1) `pick_fee.rs` gains `pub const fn required_version(stored: i32) -> i32`, the larger of `stored` and `AUTHORIZATION_VERSION`; `fee_terms_in_force`, its `FOR SHARE` twin and `switch_fee_mode` build `FeeTerms` with it before use and before `switched`, so a mode switch always lands above every version a card save has stored (a migration raising the row cannot be numbered at T428's serial position, V9, D-3347). This keeps the mode-switch rule. (2) The wording rule: a pure function `authorized(accepted: &[(i32, &str)], required: i32, current_text: &str) -> bool` in `pick_fee.rs` is true only when the business's highest accepted version is at least `required` and at least one accepted row's text equals `current_text` byte for byte; `may_confirm` reads the business's `(version, text)` rows (one query, `payments.card_authorization`, its own rows only) and calls it with `AUTHORIZATION_TEXT`, returning `ConfirmError::NewAuthorizationNeeded` exactly where it does today plus when the current wording was never accepted. Every other path of `may_confirm` and every error stays. (3) `app/payments/src/tests/authorization_floor.rs` (unit, no database): `required_version` below, at and above `AUTHORIZATION_VERSION` returns the larger, and `i32::MAX` gives `i32::MAX` with `switched` returning none; `switched` after `required_version(stored)` is above `AUTHORIZATION_VERSION` for every stored number from 1 to it; and the sequence the plan review found, played through `authorized` with explicit texts and versions: the business accepts wording W2 at version 2 (authorized at required 2); a mode switch makes required 3 (not authorized), it accepts at 3 with W2 (authorized); the wording changes to W3 at version 3, required still 3: not authorized until a row with W3 is accepted, then authorized; a row with W3 at a version below required is not enough. Under today's constants every existing test passes unchanged, `tests/integration/tests/fee_fixed_at_pick.rs` included (its businesses accept `AUTHORIZATION_TEXT` first); if one does not, stop and report the file. Money code: branch coverage stays at or above 95% (BUILD_BRIEF.md:481). Update `app/payments/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: portals: every homeowner Verify code is bound to its purpose by a local challenge with a try cap
tasks.goal: Pentest PT-03 and the PT-02 gap beyond the report (D-2348; SEC-055, SEC-008, PRIV-031). One Twilio Verify service serves every purpose and `VerifyAdapter::check_code(to, code)` (`app/adapters/src/verify.rs:50`, :86) is not bound to one, so `confirm_request` (`app/portals/src/data_download.rs:210`) acts on any of her open requests (up to 30 days old) after any passing code for her phone, the sign-in code included, and homeowner sign-in (`finish_sign_in`, `app/portals/src/homeowner_portal.rs:164`) keeps no local challenge; neither has an app-side try cap. Build: (1) `migrations/0176_portals_code_challenge.sql` adds `portals.code_challenge` (ID, purpose `homeowner_signin`, `data_copy` or `data_delete`, subject ID (her contact for sign-in, the request for copy and delete), sent at, used at, tries; app role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of `tries` and `used_at` only). (2) `app/portals/src/code_challenge.rs`: the rule (SEC-055): a challenge lives as long as the Verify code (10 minutes from its first send, the `SEND_WINDOW_SECONDS` both files use); a send (`send_sign_in_code`, `open_request` and a new `resend_request_code` for an open request) made while an unused challenge of that purpose and subject is still alive reuses it and does not reset its tries or its send time, because Twilio keeps one pending code per number for its life, so the cap is truly 5 per code; a send after the newest challenge expired or was used opens a new one; each is written in a short committed transaction before Verify is called. A check is refused before Verify is called unless the newest unused, unexpired challenge of that purpose and subject exists; it reserves a try against that challenge by one atomic `UPDATE ... SET tries = tries + 1 WHERE id = $1 AND used_at IS NULL AND tries < CODE_TRIES RETURNING`, committed before the Verify call (the cap is `business_auth::CODE_TRIES`, the same constant as T272; a reservation never comes back, so a crash or a timeout uses a try); a right code then uses the challenge with a conditional `UPDATE ... SET used_at = $2 WHERE id = $1 AND used_at IS NULL` in the same transaction as the action it confirms (the session start, or the confirmed audit row with the copy or the delete), and when no row changes (a second right check got there first) the action rolls back and nothing is done twice. No pooled connection, transaction or reservation is held across the Verify await (pentest PT-04's availability side, D-2349): `send_sign_in_code`, `finish_sign_in`, `open_request`, `confirm_request` and `resend_request_code` take `&PgPool` in place of `&mut PgConnection` and acquire a connection only for each short database step, releasing it before Verify is called; T307 calls them with the router's pool. Picks' codes and business sign-in keep their own rows (T272 binds the business code to its sent challenge). (3) No change to `stand_ins/twilio.py`: it keys a verification by `to` only, which is the shared-service model these tests need. Tests in `tests/security/tests/code_purpose.rs` (TD-SEC-60): a code sent for one purpose is refused for another before Verify is called (a sign-in code cannot confirm a delete whose own challenge expired or was used; a pick code cannot sign in); 20 simultaneous wrong checks reach Verify at most 5 times and the sixth is refused; a used challenge is refused; a right code and the action commit together; a re-send inside the code's life reuses the challenge and gives no more tries, and one after expiry or use opens a new one; two simultaneous right checks act once; with a fake Verify that hangs, 30 concurrent sends and checks leave a pool of 5 connections able to serve another request (the matrix's AVAIL-01). Update the `portals` `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md`, and add this task's line to the off-database records and recovery notes of `docs/architecture.md` (found by grep, never loaded whole; D-3079, D-3286).

(3) `app/server/tests/door_matrix.rs` (new; a test crate may not depend on `askhava-server`, D-736, so the HTTP probe lives in the server crate): against `server::build_router` over a real test database, the same six actors as the matrix (anonymous, homeowners A and B, businesses X and Y, the owner, signed in the way `auth_matrix.rs` signs them in) send every method of every section 13 row reading `yes` whose path falls under those five doors (the same prefix rules, restated in the file): a `Homeowner` route admits A and B only, to their own records (A's page never names B's job or token), and gives anyone else a 4xx with a link to `/h/sign-in` and no detail; a `Business` route admits X and Y only, a `{pick}` or `{complaint}` of the other business is the one not-found answer, and anyone else gets a 4xx with a link to `/b/sign-in` and no homeowner detail; an `Owner` route admits only the owner and gives anyone else a 4xx with a link to `/owner/sign-in`; an `ActionLink` route opens only for the token minted for that kind, object and member (`portals::api` minting, as T148's tests do), a `GET` changes nothing (SEC-026), and a token for another kind, object or member, or none, is the one not-found answer; a `Public` route answers every actor's `GET` without a session and its body holds none of the fixtures' names, phones, addresses, tokens or job numbers. tasks.title: calls: a PIN draw fails only when the OS source fails, and one failed draw costs one draw

tasks.title: server, ops and payments: the Stripe-or-webhook-errors and failed-health-check alerts are raised (D-3877)
tasks.goal: Plan change D-3877 (Fable's pre-claim check of T105, reviewed in two rounds): OPS-004 alerts Casey when "Stripe or webhook errors last over 30 minutes" and when "the 5-minute health check fails twice", but no task raises either alert and no alert kind exists for them on `main` ff584ab; T105 raises the other OPS-004 alerts. (1) Webhook outcomes: a layer on the `/webhooks` routes in the new `app/server/src/vendor_alerts.rs`, added in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs`, writes one `ops` audit row (action `server.webhook_error`, the route's code name as subject kind, a fresh UUID per request as `subject_id`, `app/ops/src/models.rs:105`; no body, no sender) for each request the app answers with a 5xx, and one `server.webhook_ok` row for the first 2xx on each route in each 5-minute window, keyed on the route and the window start (at most 12 rows an hour per route); the layer keeps no in-memory state, so this holds across restarts and across processes. Each row is written in its own transaction on a fresh connection after the response is decided; a failed write is logged and never changes the response. A refused signature is a security event, not an error. A 5xx caused by the database being down cannot be recorded; the health check below covers that case. (2) Stripe outcomes: the new `app/payments/src/stripe_errors.rs`, re-exported by one `api.rs` line, returns from `payments`' own rows the times of the window's Stripe calls that failed (`AttemptStatus::Unreachable` or no answer, `app/payments/src/charge.rs:280` to `:295`, and failed refunds) and of those that succeeded, times and outcomes only. (3) A worker task in `vendor_alerts.rs`, registered in `server::worker_registry` and first queued from `schedule_start` (`app/server/src/bin/worker.rs:74`) under a dedupe key, runs every 5 minutes. Error runs are tracked separately: one for Stripe and one for each webhook route. A Stripe run is broken only by a successful Stripe call, a webhook run only by a `server.webhook_ok` row on the same route (webhook rows read through T477's `ops` audit-subjects reader, `app/ops/src/audit_subjects.rs`). A run "lasts over 30 minutes" when an error comes 30 minutes or more after its first error with no such success in between; any run that does raises one High `ops.vendor_errors` alert, once, through `ops::api::raise_kind_once`. It runs the check T106's `/healthz` runs (`app/server/src/healthz.rs`) in process and raises one High `ops.health_check_failed` alert (the kind `app/ops/src/models.rs:218` names) when two checks in a row fail. tasks.title: server: two failed in-process health checks in a row raise one High alert, a passing one clears it (D-4280)
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4280 (Opus pre-claim scout c, Nov 18, 2026; Opus review R1): split from T518 (D-3877) for size; T518 depends on this task (TD-OPS-44 spans both test files, and this task needs no T518 code), and TD-OPS-44 is listed on T518, its main owner, while this task names its health-check cases in its acceptance. OPS-004 alerts Casey when "the 5-minute health check fails twice". The new `app/server/src/health_watch.rs` registers one worker task kind in `server::worker_registry` (the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs`) that runs, every 5 minutes, the check T106's `/healthz` runs, through T106's `pub(crate)` `healthz::check(pool, now, &limits)`, called as it is (this task does not edit `healthz.rs`); `limits` is built with `HealthLimits::from_pairs` from the worker's `pairs` in `worker_registry`. The chain follows `app/server/src/no_handler_alert.rs` (`schedule` and `run_check`): every due time is a 5-minute slot start (the epoch second divided by 300), and the start-up seed from `schedule_start` and every chained run use the same dedupe key `<kind>.<slot>`, so a restart whose slot is already queued or run queues nothing and the chain never multiplies. The next run's slot is 1 plus the larger of the run's own slot (from its due time, the slot its dedupe key names) and the slot holding `now`, so an application clock slightly behind the database clock can never make the next key equal the run's own and silently end the chain; a late run after downtime and the start-up seed then merge into one chain. Each run first checks, writing nothing; then in one transaction it queues the next slot's run with this check's result in the payload (`{"health_failed": bool}`; the seed carries `false`) and raises or clears the alert. So two failures in a row need no stored row and no in-memory state. A dead-lettered run stops the chain until the next start-up seeds it again; T366's dead-letter alert reports that. Like `no_handler_alert`, it raises and clears only in test and live: in dev and `Ci` each run still checks and queues the next slot but raises nothing. Its register function takes the environment, as `no_handler_alert::register(registry, environment, clock)` does, and the tests register the task with `Environment::Test`. The second failure in a row raises one High `ops.health_check_failed` alert (`ops::api::HEALTH_ALERT`) through `ops::api::raise_kind_once`; the first passing check clears an open one through T204's kind-taking `ops::api::acknowledge_cleared` (OPS-023, D-220). The in-process check covers the database and the worker only; an unreachable web process is UptimeRobot's alone (OPS-007). Raising at the second failure (about 5 minutes) lets T204's push fire when the alert is still open 10 minutes after it was raised. Tests in the new `tests/integration/tests/health_watch.rs` (TD-OPS-44's health-check cases, its row amended by D-4280), fake data only, the failing check planted by the test: two failed checks in a row raise one alert, one raises none, one passing check clears it; a second start-up in the same slot queues no second run; a run whose `now` is 1 second before its own slot's start still queues the next slot (its own slot plus 1); and TD-OPS-08's health case: failing at 0 and 5 minutes and passing at 10 gives no push (an auto-acknowledged alert), still failing at 15 gives the push. Update the `server` `NOTES.md` (including one line that `HEALTH_ALERT`'s doc comment in `app/ops/src/alerts.rs`, "raised by T518", now means T624) and `docs/decisions.md`. Shared worker cap (D-4280): `schedule_start` in the shared `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs` already counts about 47 of clippy's 50 body lines (`too_many_lines` is denied), so whichever task adds a seed first folds the new seeds into one helper (for example `schedule_checks(&mut conn, now)`, called once from `schedule_start`) instead of appending three more lines, and keeps every existing seed, its order and its dedupe key.

tasks.title: intake: a CLOSE text, a "Close which?" answer and a cancel-intent text close jobs through answer_close
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4051 (Casey's outside code audit, item B3, Nov 16, 2026): texting CLOSE does nothing. `answer_close` (`app/intake/src/closing.rs:60`) has no production caller (its doc, `:12`, says it waits for the D-999 dispatcher), and `reply_in` (`app/intake/src/replies.rs:104`) only uses `closes()` (`:150`, which reads `close_reading(words, &[])`, so a lone number answering "Close which?" is not even seen) to skip the name-and-address and last-question steps, then hands the text to `receive_text`, which closes nothing. This task wires `answer_close` into `reply_in`: in an open request, and only when the text is not an opt-out or HELP (`answered_elsewhere`) and its 911 screen is clear (`emergency::check(words, false)` is `Clear`, as `clear` at `replies.rs:186` reads it), a CLOSE or CERRAR text with a number or ALL, a cancel-intent message, and, while a "Close which?" is asked (`close_which` answer `asked`), a lone open request number or ALL go to `answer_close` inside the reply's transaction (its `db.begin()` is then a savepoint), and its texts are the reply's. (D-4064, the Opus pre-claim check) A text that is not clear never goes to `answer_close`: `shows_intent` matches any one clause (`app/intake/src/rules.rs:682` to `:693`), so "never mind, I smell gas" reads as intent, and `receive_text` (`app/intake/src/service.rs:144`) holds the only 911 screen (INT-002); such a text goes to `receive_text` as today, so its 911 text is queued and no job is closed. Only `Closing::Closed` and `Closing::Which` end the reply; on `Closing::Explained` (a mere mention of cancelling, or a CLOSE number that is not open) the JOB-023 line is added to the reply's texts and the text still goes on to `receive_text` and the last-question step as today, so a mention inside an intake answer is still taken; anything `answer_close` answers `Nothing` goes on as today. "cancel" alone is an opt-out answered by `messaging` and never closes a job (JOB-020, D-005). tasks.title: ops: High and critical alerts with their automatic acknowledgement, and the delivery, business and request counts they read
tasks.goal: Plan change D-3805 (Casey Nov 14, 2026: split stage-5 tasks likely to need well over 80 builder turns; nothing weakened or dropped): T105 is split into T105 (the alerts, their automatic acknowledgement and the delivery, business and request counts) and T487 (safe mode and the pause checks, which runs after it). This piece: Casey is alerted on the delivery-rate, safety, dispute and coverage conditions, one delivery alert at a time with automatic acknowledgement at 97% (OPS-002, OPS-004 to OPS-006, OPS-023, OPS-025); safe mode, the owner pause switches' every-action check and the charge side are T487's (OPS-001, OPS-003, OPS-024, FEE-038). `ops` reads nothing above it: `messaging` reports delivery counts by calling `ops::api::record_delivery_counts` and `businesses` its active-business counts by `ops::api::record_business_counts`, both added here to `ops`' `api.rs` and called here from `messaging`'s delivery handler (`handlers.rs`) and `businesses`' status changes (`service.rs`); the pause-check property test (T487's) lives in the integration crate, which sees every action, in `tests/integration/tests/safe_mode.rs` (D-491, D-493); `jobs` reports each trade's requests per calendar month by calling `ops::api::record_request_counts` from `app/jobs/src/request_counts.rs`, owned here, so OPS-006 sees which trades had a request (D-493); the email-limit push itself is T204's (TD-OPS-13, D-491). This task's migration (`migrations/0192_ops_alerts_safe_mode.sql`) holds the alert acknowledgement and push facts and also safe mode's state (D-3144: safe mode's state is `ops`', this task's migration and T487's `safe_mode.rs`), which T487 reads and writes and which no later migration adds; T487 owns no migration. Plan change D-3878: that state is a single `ops` row holding `on` (boolean) and `since` (the time it last turned on, null while off), and each push fact keeps its push time, so T487 can tell when a pushed High alert has been unacknowledged for 24 hours. The alert cases are tested in the new `tests/integration/tests/ops_alert_conditions.rs`: TD-OPS-01's delivery-rate (6 failures in 50 alerts, 5 don't; 11 in 200 alerts, 10 don't; 3 in 50 at a normal rate never alert) and coverage cases (fewer than 2 active businesses in a town, or in a trade with a request that calendar month, alerts; a trade with no request that month goes to the digest only), TD-OPS-06's acknowledgement cases (97% of the last 200 acknowledges, 96% stays open, after any acknowledgement a second drop fires no new alert until 97% of 200 was reached in between, logged and listed for Casey; a ledger alert is never acknowledged by this task's delivery-recovery or elapsed-time path (TD-OPS-06's clause, D-134); OPS-023's acknowledgement of a ledger alert by the next clean nightly check (D-220) is not built here) and TD-LIC-21's OPS-006 case; TD-OPS-01's and TD-OPS-06's safe-mode and pause-switch clauses are T487's, and their release clauses T408's (TD-OPS-40). `NewAlert` gains no field (34 files build it by literal); an acknowledgement or push fact this task adds lives in its own column or table. Plan change D-3844 (the overseer's pre-claim scout, Nov 15, 2026): `app/jobs/src/request_counts.rs` is reached through a worker task registered in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` (`worker_registry`), as `tests/integration/tests/task_registry.rs` requires, not from a request path. Plan change D-3877 (Fable's pre-claim check of stage-5 wave 0, Nov 15, 2026): OPS-023's other automatic acknowledgements (D-220: a Stripe or webhook alert after 2 hours with no errors, a health-check alert once the check passes again, a ledger alert once the next nightly check finds no difference) are T204's, which owns TD-OPS-08 where they are tested; this task builds the delivery alert's acknowledgement. The first `request_counts` task is queued by one line in `schedule_start` (the shared `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs:74`, as `schedule_sweep` is at `:83`) under a dedupe key, so a restart queues nothing more. Budget: 600 lines.

tasks.goal: Plan change D-3805 (Casey Nov 14, 2026: split stage-5 tasks likely to need well over 80 builder turns; nothing weakened or dropped): T105 is split into T105 (the alerts, their automatic acknowledgement and the counts) and this task, T487, which runs after it: owner pause switches are checked by every action; and safe mode pauses only charges and releases when a pushed High alert is unacknowledged for 24 hours, each paused item going ahead after the FEE-017 check when it ends (OPS-001, OPS-003, OPS-024, FEE-038; the alerts, OPS-002, OPS-004 to OPS-006, OPS-023 and OPS-025, are T105's, and safe mode ends when every High alert is acknowledged, OPS-023, through T105's acknowledgements). The pause-check property test lives in the integration crate, which sees every action, in `tests/integration/tests/safe_mode.rs` (D-491, D-493). Plan change D-3144 (OPS-001, OPS-003, OPS-024, PICK-048, FEE-038; D-1427): the two `safe_mode_check.rs` files once planned in `payments` and `picks` are dropped (nothing would call them). Safe mode's state is `ops`' (T105's migration `migrations/0192_ops_alerts_safe_mode.sql` and this task's `safe_mode.rs`, read through a new `ops::api::safe_mode_on`; this task adds no migration, and `app/ops/src/models.rs` and `app/ops/src/alerts.rs` are T105's), and `payments::handlers::charges_paused` (`app/payments/src/handlers.rs:92`, owned here after T359; D-1427 left this check to the task that builds safe mode) checks it beside the `charging` and `all` switches, which is all the charge side needs: a "Confirm and pay" press is refused with "try again later" before any Stripe call (`before_attempt`, `app/payments/src/charge.rs:370`, `ChargeOutcome::Paused`, OPS-024), a PICK-048 auto-confirm falls back to the Confirm step (`app/payments/src/off_session.rs:218`, `FellBack`), and the card-fix and Stripe-release timers stop and resume, because `sync_pause` (`handlers.rs:584`) reads `charges_paused` (FEE-038). The release half (a release waits while safe mode is on and goes ahead after the FEE-017 check when it ends) is new T408's, which runs after this task: TD-OPS-01's and TD-OPS-06's release clauses are proven there (TD-OPS-40), and this task's `safe_mode.rs` tests the charge side and the switches (safe mode at 24:00:00 after an unacknowledged pushed High alert, not at 23:59:59; a complaint alert never starts it; in safe mode no charge happens while safety texts, STOP confirmations, HELP replies, consent texts and quote texts still go out; safe mode ends when no other High alert is open; a "Confirm and pay" press during safe mode is refused with "try again later" and reaches no Stripe call; no charge starts by itself when safe mode ends; with safe mode or the charging switch on and a pick in Payment pending, the 1-business-hour card timer and the 4-hour Stripe release stop and resume with the time left, TD-FEE-20), while T105's `ops_alert_conditions.rs` tests the alerts. The town and trade switches are read where cards go out (T251's card pool, through `ops::api::is_paused`); TD-OPS-01's "every action checks the pause switches" property covers the actions on `main` when this task runs. `NewAlert` gains no field (34 files build it by literal). Plan change D-3878 (Fable's pre-claim check of stage-5 wave 1, Nov 16, 2026): `charges_paused` takes no time (`app/payments/src/charge.rs:384` calls `charges_paused(&mut conn)`; the only caller with a clock is the pause watch, `app/server/src/lib.rs:653` to `:657`), so 24 hours cannot be measured where it is read. `charges_paused` keeps its signature. Safe mode is a stored flag in T105's table (its safe-mode state, `migrations/0192_ops_alerts_safe_mode.sql`), set and cleared by `ops::api::run_safe_mode_check(pool, now)` in `safe_mode.rs`, a worker task (`SAFE_MODE_KIND`) registered in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` `worker_registry`, first queued by one line in `schedule_start` (the shared `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs:74`) under a dedupe key and re-queued each minute; `tests/integration/tests/task_registry.rs` then passes. So that safe mode never fails open (a gap of up to a minute after 24 hours, or a stopped worker), `charges_paused` (`app/payments/src/handlers.rs:92`) answers paused when the flag is on or when a pushed High alert is still unacknowledged 24 hours or more after its push by the database's `now()`, read through `ops::api::safe_mode_on` (`payments` may call `ops`, `kit/layers.json`), so it engages at once with or without the worker; the worker's flag is what ends safe mode (only when no other High alert is open, TD-OPS-06) and what the timed 24:00:00 and 23:59:59 cases run against. Added case: a push planted 24 hours and 1 minute ago, no worker run, and a "Confirm and pay" press answers `Paused` with no Stripe call. Budget 450 lines.

tasks.title: payments: held_release, the FEE-017 re-check that clears a pick held while safe mode was on (D-4419)
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4419 (T408 attempt 2's plan gap, Nov 18, 2026; D-3144; first drafted on `claude/plan-d4422-t408-t583-size`): the payments half of T408 (safe-mode release hold), split out so its money tests land with its code. Add `payments::api::held_release(pool, stripe, account, pick, at)` (`at: Timestamp`, as `paid_release` takes it for `store_success` and the late-success refund, `release_proof.rs:224`, `:392`) to `app/payments/src/release_proof.rs` (one `pub use` line in the shared `app/payments/src/api.rs`): the only way T408's held-release task re-clears a pick it held while safe mode was on (OPS-024: a paused release goes ahead only after the FEE-017 check). A stored attempt status cannot tell a verified event's success from a press's or the reconcile's (a press, `app/payments/src/charge.rs:234`, a late answer, `:659`, and a verified event's `store_success`, `app/payments/src/release_proof.rs:401`, all write through the same `handlers::record`, `app/payments/src/handlers.rs:118`), so for a paid pick `held_release` re-fetches the pick's stored intent from Stripe and runs `check_intent` (succeeded, mode, the server's fee, `metadata.pick_id`), as `paid_release` does (`release_proof.rs:206` to `:224`), with no connection held across the fetch; for a $0 pick it keeps `no_fee_release`'s ledger check (`release_proof.rs:243`). A pick ended in `payments` (`payments.pick_intent.ended_at`, read before the fetch and again after storing the success, as D-1478 does for `paid_release`) clears nothing, has its success stored and one late-success refund queued in one transaction (FEE-021, D-2290), and answers `ReleaseError::PickEnded`. Safe mode pauses only charges and releases (OPS-001), so a refund (an early-fraud-warning refund among them) or a dispute can land while a pick is held, `payments.pick_intent.ended_at` is not set by either (`refunds.rs` and `disputes.rs` never write it), and Stripe still reports the intent succeeded: so after storing the success, `held_release` reads, under `FOR SHARE OF` the pick's `payments.pick_intent` row as `from_stored_success` does (`release_proof.rs:294` to `:296`), whether the pick has a `payments.refund` or a `payments.dispute` row, and if so clears nothing and answers `PickEnded` (FEE-026; no second refund is queued, the money is already on its way back or disputed). The ended branch never upgrades a `FOR SHARE` lock: the refund-or-dispute read takes its `FOR SHARE OF` lock only in a transaction that writes nothing, and the ended-pick refund is written in its own transaction, as `ended_late` does (`release_proof.rs:390`), so no transaction takes `FOR SHARE` and then writes the same row. Nothing else makes a `Releasable` (SEC-030): `held_release` never calls T255's `Releasable::from_stored_success`, which re-clears only a pick whose proof was already spent (D-3358), and it mints no `ReleaseProof` (only `Minter::mint` does). Its production caller is T408's `run_held_release` (T408 runs after this task; a reader landing before its caller, as D-4202's T605 did); its `///` comment names T408 and OPS-024. Tests TD-FEE-72 in the new `app/payments/src/tests/held_release.rs` (one `mod` line in the shared `app/payments/src/tests/mod.rs`), `#[sqlx::test]` on PostgreSQL with a fake Stripe client implementing the trait `paid_release` takes, fake data only, one case per branch (a failed Stripe fetch, an intent not succeeded, an intent for another pick ID, a pick with no `payments.pick_intent` and no `payments.pick_fee` row (no fee row: `NoFeeDecision`, nothing read from Stripe), a $0 pick whose fee row has no $0 decision in the ledger, the payments-ended pick and its single refund with a second call queuing no second, a paid pick refunded while held, a paid pick disputed while held, and the two clears) so the `app/payments/` 95% branch floor holds (`tests/coverage_floor.json`). tasks.title: server: a release waits while safe mode is on and goes ahead after the FEE-017 check when it ends

(ii) `messaging.purge_expired_optout_events(contact uuid, digests bytea[])` (0195, EXECUTE for `askhava_app`; `digests` are the number's blind-index digests under every index version, computed by `privacy`, so events with no inbox row (email, portal, owner and carrier opt-outs, which `optout_event` keys by digest only) are found too, as CON-022 needs; the digests come only from `privacy::api` for that contact, and the sweep is their only caller): deletes nothing unless `last_message_at` is non-null and strictly older than `now() - interval '1827 days'`, and then only that number's opt-out events themselves strictly older than that, never one a `messaging.suppression` row references and never the number's newest opt-out event (its current STOP or START evidence, kept even if a suppression row is gone). (iii) `intake.purge_expired_consent(contact uuid)` (0196, EXECUTE for `askhava_app`): the same guard through `messaging.last_message_at`, then only that number's `intake.consent_record` rows (through `intake.homeowner`'s `contact_id`) whose `consented_at` is strictly older than `now() - interval '1827 days'`. CON-022 keeps a record 5 years after the last message to that number, and `consented_at` is app-written (`migrations/0053_intake_tables.sql:57`), so row age alone could remove a 6-year-old consent of a number texted yesterday; the last-message guard is read by the database, never passed by the caller. Every function reads `now()` itself (never a time the caller passes) and returns the deleted IDs for the audit rows. The sweep calls both purge functions for a number before it deletes that number's message-log rows, in the same transaction (the guard reads those rows). The schema rule: `tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs` fails a migration naming another module's schema (`schema_refs`, `:272`, `:799`), and an `intake` marker the message path kept could not see every outbound text (`messaging` cannot call `intake`, `kit/layers.json`) and could be missed by omission, so this task (now a harness task, since that test is T226's, T250's and T252's) adds one logged exception there, as `DYNAMIC_SQL_ALLOWED` does (`:63`): a `CROSS_SCHEMA_CALLS` list with exactly one entry, `migrations/0196_intake_consent_purge.sql` may name `messaging.last_message_at(` and nothing else of `messaging`, with its reason (CON-022, D-3753; `intake` may call `messaging`, `kit/layers.json`); any other `messaging.` name in that file, the same call in any other file, and an entry whose file or call is missing each still fail, with planted cases for all three; every existing case and finding stays as it is. What the guards rest on: `last_message_at` and the suppression check read rows the app role may DELETE (`messaging.outbox`, `messaging.inbox`, `messaging.inbox_contact` and `messaging.suppression`, `schema_grants.rs:141` to `:151`, and `inbox_contact`'s explicit grant), and `received_at` and `consented_at` are app-written, so a compromised app that deleted a number's recent message rows could make it look expired; the damage stays bounded by the row-age floor, since no function removes a row that is itself less than 1,827 days old, and the newest opt-out event always stays. The message-log tables already grant DELETE (`schema_grants.rs:141` to `:151`); `messaging.inbox_contact` gets an explicit DELETE grant in its migration. (2) The opt-out is never weakened: a number on `messaging.suppression` keeps its suppression row, the `messaging.optout_event` row that row points to (`event_id`, `migrations/0044_messaging_optout.sql:33`; digest-only, no phone) and its locked phone in the vault, because the suppression digest is keyed `homeowner-phone|v<n>` and PRIV-024's key rotation rebuilds it from the vault plaintext (D-079), so clearing the phone would lose the opt-out at the next rotation; only its other CON-022 rows (consent records, keyword events, message logs) go at 5 years. A number not on suppression loses its CON-022 rows and then its locked vault phone, cleared through `privacy::api` (`app/privacy/src/consent_phone.rs`). The opt-out events a suppression row references are kept by the `messaging` function's own condition, and the app role has no DELETE on the table at all. That an opted-out number's phone stays locked past 5 years is listed for Casey, with whether the privacy policy should say so (D-2208). (3) Tests in `tests/integration/tests/consent_purge.rs` (TD-CON-30): a number last messaged 1,826 days ago keeps everything; at 1,827 days a number not on suppression loses its rows and its vault phone, with audit rows of IDs only; an opted-out number keeps its suppression row, the opt-out event it points to and its locked phone, loses its other rows, and is still refused a text after the purge and after an index-key rotation; the function leaves a referenced opt-out event and the newest one in place; a message in between restarts its clock; and (D-3753) each purge function, with the database clock and strict comparisons, leaves a row and a last message seeded 1,826 days ago and removes a row whose last message and own time are 1,827 days and one minute ago (the minute keeps the test off the boundary); a 6-year-old consent record of a number last messaged yesterday is kept; a temporary table named `suppression` or `outbox` in the session changes nothing; the app role cannot call `messaging.last_message_at`; and a direct DELETE of either append-only table by the app role is still refused. Seeded rows are timed that far in the past, since the functions read the database clock. The rotation case builds its two-version `VAULT_INDEX_KEY` the way `tests/integration/tests/vault.rs` does (its `key(version, byte)` helper at line 32 and the v1-plus-v2 key set of `the_rotation_drill_moves_every_row_to_v2`, TD-PRIV-09) and rotates with `privacy::api::rotate_batch` as that test and `tests/integration/tests/inbound_scrub_context.rs` do; it is not skipped. Update the `messaging`, `intake` and `privacy` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`, and add this task's build-note line at the end of `app/messaging/NOTES.md` (the template's rule; D-3620, D-3079, D-3468). (b) STOP, HELP and START: there is no keyword-event table; STOP and START (every channel) are `messaging.optout_event` rows, and a HELP is its inbox row and the HELP reply's outbox row, so it goes with the message logs; no table is added for them. tasks.title: privacy and messaging: no blind-index key version is retired while an opt-out is held under it
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4418 (found by the Opus review of T563's plan fix, verified on `main` 954dd68): D-2208 and T321's goal rest on PRIV-024's rotation rebuilding the `messaging.suppression` digests from the vault plaintext (`docs/decisions.md` D-079, D-2208), but nothing does: `rotate_batch` (`app/privacy/src/vault.rs:767`) re-seals contacts and, through `index_phone` (`:483` to `:505`), replaces a contact's homeowner-phone digest with one under the active version only, and no code re-keys a suppression row. `record` lists a number under every version configured at that moment, so a number that opted out while only v1 existed has v1 rows only; once v1 is dropped from `VAULT_INDEX_KEY`, `send_checked` no longer matches it and the number would be texted again (CON-013, CON-035). The consent sweep (T563, through T701's `listing_key`) needs every contact's digest under every configured version, so it can match a listing under any of them without reading the phone. Until re-keying suppression is designed (open in D-4418; the price is that a leaked index key version cannot be retired meanwhile and every phone contact keeps a digest under it, `docs/threat-model.md:18`), PRIV-024 now says no index key version may be retired while a suppression row is held under it, and this task makes that a machine rule. (1) `Vault::index_versions(&self) -> Vec<u16>` in `app/privacy/src/vault.rs`: the configured `VAULT_INDEX_KEY` versions, ascending, read from the vault's own key map (no hashing of a dummy value), with its `///` doc and a unit test; re-exported needs nothing (it is a method of the exported `Vault`). (1b) The contact's homeowner-phone digest is kept under every configured `VAULT_INDEX_KEY` version (`privacy.contact_index`'s key is `(purpose, key_version, digest)`, `migrations/0036_privacy_vault.sql:36` to `:42`, so versions coexist; `find_by_phone` already matches any version): `index_phone` writes one row per configured version (the `blind_index` set) and deletes that contact's homeowner-phone rows under any other version; `rotate_batch` selects, besides contacts sealed under an older `VAULT_KEY`, every contact with a phone that lacks a homeowner-phone digest under a configured version or holds one under a version no longer configured, and re-seals it as today (its plaintext read audited as rotation, PRIV-003), so a batch run until it returns 0 leaves every phone contact with exactly one digest per configured version; `sender-dir` and `email` digests are unchanged. TD-PRIV-09's drill test in `tests/integration/tests/vault.rs` (T022's, taken over here, which makes this a harness task) asserts zero v1 digests after the rotation while v1 and v2 are both configured; that assertion changes, by this decision, to: with v1 and v2 configured each phone contact holds exactly one digest under each, and after a `rotate_batch` with only v2 configured none holds a v1 digest and every number is still found; the batch counts and every other assertion stay. The tests counting a contact's homeowner-phone rows (`retention_purge.rs`, `under_13_purge.rs`, `inbound_first_contact.rs`, `retention_purge_races.rs`) build one-version vaults and are unchanged. (2) New `app/messaging/src/suppression_versions.rs`: `pub async fn check_suppression_versions(conn, vault) -> Result<(), SuppressionVersionsError>` reads `SELECT DISTINCT index_version FROM messaging.suppression` (messaging's own table, static SQL) and fails with the held versions missing from `vault.index_versions()` (version numbers only, never a digest); re-exported through the shared `app/messaging/src/api.rs`. (3) The server and the worker each run it once, after building their `Vault` and connecting, before they serve a request or run a task (the server in `app/server/src/main.rs` after `vault_from_settings` at `:98`; the worker in `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs` at start, building its vault from the same two settings when both are set, as `app/server/src/lib.rs`'s `vault_from` (`:576`) does; `main.rs`, `lib.rs` and `bin/worker.rs` are shared paths), and refuse to start on a failure with a log line naming only the missing versions and D-4418; a start check that cannot read the table (the database unreachable) also refuses to start; a refused start fails closed (nothing is texted), and the host's health check keeps the previous release serving (verify with host: Railway's healthcheck gates a deploy and a failed one leaves the old deployment serving, `docs/brains/deploy-operations.md` O17 and its failure table); a process with no vault configured skips it. (4) Tests (TD-PRIV-31) in the new `tests/integration/tests/suppression_key_versions.rs`, fake numbers only, against PostgreSQL, keys built with `tests/integration/tests/vault.rs`'s `key(version, byte)` helper: an empty list passes with any key set; with v1 and v2 configured, a contact stored before v2 holds a v1 and a v2 digest after `rotate_batch`, one stored after holds both at once, and a phone change replaces both; a contact whose only digest is under a version no longer configured is picked by the next `rotate_batch` and left with exactly the configured ones; a number listed with only v1 configured passes with v1 and with v1 plus v2, and fails naming version 1 with only v2; a listing made with v1 and v2 configured passes with v1 plus v2 and fails with only v2 (its v1 row is held); `index_versions()` returns `[1, 2]` for a v1-plus-v2 key; the refusal text holds no digest. Update `app/messaging/CLAUDE.md` and `app/privacy/CLAUDE.md` with the rule. Plan change D-4473: for T645's web-chat opt-out (which has no vault and may read no phone), this task also adds `pub async fn phone_digests(conn, contact: Uuid) -> Result<Vec<(u16, [u8; 32])>, VaultError>` in `vault.rs`, re-exported through the shared `app/privacy/src/api.rs`: the contact's homeowner-phone digests as `privacy.contact_index` holds them, one per key version, in descending version order (so the first is the active one once rotated, as `blind_index` puts the active first), empty for a contact with no phone; static SQL, no plaintext read, no audit row, no row lock, and it runs inside a transaction (no `ensure_bare`): these are HMAC blind indexes, not contact values, so no vault-read grant applies (PRIV-002, as `find_by_phone` reads the same table). With (1b), a contact stored or rotated under the configured versions holds exactly the set `record` computes from the plaintext. T563 may read its digests through it instead of its own read in `consent_phone.rs` (D-4280 is unchanged either way). Its test, in `tests/integration/tests/suppression_key_versions.rs`: with v1 and v2 configured a stored contact's `phone_digests` equal, as a set, `blind_index` of its fake number, the highest version first; a contact with no phone gives an empty list; it works inside an open transaction. Plan change D-4473, review round 2: so that `phone_digests` (and T563's listing key) never carry a digest under a version that is no longer configured, the start step gains, in `vault.rs` and before `check_suppression_versions`, `pub async fn settle_index_versions(conn, vault) -> Result<(), IndexVersionsError>`, re-exported through the shared `app/privacy/src/api.rs` and run once by the server and the worker after building their `Vault` (same place, same refusal handling as (3); a process with no vault skips it): (a) prune: in one static-SQL statement, delete the homeowner-phone `privacy.contact_index` rows under a version not in `vault.index_versions()` for contacts that already hold a homeowner-phone digest under a configured version (no plaintext read; nothing else is deleted); (b) refuse: when any contact holds homeowner-phone rows and none under a configured version (a version dropped before `rotate_batch` finished under both, against PRIV-024's order: add the new version, rotate until 0, then drop the old), fail and refuse to start with a log line naming the configured versions and the count of such contacts only, never a contact ID or digest. Fail closed: nothing is texted. Rolling deploys: an old process still running with the old key set can write a row under the dropped version after a new process started; the next start prunes it under (a), or, if it is a `messaging.suppression` row, `check_suppression_versions` refuses the start (fails closed). TD-PRIV-31 gains both cases.

tasks.title: messaging: a per-number opt-out lock, and the listing key and re-check the consent sweep needs before it clears a phone
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4418 (the attempt-1 plan gap of BLOCKED T563, verified on `main` c509877b): the daily consent sweep (T563) decides whether to clear a number's vault phone by a suppression check made before its per-number transaction, and `record` (`app/messaging/src/optout.rs:332` to `:349`, the one writer of `messaging.suppression` rows: `suppress` at `:321` for the help-email, email-reply, form, portal and owner paths, the texted STOP in `on_inbound_text` at `:162`, the carrier 21610 in `send_checked` at `:397`) takes no lock, so an opt-out that commits between that check and the clear leaves a listed number with no vault phone, which D-079 keeps so the opt-out stays honored (CON-022, CON-035). This task, run before T563, gives `messaging` a per-number opt-out lock and the two calls the sweep needs, all in `app/messaging/src/optout.rs`, the public ones re-exported through the shared `app/messaging/src/api.rs`. (1) A private helper (for example `lock_number(tx, digests)`) takes, for each distinct digest of the number (its homeowner-phone blind-index digests under every configured `VAULT_INDEX_KEY` version, the set `digests` at `:441` returns), `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(encode($1::bytea, 'hex'), 4418))`: the new seed 4418, used by no other advisory lock (seeds 0, 21, 43, 55, 76, 151, 274, 391 and 481 are taken in `app/`; `grep -rn pg_advisory app/` before you start and pick no taken one), one statement per digest in ascending byte order of the digest, so two transactions locking one number take its keys in the same order. The lock is transaction-scoped, so every caller runs inside a transaction. (2) `record` takes that lock as its first statement, before the opt-out event insert. Its three callers already call it inside a transaction (`suppress`'s own, `on_inbound_text`'s and `send_checked`'s 21610 transaction), and nothing else about them changes: `suppress`'s newly-listed answer, the event, the confirmation, the alert and the block stay as they are. START (`lift_suppression`) takes no lock: it only takes a number off the list, and a sweep that still sees the number listed keeps its phone. (3) `pub fn listing_key(vault, indexed: &[(u16, [u8; 32])]) -> Option<ListingKey>`, pure, no database and no vault plaintext read (D-4280 stands: the sweep never reads a phone): `indexed` is the contact's homeowner-phone digests as `privacy.contact_index` holds them, one per key version (T563 reads them through `privacy::api`, D-4280; T702 keeps a contact's digest under every configured version). It answers `Some` only when `indexed` holds a digest under every version `Vault::index_versions()` (T702's) lists; the key is then exactly those digests, one per configured version, which is the set `record` and `send_checked` compute from the plaintext. Otherwise (a configured version's digest missing, a rotation not yet run for that contact) it answers `None` and the sweep keeps the phone that run. Why not one digest: nothing re-keys `messaging.suppression`, so a number listed while only v1 existed has v1 rows only; its contact's v1 digest still matches them while v1 is configured, and T702 refuses to start once v1 is dropped while such a row is held. Reading the plaintext instead would reverse D-4280 and add a daily burst of audited reads against SEC-047's hourly baseline (`docs/spec/security.md:51`). `ListingKey` holds only the digests, with no public field or constructor and a `Debug` that prints no digest. (4) `pub async fn still_unlisted(tx, key: &ListingKey) -> Result<bool, OutboxError>` takes the lock of (1) for the key's digests, then, in a separate later statement (so under READ COMMITTED its snapshot is taken after the lock is granted and sees every opt-out committed before it), reads, in one statement, whether the number has a suppression row under any of the key's digests and whether any `messaging.suppression` row at all is under a version outside the key's versions (T702's start check makes that impossible; it stays as a defense), and answers `true` only when neither holds. The lock is held to the caller's commit. Its `///` doc says: call it inside a READ COMMITTED transaction, as that transaction's first statement, holding no other lock, and make no outside call in that transaction. What the lock does not close (D-4418, accepted): an opt-out whose caller resolved the number before the sweep's transaction (the portal's phone on file, a voice press-9, an inbound text matched to its contact) and whose `record` waits on the sweep's lock commits after the sweep cleared the phone; the number is then listed by digest under every configured version, as any listing is, and is still refused every text, but has no vault phone behind it. (5) Tests (TD-CON-37) in the new `tests/integration/tests/optout_number_lock.rs`, fake numbers only, against PostgreSQL: while a test transaction holds `still_unlisted`'s lock for a number, `suppress` of that number (portal channel) and a texted STOP through `on_inbound_text`, each on its own connection in a spawned task, are each seen waiting (a bounded poll of `pg_locks` for an ungranted `advisory` lock of that backend's pid, failing rather than hanging) and finish only after the test transaction commits, the number then listed; with `suppress` called inside an open outer transaction on one connection (its own `begin` is then a savepoint, so `record`'s lock is held to the outer commit), `still_unlisted` on another connection is seen waiting in `pg_locks` and, after the outer commit, answers `false` (this fails if the read is made before the lock is granted, in the same statement, or under REPEATABLE READ); a `suppress` committed before `still_unlisted` makes it answer `false`; a number never listed answers `true`; with one index version configured, `listing_key` of the contact's indexed digest is `Some` and writes no vault-read audit row; with v1 and v2 configured (the two-version `VAULT_INDEX_KEY` built with `tests/integration/tests/vault.rs`'s `key(version, byte)` helper, TD-PRIV-09) and the contact's digests under both after `rotate_batch`, it is `Some` with both, and `None` when the contact has only its v1 digest; a number listed while only v1 existed, its contact then rotated so it holds v1 and v2 digests, both configured, makes `still_unlisted` answer `false`, and an unlisted number's key answers `true`; with only v2 configured while a v1 suppression row is held (a state T702 refuses at start, built directly in the test), `still_unlisted` answers `false` for any number; the lock on one number does not hold up `suppress` of another. Every existing T029, T093, T321, T356 and T357 test passes unchanged. Privacy and consent work: an Opus worker, an Opus privacy, compliance and security review, and two review rounds.

tasks.title: calls and server: a random stored PIN per line, unique on its number, durable PIN-try counts, and the inbound voice route
tasks.goal: A line's PIN is its ID modulo 10,000 (`calls::api::job_pin`, D-1684), and line IDs are not secret; the 6-a-day count is the caller's input with no storage (D-1685); and no inbound-voice route serves the TwiML (D-1708). D-1684 and D-1685 named T078 or T080, both DONE without it (external audit A09, D-1755). (1) `migrations/0151_calls_pins_attempts.sql`: a `pin` column on `calls.number_pool` (four digits, drawn from the OS random source, unique among open lines of one pool number by a partial unique index) and `calls.pin_try` (a digest of the calling number, never the number: HMAC-SHA-256 under the ID secret with the domain label `pin-try|v1` over the normalized E.164 number, derived with `core`'s ID-secret derivation as `IdempotencyKey::derive` is, listed under `ID_SECRET` in the PRIV-024 key inventory and re-derived when that secret rotates; pool number; Arizona day; count; queries in `app/calls/src/models.rs`), app role SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE of the count only. (2) `app/calls/src/pins.rs`: allocation in `assign_number`'s transaction (`app/calls/src/service.rs`) retries a collision a bounded number of times, then raises the existing pool alert and refuses the line; `job_pin` and every read of the PIN come from the stored column (`routing.rs`), never the line ID; the try count is one atomic `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING` per wrong try, so concurrent wrong tries cannot pass 6 a day, and a repeated Twilio callback (same CallSid and digits) is not another try (recorded per CallSid). (3) `app/server/src/inbound_voice.rs`: the signature-checked Twilio voice webhook (SEC-016) for the pool numbers, recorded by CallSid (SEC-017), finding the party, lines, stored counts and STIR/SHAKEN attestation and serving `calls::api` TwiML (prompt, PIN, read-back on A attestation only, dial), merged in the shared `lib.rs`; the same migration creates `calls.call_start` (the parent CallSid unique, the line, the start time, the dialed leg's SID filled later by T271; app role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of the dialed SID only), and the webhook stores the call's start there, once per parent CallSid, at the moment it answers with the dial, so FEE-022 judges each call by when it started (D-1836). (1) `migrations/0154_quotes_job_text.sql`: `quotes.job_description`, one row per inbound text whose scrubbed words describe a job (request ID, job ID, a message ID typed `uuid`, the words, the recorded time; unique on message ID and job ID together, since a SPLIT opens a second job from the same text, `app/intake/src/routing.rs:423` to `:443`; the message ID is the `messaging.inbox` row ID for a text and the chat message's own ID for web chat, which has no inbox row, `migrations/0053_intake_tables.sql:54` to `:59`; no foreign key to `messaging.inbox`, so a later inbox purge is never blocked), and `quotes.shown_card`, one row per card shown or released for a job (request ID, job ID and the 32-hex card digest, unique together and checked by pattern; the card text, town, place code and photo IDs exactly as `build_card` made them; the category code and the remaining candidate job type codes; an `emergency` mark, true only for a card stored on the INT-029 emergency path; the recorded time; `sent_at`, null until the card sender marks it); no name, phone, email, street address or contact column; app role SELECT, INSERT and DELETE on both, and UPDATE of `shown_card.sent_at` only. (2) `app/quotes/src/job_text.rs`, through the shared `quotes::api`: `keep_description(conn, (request, job), message, &ScrubbedText, at)` takes only the scrubber's `ScrubbedText` (`app/privacy/src/scrub.rs:320`, made only by `privacy::api`), so raw words cannot be stored (T277's rule, D-3118), and a repeat for the same message and job stores nothing; `description(conn, job)` gives the job's stored words in time order, or `None`; `keep_card(conn, (request, job), digest, &JobCard, (category, candidates, emergency), at)` stores a card only when `digest` is its text's card digest, which `quotes` computes itself with the workspace `sha2` (added to the shared `app/quotes/Cargo.toml`; `quotes` may not call `intake`, `kit/layers.json`): the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of `JobCard::text`, the value `intake::api::card_digest` gives and approval stores, the test asserting the two agree, refuses any other digest without writing, and stores nothing on a repeat; `stored_card(conn, job, digest)` gives that card (rebuilt through a new crate-private constructor in `app/quotes/src/cards.rs`; `build_card` stays the only public way to make one; `JobCard`'s derived `Debug` (`cards.rs:108`) becomes a hand-written one that hides the text, as `CardParts`' does, `:89` to `:102`), its category and candidates, only while the stored text's digest still equals `digest` (checked on every read, so the card sent is the card approved, CARD-007); `unsent_cards(conn, request)` gives, for each job of the request with no card sent, its newest stored card with its `emergency` mark, oldest job first (the emergency path, which has no approval step and sends only marked cards, T251); `mark_card_sent(conn, job, digest, at)` sets `sent_at` once; `sent_card(conn, job)` gives the card that went out, for the business job page and the quote form (CARD-023). tasks.title: payments and picks: the fee fixed at the pick is stored by payments, a press must match it, and a fee-mode switch after the pick is refused before any charge
tasks.goal: No code stores the fee fixed at the pick: `picks`' `new_pick` (`app/picks/src/service.rs:340`) says "No fee ... here", `payments`' `fee_at_pick` (`app/payments/src/rules.rs:496`) is a pure function nothing outside tests calls, and `open_intent` and `confirm_and_pay` (`app/payments/src/charge.rs:91`, `:146`) charge whatever `Press::amount_cents` the caller passes (`app/payments/src/models.rs:325`), checking only that it is not 0 (third external audit, D-1871). And the fee-mode check runs only after Stripe has charged: `record_fee_at_confirm` (`app/payments/src/service.rs:344`) refuses with `ConfirmError::Mismatch` when the mode changed, so a switch between the pick and Confirm leaves money moved with no ledger entry until the reconcile; and nothing stores the fee terms in force: `switch_fee_mode` (`app/payments/src/service.rs:207`) only returns them and every caller passes its own `FeeTerms`. (1) `migrations/0155_payments_fee_terms_pick_fee.sql`: `payments.fee_terms`, one row (mode and authorization version), seeded with `tiers` and `AUTHORIZATION_VERSION`, the app role SELECT and UPDATE only; and `payments.pick_fee` (`pick_id` primary key, `business_id`, `job_id`, `mode` `tiers` or `flat`, `kind` `charged` or `fee_free`, `amount_cents` at or above 0 and above 0 only for `charged`, `terms_version`, `fixed_at`), the app role SELECT and INSERT only. `switch_fee_mode` writes the new terms to `payments.fee_terms` in its own transaction with its audit row (T108's owner switch calls it and stores nothing else), and `payments::api::fee_terms_in_force(conn)` reads them; `picks` and T261 read the terms only through it. (2) `app/payments/src/pick_fee.rs`: `payments::api::fix_fee_at_pick(tx, pick, business, job, &PickedFee, at)` writes it once (a repeat with the same values is a no-op, different values an error) and `pick_fee(conn, pick)` reads it. (3) `new_pick` computes the fee with `fee_at_pick` from the chosen quote (its amounts and period), the job's category and job type facts and `fee_terms_in_force`, through the modules' `api`s (FEE-005's inputs only, D-1415), and calls `fix_fee_at_pick` in the pick's own transaction; a pick whose fee can't be fixed is not stored. (4) `open_intent` and `confirm_and_pay` read `pick_fee` before anything else: no row, a different business or job, a $0 fee, or `amount_cents` other than the stored one is the new `ChargeError::FeeMismatch`, and Stripe is not called; an existing `pick_intent` whose amount differs from the stored fee is the same refusal. (5) The mode check moves before the charge: `may_confirm` takes the pick, reads `fee_terms_in_force` itself and refuses with the new `ConfirmError::FeeModeChanged` when the stored `mode` differs from them, before any PaymentIntent is opened or confirmed; `record_fee_at_confirm` takes the pick and writes the stored fee, comparing the gate's `Authorized` (whose mode matched the pick's at the gate) with the stored mode, so a switch that commits after the gate changes nothing for this pick and the post-charge write can no longer fail for a mode switch. D-072 still applies to every pick made after a switch. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/fee_fixed_at_pick.rs`. This is a harness task because it changes tests of DONE tasks (T060's `fee_mode_switch.rs` and `fee_at_pick.rs`, T062's `charge_attempts.rs`, T189's `confirm_and_pay.rs`) and T263's `fee_limit_race.rs`: each fixture only gains the stored fee terms and the stored pick fee its presses now need (and `may_confirm` the pick), and no expected value changes. Update the `payments` and `picks` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md` (`docs/architecture.md` section 3 already lists the new table, D-1871).

tasks.title: architecture test: dynamic SQL in a migration is a TD-SEC-10 finding unless allow-listed with a reason
tasks.goal: Dynamic SQL hides schema references from TD-SEC-10 (D-1677): `schema_refs` in `tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs` lexes dollar-quoted bodies as SQL but cannot see a schema name built while a migration runs, so a migration such as `DO $x$ BEGIN EXECUTE format('ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA %I REVOKE ...', nsp); END $x$;` names no schema literally and passes (seen in T250's third attempt, PR #293, not merged). In that test (T226's, then T250's, taken over here after T250 merges) add a dynamic-SQL rule over each migration's lexed tokens (the tokens `schema_refs` reads, so comments and `'...'` strings never count). A file gives one finding, `migrations/<file>: dynamic SQL (`<construct>`) hides schema references from this check`, naming the first construct found, when it holds: a `DO` statement (the token `do` first in a statement, at the start of the file or after `;`, so `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and a rule's `DO INSTEAD` never count); an `execute` token not followed by `function`, `procedure`, `on` or `,` (the PL/pgSQL dynamic statement, including inside a `CREATE FUNCTION` or `CREATE PROCEDURE` body, `RETURN QUERY EXECUTE` and a cursor's `FOR EXECUTE`; a trigger's `EXECUTE FUNCTION` and `GRANT`/`REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION` are not dynamic); or a call of `format`, `quote_ident`, `quote_literal` or `quote_nullable` (the name followed by `(`). The SQL of each query macro and `query_file*` file under `app/` gets the same finding for `DO` and `execute` (a `format(` there only formats a value). A file is exempt only when its path is in a new constant `DYNAMIC_SQL_ALLOWED: [(&str, &str); N]` (path, one-line reason); it starts with one entry, `migrations/0019_core_db_migrations.sql`, whose `DO $guard$` block only raises an error when the role `askhava_app` is missing and builds no SQL (T012). An entry whose file is missing or no longer holds dynamic SQL is itself one finding, so the list cannot go stale. The checks take the allow list as a parameter: `td_sec_10_migrations_and_sql_obey_the_rules` passes the constant and each plant passes its own, so a planted path never enters the real list. Planted cases giving exactly one finding each: a `DO` block, an `EXECUTE` in a `CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE plpgsql` body, a `format()`-built statement, a query macro holding `EXECUTE`, and a stale allow-list entry; planted cases giving none: an allow-listed file holding a `DO` block, an `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, a `CREATE TRIGGER ... EXECUTE FUNCTION` and a `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION`. Every earlier case, T250's included, still gives exactly its one finding: each T250 case whose plant holds a `DO` block (those proving a `DO` block voids the REVOKE exception, such as a REVOKE beside a `DO` block and a REVOKE inside one) runs with its planted file on its own allow list, so it still proves only its own rule. If another migration on `main` holds dynamic SQL when this task starts, list it only when it builds no schema name at run time, with its reason; otherwise stop and report. Update the test's `//!` header to name the rule, and the `migrations/` entry of `docs/architecture.md` section 2 (T226's paragraph on this test) to name it too (section 4 rule 3 already states it, D-1677).

tasks.goal: Decisions hand work to later tasks that are already DONE or do not own the files (D-1684, D-1685, D-1688, D-1712, D-1715 and others), and no check notices (external audit A12, D-1760). `docs/integration-closure.md` is the one register of cross-module handoffs. Add to `scripts/stage_exit.py` a fifth condition: read the register's table; a row whose area is `security`, `money` or `privacy` and whose status is not `closed` is judged at stage N only when every owner it names has a `stage` at or below N in `kit/tasks.json` (a row with a later-stage owner is printed and not failed at N, because the runner re-runs `stage_exit.evaluate()` for every earlier stage on every claim, `runner/state.py:403`, and an earlier stage must not close again behind it); a judged row fails when it names only tasks DONE or SKIPPED in the state; a row with no owner at all, or naming a task id missing from `kit/tasks.json`, fails at every stage; a `closed` row must carry evidence (a merged commit SHA or PR number and a test name) or it fails too; rows of other areas are printed, never failing. The start is recorded where the app must already be reached: T262's inbound voice webhook stores it in `calls.call_start` (T262's migration 0151) keyed by the parent CallSid when it answers, and T271's route records the dialed leg's `initiated` callback against that row by `ParentCallSid`. In `app/calls/src/handlers.rs`: `dial_twiml` asks for the dialed leg's `initiated` and final status callbacks at T271's route; `call_start_confirmed(db, parent, dialed, at)` records the dialed leg's SID on the parent's row, or creates the row at `at` when the webhook's write was lost (a repeat or late callback never moves a start); `call_log` joins each logged call to its start by the dialed SID and returns `LoggedCall::started_at: Option<Timestamp>`. `call_record` uses `started_at`; a call whose start was still not recorded uses its end time for every FEE-022 check and counts as a qualifying attempt, because a lost callback is Ask Hava's fault and the business must not lose its refund for it (D-1836; `payments`' rules are not changed). This is a harness task because it takes over T191's `tests/integration/tests/unreachable_refund.rs`: its `call` helper sets `started_at` to the time it already passes, and no expected value changes. New cases in `tests/integration/tests/call_start.rs`. Update the `calls` and `picks` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.
