tasks.title: picks and payments: the unreachable refund and the fraud warning close only on a succeeded refund, and a free pick ends as a no-show too
tasks.goal: Two defects in T191's `app/picks/src/unreachable_refund.rs` (merged in #323), found by the second external audit (B07, B08, D-1836); B06's start time is T282's. (1) Refund outcome (B07): `refund_waiting` treats `RefundOutcome::Unchanged` like `Refunded`, but `Unchanged` also means a try still in flight (`RefundStatus::next` answers `Nothing` for a `sending` or `failed` row with no matching retry, `app/payments/src/status.rs`, and `refunds::finish` turns that into `Unchanged`), so a second run while the first Stripe request is open closes the job and emails "your fee is refunded" before Stripe has answered (D-1819 (1)). New `app/payments/src/refund_state.rs`, exported through `payments`' shared `api.rs`: `refund_state(conn, pick) -> RefundState::{NoRefund, InFlight, Succeeded, Failed, Blocked}`, read from the authoritative `payments.refund` rows as T258 leaves them (`sending` and `pending` are in flight; only Stripe's `succeeded` is `Succeeded`; `failed` and `canceled` are `Failed`; a disputed charge is `Blocked`). `decide_at_96_hours` and `fraud_warning` close the job, move it, end the pick or queue the success email only when that read answers `Succeeded`, whatever `request_refund` or `early_fraud_warning` returned; `InFlight` gives `AtNinetySix::RefundWaiting` with a new in-flight marker (and `fraud_warning` `false`), so the caller (T281) runs the step again and the close and email still happen once (the per-pick dedupe stays). `RefundOutcome` and the refund state machine are T258's and are not changed here. (2) Fee-free no-show (B08): `end_pick` updates only a `paid` pick and drops the row count, so `no_call_at_72_hours` returns a fee-free introduction's job to Quotes ready and closes its line while the pick stays `free` (`aftermath.rs` counts `paid` and `free` as connected). The no-show ends a `paid` or `free` pick as `no_show` with its ended time in the same transaction as the job move and the line close; when no pick matches either status, the whole transaction rolls back and the function returns an explicit result, never a silent success. `fraud_warning` still ends only a `paid` pick (FEE-052 never applies to a fee-free pick). New cases in `tests/integration/tests/unreachable_refund_states.rs`; T191's test file stays as T282 leaves it. Money code: the `app/payments/` 95% floor holds and every branch of `refund_state` is covered. Update `docs/architecture.md` section 7 (as built), the `picks` and `payments` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: portals: the sign-in link cap and the code-try cap are atomic admissions, so concurrent requests cannot pass them
tasks.goal: D-1725 allows at most 5 sign-in links per member in 15 minutes and D-1777 at most 5 failed code checks per link, but both are check-then-act: `send_one` counts links (`models::links_since`, `app/portals/src/models.rs`) and then inserts and sends, and `check_once` counts `auth_failed` events, calls Verify and records the failure afterwards (`app/portals/src/business_auth.rs:444`, `:652`), so simultaneous requests that all see 4 all go through (second external audit B01, D-1837). (1) Links: the count and the insert of the new `portals.login_link` row happen in one short transaction under a per-member transaction-scoped lock (`pg_advisory_xact_lock` on the member's ID under a `portals` key namespace), committed before the email is sent; no transaction is held across the mail call. (2) Code tries: `migrations/0167_portals_code_tries.sql` adds `portals.code_try` (link ID, try number 1 to 5 unique per link, reserved time, outcome `pending`, `right`, `wrong` or `abandoned`; app role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of the outcome only); a check first reserves the next try number in its own short transaction (the unique key and the check constraint refuse a sixth), then calls Verify with no transaction open, then records the outcome; a reservation left `pending` (a crash or a Verify timeout) counts as a used try, so a restart never gives a try back; the fifth used try uses the link up and shows the "stopped working" screen as today; a right code consumes the link once (the existing guarded `UPDATE`), and a concurrent right code and wrong code never both sign in. Each wrong or failed check still writes its `auth_failed` security event (SEC-048). T089's per-IP and per-business limits sit in front of these and never re-count links or tries (D-1837). Tests in `tests/security/tests/signin_admission.rs` with 20 simultaneous requests over several pooled connections. Update the `portals` `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` section 10 and `docs/decisions.md`. Pentest PT-04 and PT-03's business half (D-2349): `send_once` (`app/portals/src/business_auth.rs:630`) holds a transaction across `codes.verify.send`, and `check_once` (:664) never requires that a code was sent for its link. This sets aside only D-1776's held transaction. (3) The same migration adds `portals.code_send` (link ID primary key, reserved at, outcome `pending`, `sent` or `failed`); a press reserves the link's one send in a short committed transaction (a new row, or a `failed` one, or a `pending` one older than the adapter's 15-second timeout plus a minute, which a crash left), calls Verify with no transaction open, then records `sent` or `failed`, so a failed send can be pressed again and two presses at once send once; it replaces the `code-sent:<link>` marker row. (4) `check_once` refuses a link whose send is not `sent` before any try is reserved or Verify is called. Tests in `signin_admission.rs` (TD-SEC-38): a failed send can be retried; 20 simultaneous presses send once; a check with no sent code reaches Verify zero times; with a fake Verify that hangs, no transaction is open during the wait. (5) No pooled connection is held across a Verify call either (PT-04's availability side, D-2349): `device_step`, `send_once` and `check_once` take the handler's `&PgPool` (`state.pool`, already in this file) in place of `&mut PgConnection` and acquire a connection only for each short database step, releasing it before the send or the check; with a fake Verify that hangs, 30 concurrent presses and checks leave a pool of 5 connections able to serve another request (the matrix's AVAIL-01, TD-SEC-38). Nov 10 code review batch 2, portals F4 (D-2635; D-1725): `links_since` (`app/portals/src/models.rs:62`) counts every `portals.login_link` row of the last 15 minutes, including the row `remember_device` (`business_auth.rs`) inserts on a new-device sign-in with `created_at` now, so a member who signs in on a new device loses one of the 5 links; the count (which this task rewrites) leaves out remembered-device rows. TD-SEC-38 gains the case: a new-device sign-in, then 5 link requests, all 5 send.

tasks.title: intake and privacy: the 180-day contact purge decides and clears under one lock order shared with new requests and holds
tasks.goal: The contact purge reads whether another request is live and whether any job is held (`free_contact`, `app/intake/src/purge.rs:93`), returns the contact, and only then `purge_contact` (`app/privacy/src/purge.rs:113`) clears it in a transaction of its own, so a request opened or a hold placed between the read and the clear loses its details (second external audit B03, D-1839). One lock order for everything that decides retention, documented in `docs/architecture.md` section 8: (1) a transaction-scoped retention advisory key, exclusive for a purge's decide-and-clear transaction and shared for each hold placement and release in `privacy`; (2) the homeowner row (`lock_homeowner`, which every request-opening writer already takes); (3) the vault contact row. The contact stage and the jobless-request stage (`run_purge`, `run_request_purge`) each take (1) and (2), re-read eligibility after the locks are held in one statement snapshot, and clear the contact in the same transaction (`purge_contact` runs inside it as a savepoint), so a request that commits first is seen and one that commits later waits. The hold authority is durable at the decision: a hold-producing `core.task` (`payments`' dispute hold and `businesses`' complaint hold events for any of her jobs) that is pending or failed counts as a hold, read through one new `core` function, `core::api::unfinished(conn, kind, key_prefix) -> bool` in `app/core/src/task_queries.rs` (exported through `core`'s shared `api.rs`; `intake` may call `core`), so the purge never relies on the hour between stages. No transaction is held across an outside call. PostgreSQL barrier tests in `tests/integration/tests/retention_purge_races.rs`. Update the `intake` and `privacy` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: adapters and stand-ins: local write-once storage that a racing writer cannot alter, object delete and list, and the Twilio message-body delete
tasks.goal: (1) B05 (second external audit, D-1841): `write_once` (`app/adapters/src/storage.rs:72`) writes every attempt to the same deterministic `<name>.<key>.part` with `std::fs::write`, which truncates and rewrites one shared file, then hard-links it into place, so a racing retry can empty or change an object already published. Each attempt now creates its own temporary file exclusively (`create_new`, a random suffix from the OS source), writes it fully, `sync_all`s and closes it, and publishes with `hard_link` (which never replaces an existing object); it compares bytes with an existing object only once that object's publication is complete, and removes only its own temporary file. Directory-fsync crash durability is decided and recorded in the decision entry. (2) D-1803's missing capabilities, additive so no existing fake changes (the `RefundStripe` pattern, D-1753): `StorageDelete: StorageAdapter` with `delete_object(name)` (an absent object is success) and `list_objects(prefix)`, implemented for `LocalStorage`; `SmsBodyDelete: SmsAdapter` with `delete_message_body(sid)` for Twilio's documented message delete (or body redaction, whichever the vendor documents for removing a body; the choice recorded), implemented for `TwilioSms` in `app/adapters/src/sms.rs`. The Twilio stand-in (`stand_ins/twilio.py`, its route in `stand_ins/server.py`) answers that call and afterwards returns no body for the message, and a repeat answers as Twilio does. The real B2 store (T134) and the Twilio sandbox (T129, T131) implement or check the same traits later. The `photos/` prefix uses its own key with read, list and delete; PRIV-029's write-only, prefix-scoped token, versioning and object lock stay in force for the audit-stream and export (backup) prefixes (D-1841). Tests: the competing-writer cases in `app/adapters/src/tests/storage.rs`; the stand-in in `tests/contract/test_twilio_body_delete.py`. Update the `adapters` `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` section 7 and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: server: every request has a whole-request time limit, answered 503 with the security headers
tasks.goal: `tower-http`'s `timeout` feature is enabled (`Cargo.toml:38`) but `build_router` (`app/server/src/lib.rs:75`) applies no time limit, so a request whose body trickles in, or a handler that hangs, holds its connection and task without end (third external audit, D-1870; threat model D13). (1) `app/server/src/request_timeout.rs`: the limit is a setting, `ASKHAVA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS`, added to the typed settings in the shared `app/core/src/settings.rs` (D-493) and read from them at start-up (default 60 seconds, allowed 10 to 300; any other value, or one that is not a whole number, stops start-up with a message naming the key, never the value). 60 seconds is longer than the longest chain of bounded vendor calls one handler makes today (a Confirm press makes at most three Stripe calls at the adapters' 15-second limit, `app/adapters/src/base.rs:211`), so the limit stops only a stalled request, never a slow vendor call the adapters already bound. (2) `build_router` takes the limit and applies it to every route, inside the `security_headers` layer, so a timed-out request is answered `503 Service Unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5`, the SEC-012 headers and `Cache-Control: no-store`, and its handler future is dropped (every write a handler makes is in a transaction or keyed, so a dropped request commits nothing half-done; a webhook sender retries a 503, SEC-017). A Confirm press dropped in the middle of a Stripe call leaves its attempt `sent`; it is never retried until Stripe, asked directly, says it failed (FEE-037's sent-then-fetch path in `confirm_and_pay` and `repeat_press`), so the limit can never cause a second charge. The worker has no HTTP routes and is unchanged. (3) `app/server/tests/request_timeout.rs`, with `tokio::time::pause`: a route that never answers is cut at the limit with 503, `Retry-After`, the security headers and the request ID; a route that answers just inside it is untouched; a body that stops arriving is cut the same way; each bad setting value stops start-up. Update the `server` `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` section 2 (the layer order) and `docs/decisions.md`. (4) Fourth external audit F6 and F37 (D-2208): `build_router` also applies `tower-http`'s `CatchPanicLayer` (the `catch-panic` feature is on, `Cargo.toml:38`) inside the security-headers layer, so a handler that panics is answered 500 with the SEC-012 headers, `no-store` and the request ID and a body that names no panic message; and `ASKHAVA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` with a path after its host (anything but the trailing slash it drops, `app/core/src/settings.rs:397`, the shared typed settings) stops start-up naming the key, since the routes are served at the root and the Twilio signature check signs the public base plus the route path. tasks.title: worked examples: pin D-033 for one-cent-wide recurring ranges at the $500 and $1,500 edges
tasks.goal: D-033 says the fee basis is computed exactly and rounded down to the whole cent once, before the tier is chosen; `four_months` (`app/payments/src/rules.rs:290`) does exactly that for a recurring range, from the sum of its two ends, and no worked example has a recurring range whose midpoint is a half cent, so nothing pins it (third external audit, which read the rule as "floor the midpoint first"; that reading was rejected, D-1874). This is not a fee change. Add rows to `docs/catalog/worked_examples.yaml` after W40 (W41 onward): for each recurring period (weekly, every two weeks, monthly, quarterly, yearly) and each edge ($500.00 and $1,500.00), the one-cent-wide range (low L, high L + $0.01) whose exact 4-month basis is the nearest reachable on each side of the edge (the highest basis below it and the lowest at or above it), plus, where a one-cent-wide range reaches it exactly, the basis a cent above the edge. Worked from `four_months` (`app/payments/src/rules.rs:290`) on `main`: only yearly reaches a cent below, at and a cent above both edges ($1,499.97–$1,499.98 → $499.99, $1,500.00–$1,500.01 → $500.00, $1,500.03–$1,500.04 → $500.01; $4,499.97–$4,499.98, $4,500.00–$4,500.01 and $4,500.03–$4,500.04 for $1,500); quarterly reaches a cent below and at but not a cent above ($374.99–$375.00 → $499.99, $375.00–$375.01 → $500.00; $1,124.99–$1,125.00 and $1,125.00–$1,125.01 for $1,500); weekly, every two weeks and monthly reach none of the three exactly, so their rows are the nearest on each side (weekly $28.84–$28.85 → $499.98 and $28.85–$28.86 → $500.15, $86.53–$86.54 → $1,499.94 and $86.54–$86.55 → $1,500.11; every two weeks $57.68–$57.69 → $499.93 and $57.69–$57.70 → $500.02, $173.07–$173.08 → $1,499.98 and $173.08–$173.09 → $1,500.07; monthly $124.99–$125.00 → $499.98 and $125.00–$125.01 → $500.02, $374.99–$375.00 → $1,499.98 and $375.00–$375.01 → $1,500.02); 22 rows in all, numbered W41 to W62 in this order: weekly, every two weeks, monthly, quarterly, yearly, each period's $500 rows then its $1,500 rows in rising basis (W41–W44 weekly, W45–W48 every two weeks, W49–W52 monthly, W53–W56 quarterly, W57–W62 yearly); the four whose basis is above $1,500 are W44 (weekly, $1,500.11), W48 (every two weeks, $1,500.07), W52 (monthly, $1,500.02) and W62 (yearly, $1,500.01), each $75 under the cap and $199 without it; each row's `fee_basis` and `fee` are worked from D-033 (exact sum of the ends times the period's monthly factor times 4, divided once, rounded down to the cent), with the recurring cap of $75 applying above $1,500 (FEE-039). Example: every two weeks, $57.69 to $57.70: (5,769 + 5,770) × 26 × 4 ÷ (12 × 2) = 50,002.33 cents, basis $500.02, fee $75 (flooring the midpoint first would give $499.98 and $25). Rows a period cannot reach are listed in the decision with the nearest reachable amounts instead. `scripts/check_catalog.py` and `app/payments/src/tests/worked_examples.rs` (`tests::worked_examples`) must pass with their logic unchanged. Two DONE tests pin the recurring rows by data (D-1400), so a new row fails them until their data follows (D-2386): this task also owns `app/payments/src/tests/worked_examples.rs` (T058's), where it adds the new row ids to the `RECURRING` list (`:18`) and its length, and `app/payments/src/tests/recurring.rs` (T188's and T244's), where `checked == 14` (`:130`) rises to exactly 14 plus the rows added (36 for the 22 rows above), the uncapped list `["W20", "W33"]` (`:122`, the rows that pay $199 with the cap removed) gains exactly W44, W48, W52 and W62, and the doc comment above the test (`:98`) names the new rows. Data changes only: no other line of either file changes, no assertion is removed or loosened, and the counts are exact. This is a harness task because the worked examples are a locked catalog file no queued task owns and it takes over two DONE tasks' test files for data only. Update `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: calls and server: a voice read-back confirm connects only the line that was read back
tasks.goal: Fourth external audit F39 (D-2201; CALL-005, CALL-002): after two bad PINs from a business's linked phone the read-back names the homeowner of one line (`calls::routing` answers `Answer::ReadBack(line, words)`, `app/calls/src/routing.rs:406`), but `pins::reply` drops the line (`app/calls/src/pins.rs:299`), the voice route's confirm URL carries only the try number (`app/server/src/inbound_voice.rs:206`), and `voice_confirm` connects whichever open line of the caller's business is newest at the press (`pins.rs:335`), so a line opened, closed or moved between the read-back and the press bridges the caller to a homeowner who was never read back. (1) The line read back is bound to its try: `migrations/0174_calls_readback_line.sql` adds a nullable `readback_line` (the line's ID) to the try's `calls.pin_call` row, inserted with the row: `Step::ReadBack(line)` is known in `judged_count` before `count_once` writes the row, so the line goes in that insert, in that transaction, and no `UPDATE` grant is added. Twilio's resend of the read-back turn returns early in `judged_count` (the row exists) and today `answer_for` recomputes from the live pool; the repeat reads back the bound line from the row instead, never a newly chosen one; the confirm URL stays `?confirm=<try>`, so nothing about the line goes to Twilio or the caller. (2) `voice_confirm` reads the bound line and connects it only when the press confirms, the try is the recorded A-attested read-back try (as today), and that line is still open on the call's pool number and still belongs to the caller's linked business; otherwise it answers as for an unconfirmed press today (ask for the PIN again, or hang up) and never connects another line; the newest-line lookup is removed. (3) Tests in `app/server/tests/voice_confirm_line.rs` through the served voice route with signed fake requests (TD-CALL-17): a second line B opened for the same business between the read-back and the press connects A and never B; the read-back line A closed while B is open, or A no longer the caller's business, connects nobody; a confirm on a try other than the read-back try (a row with no `readback_line`) connects nobody; a resend of the read-back turn reads back the bound line; the unchanged case connects exactly the line read back, and a repeated identical confirm connects it again and writes no second `call_start`. Every existing `app/server/tests/inbound_voice.rs` and `tests/integration/tests/call_pins.rs` case passes unchanged. The overseer runs an independent security review of the hand-in (D-2201). Update the `calls` and `server` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: payments and picks: a dispute's auto-submit mark and its task, and an owner submission and its fee, commit together; a worker decides auto-submit
tasks.goal: Fourth external audit F44 (D-2204; FEE-027, FEE-050): `payments::mark_auto_submit` (`app/payments/src/disputes.rs:169`) commits the `auto_submit` mark and only then queues the submit task, and `record_owner_submission` (`:197`) commits `submitted_at` and only then appends the $15 countering fee, each on whatever connection its caller passes; a failure between the two leaves the mark or `submitted_at` set, every retry answers `false`, and the submit task or the fee is lost for good. Nothing calls `picks::dispute_auto_submit` (`app/picks/src/unreachable_refund.rs:510`) outside tests, so no dispute is ever auto-submitted. (1) In `disputes.rs` both functions open one transaction on the connection they are given (`Acquire::begin`, a savepoint inside a caller's transaction) for their two writes, so the mark and its task, and `submitted_at` and its fee, commit together or not at all; `record_dispute` queues one `picks.dispute_opened` `core.task` (dedupe key per dispute) in the transaction that records a new dispute. (2) `app/picks/src/dispute_steps.rs` holds the `picks.dispute_opened` handler, registered in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs`: it reads whether the disputed charge's pick was released, its call attempts (`calls::api::call_log` through T270's `call_record`), and whether the payment was 3DS-authenticated: it first calls T405's `payments::api::record_three_ds` for the disputed pick (with a `StripePayments` client that `worker_registry` in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` (`:456`) builds from the settings as `release_sink.rs`'s private `stripe_client` (`:226`) does: the secret key, the mode's base URL and the SEC-032 base-URL check, built in `lib.rs` without editing `release_sink.rs`; worker_registry builds no Stripe client today; the handler is registered on every path: with no Stripe key (dev and CI) it records nothing and reads only what is stored, which is false when nothing is, and in test and live a missing key is a start-up error naming it, as `notice_senders` does; a fetch error is retried by the queue), then reads `payments::api::three_ds_authenticated`, where no stored row or an unknown result reads as `false` (D-3118); and calls `dispute_auto_submit` in one transaction; a failed run is retried by the queue and a repeat marks nothing twice. FEE-050 is judged again at the due date less `SUBMIT_BEFORE` (2 days): `record_dispute` also queues a second `picks.dispute_opened` run for that time (its own dedupe key), so a call attempt or release recorded after the dispute opened still marks it before the submit task runs; an already-marked or submitted dispute is unchanged. (3) Tests in `tests/integration/tests/dispute_submit.rs` (TD-FEE-51): a failure injected between the mark and its task, and between `submitted_at` and its fee, leaves neither, and the retry marks, queues or records once; a released, called dispute is marked through the worker; a released dispute with no call attempt is marked only when its stored 3DS result is authenticated (T405's fake source), and waits for Casey when it is not or is unknown; and its evidence submitted 2 days before the due date; a dispute whose first call attempt is logged after it opened is marked by the run at due less 2 days; an unreleased one waits for Casey; Casey's own submission (`record_owner_submission` called directly: T205's page and T304's route depend on this task, so they come later) records the fee once and stops the auto-submit. `payments` is money code: its 95% branch floor holds; the overseer runs an independent money review of the hand-in (D-2204). Now, in `refunds.rs` (with a shared check in `refund_stripe.rs` that `reconcile` also uses, T334): a succeeded refund in `usd` whose reported amount is present and differs from the charged amount records the ledger refund at the amount Stripe reported (the ledger matches the money), raises one High `payments.refund_amount_mismatch` alert for that pick (only while none is open for it), and sends no "refunded in full" notice; a refund whose currency is present and not `usd` is treated as unconfirmed: it is recorded at the charged amount, never at the foreign figure, with one High `payments.refund_amount_unconfirmed` alert, and no "refunded in full" notice; a refund whose amount is missing is re-read once with `fetch_refund`, and if it is still missing it is recorded at the charged amount (the app only asks for full refunds) with the same unconfirmed alert, and its notice goes as today; a refund with an amount but no currency is handled as a missing amount (re-read once, then recorded at the charged amount with the unconfirmed alert, its notice going), never booked at the reported figure. Its callers pass the `Refund` they hold: `refund_event`, and `run_refund_check` (`app/payments/src/refunds.rs:661`, the `Refund` it fetched); the owned `refund_lifecycle.rs` calls (:303, :305) change only to pass a `Refund`, and no expected value changes. A new read `refund_in_full(pool, stripe, pick)` in `refunds.rs` (exported through `api.rs`) answers `false` only on positive evidence that the pick's succeeded refund is not the whole charge in `usd`: the ledger holds its refund at an amount other than the charge, or a re-read of its `re_…` with `fetch_refund` reports a currency other than `usd` or a `usd` amount other than the charge; it answers `true` when the re-read reports no amount or no currency, or fails with `AdapterError::NotSent` (what the provided `read_refund` answers, `app/adapters/src/payments.rs:189`, and so the test fakes), so a missing amount's notice goes as D-2303 says; any other read error is `Err(MoneyEventError::Stripe)`, never `true`, because a foreign-currency refund must not be announced and neither the ledger nor an alert tells it from a missing amount. tasks.title: payments: the nightly reconcile catches up after an outage from its last good run, reads Stripe in pages, and checks refund amounts
tasks.goal: Sixth audit U-07 and U-05's reconcile half (D-2304, D-2303; FEE-029, FEE-051, FEE-028). After T288 (which keeps unsettled charges open) and T333: (1) `LOOKBACK` is 7 days (`app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:71`), so a charge whose events all fell before a reconcile outage of more than 7 days is never read. `migrations/0178_payments_reconcile_checkpoint.sql` adds `payments.reconcile_checkpoint` (one row: the start of the last run that finished; app role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of that column only); each run reads every charge created since the earlier of now − 7 days and that time − 1 day, with no cap (the charge list, `GET /v1/charges` with `created[gte]`, has no 30-day limit), so no charge is skipped however long the outage; when the gap since the last finished run is over 2 days it also raises one High `payments.reconcile_gap` alert, as information only (it skips nothing); the checkpoint moves only when a run finishes. (2) `ReconcileStripe::list_charges` (:84) returns an unbounded `Vec`; it stays as it is, and the trait gains a paged read, `list_charges_page` (`since`, a cursor, a page size of at most 100; it returns the page and the next cursor, none after the last page), with a provided body built on `list_charges` the way `fetch_charge`'s is (:89 to :99): it orders the list by charge ID (`StripeCharge` has no creation time, `app/payments/src/models.rs:631`, and no field is added, since done tests build it by name), the cursor is the last ID of the previous page and a page holds the charges with a greater ID (plan change D-3055); T335's override keeps Stripe's own order and cursor. The run reads only through `list_charges_page` and handles one page at a time in bounded batches, committing page by page, so memory and transaction size do not grow with volume; the FEE-030 cent-match totals (gross charges, refunds, disputes, fees) accumulate across pages and are compared once at the end of the run. And the fake's sent log filters by the app's own `MessageKey` (`stand_ins/server.py:124`), which Twilio cannot store. Fix: (1) `TwilioSms` (built in `app/adapters/src/base.rs:106`) carries the status URL, `<ASKHAVA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/webhooks/twilio/status` (Twilio signs the full callback URL, and `verify_webhook` checks the public base, path and query, `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs:162`, `:173`, so the URL sent must be exactly the URL the route rebuilds), and `send_text` adds `StatusCallback` to every create; the base URL is a setting of the composition, not of `TwilioConfig` (`app/adapters/src/config.rs`, T016's, whose `twilio_clients(&config)` is called in done adapter tests this task does not own), so `TwilioSms` gains a setter taking the status URL, called where the composition builds the client (`app/server/src/lib.rs:483`, shared) from `Settings::public_base_url` (D-3112); with no public base URL (dev and CI without webhooks) it sends none, as today. (2) `stand_ins/twilio.py`: `create_message` stores the `StatusCallback` it was given; `status_callback` for a message created without one refuses (the control route answers 409 and records no callback), and with one returns the URL with the params, so a test posts to the URL the app asked for. (3) The fake's Messages list honours Twilio's own filters `To`, `From`, `DateSent`, `DateSent<` and `DateSent>` (dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, UTC); `MessageKey` stays a stand-in-only filter, documented in `stand_ins/server.py` as test-only and used only by `core::test_control`, never by app code (T110 matches without it, D-2764). (4) Tests: `tests/integration/tests/sms_status_callback.rs` sends a text through the adapter against the served stand-in with a public base URL set and asserts the fake recorded `StatusCallback` equal to that URL plus `/webhooks/twilio/status` (fails before the fix), and that the route accepts the callback the fake then gives (signature over that URL); `tests/contract/test_twilio_contract.py` and `tests/contract/test_stand_in_server.py`: no callback for a message created without `StatusCallback`, one aimed at the given URL with it, and the `From` and `DateSent` filters. tasks.title: adapters, calls and stand-in (harness): every outbound call carries its TwiML and status callbacks, and the safety call's answer is received
tasks.goal: Nov 11 vendor-double review batch 4, F3 (D-2762; CALL-006, CALL-022, OPS-028, INT-004, SEC-016). `TwilioVoice::open_call` posts only `To` and `From` (`app/adapters/src/voice.rs:55`); Twilio's Calls API needs one of `Url`, `Twiml` or `ApplicationSid` and refuses the create without one, and fetches the call's TwiML only from that parameter. So once T330 registers `place_safety_call` (`app/calls/src/voice.rs:319`) and T108 calls `ring_owner` (`:492`, whose comment expects `owner_bridge_twiml` to run on Casey's answered leg), every safety call and owner bridge fails at Twilio; and no call asks for status callbacks, so `safety_call_answered` (`:464`) is never called. The fake's `create_call` (`stand_ins/twilio.py:264`) takes `To` and `From` only and succeeds. Fix: (1) `VoiceAdapter::open_call` (`app/adapters/src/voice.rs:26`) gains one parameter, a `&CallPlan` (new, in `voice.rs`: the script and the callback settings below), so no create can leave without a script (D-3112: chosen over a second trait method with a default body, which would keep a script-less create that Twilio refuses); it takes the call's script as inline `Twiml` (at most 4,000 characters) for both call kinds, never a `Url` (the owner bridge's TwiML holds the homeowner's number, which must never sit in a URL, so no TwiML-serving route is added), a `StatusCallback` URL on the public base and its `StatusCallbackEvent` list; the safety call asks for Twilio's answering-machine detection with `MachineDetection`, `AsyncAmd=true` and `AsyncAmdStatusCallback` pointing at the same status route with the same alert query (the worker cites the Calls API page). (2) `place_safety_call` sends `safety_twiml` (with its `Gather` `action` an absolute URL on the public base, since inline TwiML has no document URL to resolve a relative one against) and `ring_owner` sends `owner_bridge_twiml` (its signature gains the homeowner's number and the safety words; T108, after this task, calls the new form); a script builder's `None` places no call and logs as today. (3) Two new signed routes in `app/server/src/voice_status.rs`, merged in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` like `inbound_voice` and verified like every Twilio webhook over the public base, path and query (SEC-016); each query carries only the alert ID. (a) `POST /webhooks/twilio/voice/status?alert=<id>`: with async detection Twilio posts `answered` before the detection result and without `AnsweredBy`, so the call is decided only by the detection result (`AnsweredBy` `human` to `Person`, `machine_start`, `machine_end_*` and `fax` to `Machine`, `unknown` to `Unknown`) or by a final `CallStatus` of `no-answer`, `busy`, `failed` or `canceled` (`Nobody`); `safety_call_answered` runs once per CallSid (the first deciding post wins); any other callback (`initiated`, `ringing`, `answered`, a `completed` after a decision) is acknowledged and changes nothing; an owner-bridge callback is acknowledged and changes nothing. (b) `POST /webhooks/twilio/voice/safety-key?alert=<id>`, the absolute `Gather` `action` that `safety_twiml` (`app/calls/src/voice.rs:226`) posts the key press to: it calls `safety_call_key` (`:411`; "9" puts her number on the suppression list, CON-035) and answers `hangup_twiml`; a repeat post for the same CallSid changes nothing. (4) `stand_ins/twilio.py`: `create_call` refuses a create with none of `Url`, `Twiml`, `ApplicationSid` with Twilio's 400 error shape, stores the callback URL and events, and a control emits callbacks only to the stored URLs, as Twilio does: `answered` without `AnsweredBy`, then, when detection was asked, the detection result as a separate post to the `AsyncAmdStatusCallback`, then `completed`. Tests: `tests/contract/test_twilio_voice_contract.py` (the refusal, the stored callback, no callback without one) and `tests/integration/tests/voice_call_plan.rs` (a safety call through the served stand-in carries its TwiML and callback, fails before the fix; a `human` detection result acknowledges the alert once; `answered` followed by `machine_end_beep` never acknowledges it (OPS-028); `no-answer` logs `nobody`; a repeat callback changes nothing; a key press of 9 on the safety-key route puts her number on the suppression list and answers hang-up TwiML, another key does not; the owner bridge carries `owner_bridge_twiml`). If T330 has registered `place_safety_call`, update its registration in the shared `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs`. T131 checks the parameters against Twilio. Update `app/calls/CLAUDE.md`, `app/adapters/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` (section 7 and the two rows in the section 13 route table) and `docs/decisions.md`. Plan change D-3112: done tests this task did not write implement or call `open_call` and `ring_owner`: the fakes `FakeVoice` and `RefusingVoice` (`tests/integration/tests/voice_calls.rs:90`, `:118`; T080, T383), `ring_owner`'s call at `tests/integration/tests/voice_calls.rs:388`, and the calls at `app/adapters/src/tests/adapter_config.rs:397` (T016, T338; against the stand-in, which now refuses a create with no script) and `tests/integration/tests/no_recording.rs:94` (T078). Also (review round): `stand_ins/server.py:154` passes only `To` and `From` to `create_call`, so the served stand-in could not receive `Twiml`, `StatusCallback`, `StatusCallbackEvent`, `MachineDetection`, `AsyncAmd` or `AsyncAmdStatusCallback` nor offer the callback control route, and the done `tests/contract/test_stand_in_server.py:165` (T167, T377) creates a call with only `To` and `From` and expects 201, which the refusal breaks; this task owns both: `server.py` passes the new form fields and adds the control route, and the contract test's one create gains a fixture `Twiml` (one line, its assertions unchanged). This task owns the three Rust files for signature-only edits: each fake gains the unused plan parameter, each call passes a fixture plan (in `no_recording.rs` a TwiML holding no "record", so its assertion over the request still holds as written) and `ring_owner`'s call its new arguments; no assertion, case or expected value changes, none is removed and no case is added there.

tasks.title: portals and server: security-event rows are capped per address, and webhook refusals are security events
tasks.goal: Plan change D-3445 split T319 in two: this task caps security-event rows and makes webhook refusals security events; T436 adds the daily session sweep and the rate-limit prune. Fourth external audit F14 and F5 (D-2207; SEC-048, SEC-016): (1) `portals::security`'s refusal (`app/portals/src/security.rs:96`) takes a pool connection and writes a security-event row before any limit, so a flood of cross-site or bad-CSRF requests turns each into a database write. An in-process counter, checked before the pool is touched, writes at most N rows per (event kind, client address as SEC-040 takes it, route) per minute and only counts the rest, logged as one line per minute with the count and no address; the 403 answer is unchanged. N is a setting in the shared `app/core/src/settings.rs` whose default is `EVENTS_PER_HOUR_ALERT` (50, `app/portals/src/security.rs:59`) and which is clamped up to it (a lower value is raised to it and logged at start-up), because the burst alert counts stored rows over the last hour (`security.rs:318`), so a cap below the threshold would stop it from ever firing. `WebSecurity::new(pool, clock)` is called in seven files this task does not own (`feedback.rs`, `pick_flow.rs`, `checkin.rs`, `quote_page.rs`, `business_auth.rs` in `app/portals/src/`, and `tests/security/tests/link_scanners.rs`, `cookies_csrf.rs`), so its signature does not change: N reaches the counter through a process-wide setter in `security.rs` called once from the shared `app/server/src/main.rs` at start-up, the default holding when it is never called (tests) (D-3134). Until T135 proves that the edge overwrites the client-address header, a forged header must not buy a fresh cap: the counter also keeps a per-(kind, route) ceiling of N rows per minute across all addresses, so a flood with a new forged address on each request still writes at most N rows a minute per kind and route (the burst alert fires from those). (2) The Stripe, Twilio text and Twilio voice webhook routes answer a source or signature refusal 403 with a log line and record no security event, so SEC-048's hourly alert never sees them and a rotated Stripe address list fails silently. `app/server/src/webhook_refusals.rs` is a layer the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` puts on those three routers only: each 403 they answer records one `webhook_signature_failed` event (route and request ID, no actor) through `portals::api::record_security_event`, under the same cap; first check that those routes answer 403 for nothing else, and if one does, tell the cases apart without reading the body. Tests in `tests/security/tests/security_event_cap.rs` (TD-SEC-53); every existing security-event test passes unchanged. Update the `portals` and `server` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: payments: a won dispute records the countering fee's return and the disputed amount's return, and the reconcile compares only disputes not won
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, payments F2 (D-2625; FEE-027 to FEE-030, FEE-050; D-1383, D-1753): `charge.dispute.closed` (`dispute_closed`, `app/payments/src/routes.rs:537`) only writes an audit row and a High alert; it never reads the event's `status` (`read_object` keeps only `/id`), and no code writes `EntryKind::CounteringFeeReturn` (`app/payments/src/ledger.rs:32`). So when Casey wins a $75 dispute whose evidence was submitted, the ledger keeps the `dispute` 9000 and the `countering-fee` 1500 as lost, `MoneyView::net()` understates by $90 for good, the money view keeps a dispute that was won, and the reconcile cannot see it because `MoneyTotals::of_stripe` counts a dispute whatever its status. D-1383 left "how a won dispute's returned amount is recorded" to the dispute tasks, and none took it. Fix: `dispute_closed` reads `status`; on `won`, in the event's transaction and once per dispute, it appends a `countering-fee-return` equal to the recorded countering fee (when one was recorded, FEE-050) and a `dispute-reversal` of the disputed amount (Stripe's $15 dispute fee itself stays a cost: `docs/brains/payments-stripe.md:102` returns only the countering fee on a win), the stored code made only by a `LedgerEntry` constructor and folded by every ledger reader as a negative dispute, as D-1753 did for `refund-reversal` (not an `EntryKind` variant, so `portals`' exhaustive statement match is untouched; `migrations/0184_payments_dispute_reversal.sql` adds the code to the ledger's `kind` check; FEE-028 lists it since D-2625); any other closing status changes nothing but the audit and alert as today. The `dispute-reversal` row carries the dispute's `dp_` ID as its Stripe ID. The reconcile compares the disputed amounts of disputes not won only, with no Stripe read: in its ledger read (`ledger_totals`, `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:897` once T334 is on `main`) it also reads which of the listed `dp_` IDs already have a `dispute-reversal` row and leaves those disputes out of both sides (a won dispute is known from the webhook). `DisputeStripe` (`app/payments/src/disputes.rs:42`) has only `submit_evidence`, and carrying a status on `StripeCharge.dispute` (`app/payments/src/models.rs:643`) would break its literals in six files this task does not own, so neither changes (D-3134). Tests in `tests/integration/tests/dispute_won.rs` (TD-FEE-65), each failing on today's `main`: after a submitted dispute, a `won` closure leaves `MoneyView.dispute_fees` equal to the dispute fee only and the net disputed amount 0; the same event again appends nothing; a `lost` closure changes no ledger row; a won dispute with no countering fee appends no `countering-fee-return`; the reconcile over a won dispute raises no difference. Money: 95% branch floor; the overseer runs an independent money review of the hand-in. Update the `payments` `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md`. The business statement's wording for a won dispute is T204's (it owns `app/portals/src/business_portal.rs`); this task only folds the new code in the ledger readers it owns.

tasks.title: privacy: key rotation re-seals stored photos too, so dropping the old vault key never makes a photo unreadable
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, privacy F2 (D-2626; PRIV-023, PRIV-024): `rotate_batch` (`app/privacy/src/vault.rs:668`) moves `privacy.contact` and `privacy.stated_name` to the newest key, but no code re-seals `privacy.photo` (only the INSERT at `app/privacy/src/photos.rs:358`; the app role has no UPDATE on it), and `PhotoSeal::open` needs the row's `key_version` in its key map. The documented drill (`app/privacy/CLAUDE.md`: run `rotate_batch` until it returns 0, then drop `1:`) therefore makes every photo sealed under v1 fail with `PhotoError::Sealed` (not even `LinkDead`) for the rest of its life (job close plus 30 days, longer under a dispute hold), or forces the old key to stay live, which defeats a rotation after a key leak. Fix: `rotate_photos(db, seal, storage, limit)` in `photos.rs` re-seals, in bounded batches, each photo whose `key_version` is below the active one: it reads the object, opens it under its version and AAD, seals it under the active version and AAD, writes it as a new object, then moves the row to the new object and version in one statement that matches the row only while it still holds the old `key_version` and `storage_key` it read (a row moved meanwhile is left alone and its new object becomes an orphan for the sweep) and deletes the old object only after that commits (a crash at any step leaves a readable photo and at most one orphan, which the orphan sweep removes, D-1793); `migrations/0180_privacy_photo_reseal.sql` grants the app role UPDATE on exactly those columns of `privacy.photo`. The drill in the crate doc becomes: run `rotate_batch` and `rotate_photos` until both return 0, then drop the old key. No plaintext is logged or kept; open audits are not written for a re-seal (it returns nothing to a reader). Tests in `tests/integration/tests/photo_key_rotation.rs` (TD-PRIV-24), each failing on today's `main` where noted: a photo stored under v1, then the drill with `2:K2,1:K1`, then `VAULT_KEY=2:K2` alone: `open_link` still returns the same bytes (fails today); a run over no old photos returns 0; a re-seal interrupted after the new object is written leaves the photo readable under the old row; the row's version and the AAD bind the new object. `the_rotation_drill_moves_every_row_to_v2` passes unchanged. Update the `privacy` `CLAUDE.md`, the key-rotation runbook line it cites, and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: picks: the release claim re-checks the pick under its row lock, and a fraud end refuses a pick already released
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, privacy F3, as fixed by the plan review's H3 and its re-review (D-2627; PICK-022, PRIV-005, FEE-052): the release claim reads its target unlocked (`show`, `app/picks/src/release.rs:287`, through `release_target`) and `record` (`:428`) inserts `picks.release` with `ON CONFLICT (pick_id)` only, while `fraud_warning` (`app/picks/src/unreachable_refund.rs:533`) first calls `payments::api::early_fraud_warning` (`app/payments/src/refunds.rs:152`) with the caller's `released` snapshot, before any lock, so the refund is sent while a racing release can still commit and open the name and address: the business gets the refund and the details (FEE-052 refunds only a charge whose details were not yet released). Fix, all in `picks`: (1) the fraud path first runs one short transaction that takes `SELECT … FROM picks.pick WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE`, then, in a separate statement under that lock, reads whether a `picks.release` row exists; the pick counts as released when that row exists or the caller's `released` flag already says so (stricter only: a caller's `true` is never read as `false`, D-3118; the done `tests/integration/tests/unreachable_refund.rs` (T191, T282) passes `true` for a pick with no release row at `:487`, expects `Ok(false)` and, at `:500`, exactly one succeeded refund for that pick, from its later `false` call); if it counts as released the warning only alerts (the pick goes to Casey's decision list, as today); if none exists it inserts a durable marker, one `picks.fraud_hold` row for the pick (`migrations/0181_picks_fraud_hold.sql`: pick ID primary key, time; the app role may INSERT and SELECT only), idempotently (`ON CONFLICT (pick_id) DO NOTHING`, since the fraud path may run again for the same pick: the done `unreachable_refund.rs` calls it at `:489` to `:493` with a failing refund client and again at `:497` with a working one, which must then refund), and commits; only then does it call `early_fraud_warning` with `released` as decided under that lock (false here), so the refund goes out only for a pick that can no longer be released; the existing job move and `fraud_refunded` end follow as today once the refund is read as succeeded; (2) `record` takes the same `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the pick first in the claim's transaction, then, in a separate statement, checks that the pick still has the wanted status, no end and no `picks.fraud_hold` row, and answers `MovedOn` otherwise: on a regular job (`claim_then_read`, `:322`) that is before any vault read; an emergency job reads the vault before it claims (`read_then_claim`, `:340`, INT-029), so there the refused claim follows a read but shows and releases nothing; (3) `end_pick` (`:482`) keeps its status-only guard: `no_call_at_72_hours` (`:451`) and the other callers end released picks through it, and only the fraud path checks for a release row. This is a clarification consistent with FEE-052's order (alert; refund an unreleased charge at once; list a released one): "not yet released" is decided under the pick's lock and the release is then refused, never both. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/release_fraud_race.rs` (TD-PICK-59), two connections and row locks, no sleeps: (a) the claim locks the pick, inserts its release row and holds its transaction open; the fraud path blocks on the pick lock; the claim commits; the fraud path then finds the release row, writes no hold and sends no refund (the fake refund client is never called); (b) on a regular (non-emergency) job, the fraud path commits its hold first; the claim then answers `MovedOn`, writes no release row and no `vault_read.picks.release` audit row, and the refund is sent once; (c) `no_call_at_72_hours` still ends a released, paid pick as a no-show; the plain release and the plain fraud end behave as before. Update the `picks` `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md`. Any test this task writes that builds an `adapters::api::PaymentIntent` (a fake `IntentStripe` or `PaymentsAdapter` answering an intent) builds it with `serde_json::from_value` (the type derives `Deserialize`), never a struct literal, and gives a succeeded intent a fake `ch_` `latest_charge`, so T352's new field (`#[serde(default)]`) breaks no file T352 does not own (D-3134).

tasks.title: messaging and server (harness): the worker sends queued texts once, re-checking quiet hours, the line and the suppression list at the moment of sending
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, messaging F4 and batch 2 jobs F1, D-2188's unowned follow-up, and the plan review's M4 (D-2628; QH-001, QH-006, QH-008, TXT-011, TXT-014, TXT-021, CON-009, CON-030; D-558). Three defects in one path. (a) Nothing in production sends a `messaging.outbox` row: `send_on_line` (`app/messaging/src/mode.rs:225`) and `send_checked` (`app/messaging/src/optout.rs:310`) have only test callers, so no consent text, HELP reply, opt-out confirmation or job text reaches a phone. (b) The send path never checks quiet hours and the outbox has no not-before time, so once a sender drains rows as written, a row queued at night goes at once. (c) A text can go out twice: `claim` (`app/messaging/src/models.rs:211`) takes rows in `queued` or `sending`, and `send` (`app/messaging/src/service.rs:184`) resends a `sending` row under the same key, relying on carrier dedupe Twilio does not do (D-558; the done test `td_txt_04_a_killed_worker_resends_under_the_same_key_and_delivers_once` passes only because its fake carrier dedupes by key); it fails after an accept followed by a 15-second client timeout, the 120-second handler timeout, a kill during the drain, or a lost lease while a second worker reclaims the row. Fix: (1) `migrations/0182_messaging_outbox_not_before.sql` adds nullable `not_before` and `sending_since` columns and widens the outbox `status` check (`migrations/0042_messaging_outbox.sql:29`, and any later widening) to add `expired` and `unknown`; (2) `not_before` is set at enqueue from the row's message kind and `rules::decide` (`Hold { until }`), with no change to `NewText` or any struct done tests build by name; the quiet-hours recheck at the send instant lives in the sender, not in `send_checked` or `claim` (plan change D-3055): before each send, `outbox_sender.rs` re-runs the quiet-hours rule at that instant (QH-001, QH-008 for a retry) with the QH-004 exemption decided when the row was queued, not from the kind alone: the outbox row records no emergency flag and no inbound time (`migrations/0042_messaging_outbox.sql:21` to `:34`), so `migrations/0182_messaging_outbox_not_before.sql` (this task's) also adds a nullable `quiet_exempt_until`, written at enqueue from the facts `rules::decide` reads (`rules::Outgoing`, `app/messaging/src/rules.rs:180`): `infinity` for an any-hour kind (the 911 text, keyword replies, pick codes, the after-hours notice) and for an emergency job's quote, quote-count, question and pick-step texts; the person's inbound time plus 15 minutes for a direct reply; empty otherwise (the business-email exemption is email, not the outbox). Plain `enqueue` (`app/messaging/src/service.rs:141`, this task's) writes `infinity` itself for an any-hour kind, read from the row's template ID, so no producer of those kinds needs a change; the two facts a template ID cannot show (an emergency job, a direct reply's inbound time) come through a new entry point beside it, `enqueue_exempt`, so `NewText` is unchanged. No producer file is changed here: every production producer calls plain `enqueue` (`app/picks/src/service.rs:195`, `app/intake/src/routing.rs:516`, `conversation.rs:438`, `service.rs:301`, `closing.rs:209`, `handlers.rs:360`, `job_texts.rs:358`, `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs:541`), and T402 moves those that queue an emergency job's texts or a direct reply to `enqueue_exempt`; until then such a text queued at night waits for 8 a.m., the safe side of QH-004 (plan change D-3106); at send the row goes when the instant is inside the window or before `quiet_exempt_until` (a direct reply sent after its 15 minutes waits for the window, as `rules::retry` says), and on a hold sets `not_before` and leaves the row `queued` without reaching the carrier; `send_checked` and `send_on_line` keep their consent, suppression and line checks and gain no clock rule, because done tests call `send_checked` directly at night for ordinary `first_quote` rows and expect them to go (`tests/integration/tests/help_start.rs:191` and `:207`, T030's, at `NIGHT`, 23:00 Arizona time; `tests/integration/tests/optout_flow.rs:198` and `:448`, T029's, at `NOW`, 00:33 Arizona time); the sender is their only production caller (defect (a)), and no other production code may call them for a row of a quiet-hours kind; the CON-018 HELP reply and the CON-009 confirmation keep their any-hour rule; (3) the fence: `claim` takes only a `queued` row, moving it to `sending` with `sending_since` in one statement, so two senders can never both hold it; the sender's own due query picks only rows whose `not_before` has passed, and `claim` does not read `not_before`, for the same done tests; the carrier call runs outside any transaction; a definite refusal (the vendor's 4xx, 21610 as today) moves the row back to `queued` for the TXT-014 retries or blocks it, inside `service::send` itself (`app/messaging/src/service.rs:185`), not in the sender: the done `tests/integration/tests/text_retries.rs` (`:157` to `:159`) calls `send_checked` four times on one row with a carrier answering `AdapterError::NotSent` and expects `Err(Carrier)` each time, so the row is `queued` again before `send` returns (`AdapterError::OutcomeUnknown` is the unknown outcome); an unknown outcome (timeout, connection lost after the request was sent) and any row still `sending` 5 minutes after `sending_since` (a crash) move to `unknown` and are never resent blind, the move dropping the row's body in the same statement (`retention::cut_bodies`, `app/messaging/src/retention.rs:129`, cuts only `queued` and `sending` rows, so `0182` also widens `outbox_body_check`, `migrations/0089_messaging_retries_email.sql:24`, to let `unknown` and `expired` rows hold no body; a row marked `expired` drops its body the same way): an important text (TXT-014) goes to its email copy and portal line as after its last retry, and one Low `messaging.send_outcome_unknown` alert is raised per row with no body or phone; (4) `app/messaging/src/outbox_sender.rs`: a `messaging.send_due` worker task, registered in `worker_registry` in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` (T327, D-2849; `bin/worker.rs` only calls it) with the Twilio settings like `picks.line_retry`, claims due rows in bounded batches, sends each through `send_on_line`, sweeps stale `sending` rows to `unknown`, and re-queues itself; (5) a non-reply row queued while its line was paused, switched off or suspended is marked `expired` with one audit row and never sent (D-2188), and a CON-009 confirmation older than 5 minutes is never sent (CON-030). This is a harness task because it rewrites the done TD-TXT-04 test in `tests/integration/tests/outbox.rs`, whose premise (the carrier dedupes a resend) D-558 left unverified and is false for Twilio: the killed-worker case now asserts one carrier call and the row `unknown`, never two calls; every other assertion in that file is kept. The Twilio sent-log lookup that could settle an `unknown` row (OPS-017) is not built here. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/outbox_sender.rs` (TD-QH-05), through the worker with the stand-in Twilio and a fake carrier that does not dedupe: a `caller_missed` row queued at 21:30 Arizona time for a 928 number is not sent at 21:31 and is sent at 08:00; a consent text queued at 14:00 goes at once; a suppressed number gets only HELP; a row queued while the line was suspended is expired when it reopens; a confirmation goes within 5 minutes or never; a worker killed after the carrier accepted leaves one delivery and the row `unknown` after 5 minutes, never two deliveries; two workers racing for one row make one carrier call; a timeout gives `unknown`, the email copy for an important text, and one alert. Every other TD-TXT and TD-CON case and `suspension_mode.rs` pass unchanged. Update the `messaging` and `server` `CLAUDE.md` files, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: server, messaging and intake: START into an open request restarts with the consent text, an opt-out while texting is off is confirmed by email, CANCEL pauses the job, and a listed homeowner who writes is followed up
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, messaging F2, F3 and F5 and CON-016, the route half (D-2629; CON-001, CON-015, CON-016, CON-028, CON-029, CON-030; D-1229). After T336 (the last earlier owner of `inbound_text.rs`), T356 and T360 (the emails). (1) START into a still-open request: the route treats `Outcome::Resubscribed` like `Open` (`app/server/src/inbound_text.rs:387`) and passes "START" to `intake::receive_reply`, whose rules send no consent text once one was sent (`app/intake/src/rules.rs:100`), so a homeowner who opted out and texts START later gets no consent text and "START" is heard as an answer (CON-015, CON-001). Now the route calls a new `intake::api::restart_after_start` (`app/intake/src/resubscribe.rs`), which queues the existing consent text again under the START inbox row as its subject, records it as sent, and passes nothing to the open question. (2) An opt-out while the homeowner line is switched off, suspended or restored and waiting gets no confirmation: `confirm` (`app/messaging/src/optout.rs:195`) answers "email instead" only for the ops pause and never reads `messaging.mode_state`, and the route drops the `email` flag (`inbound_text.rs:372`). Now `confirm` decides "paused" from the same facts `send_on_line` uses and queues no text then, and the route queues one follow-up task (below) for the confirmation email. (3) D-1229 named the inbound route to call `intake::api::on_opt_out` after `Outcome::OptedOut`; no task did, and T330 builds only the `intake.opted_out_live_job` handler that `on_opt_out` queues (it owns no route file), so a sole CANCEL while a pick waits for Confirm neither pauses the job nor withdraws the pick; the route now calls `on_opt_out` in the delivery's transaction, and T330's handler does the rest. (4) CON-016: on `Outcome::Suppressed` with no START the route queues one follow-up task for T360's `queue_optout_wrote_again`; the CON-017 emergency alert is unchanged. The follow-up (D-3118): T360's functions take the key secret and the footer postal address, `Webhooks` (`inbound_text.rs:87`) holds no postal address and is built by literal in seven done test files, and `Outcome::OptedOut` (`app/messaging/src/optout.rs:109`) carries no event ID or language and is matched field by field in `tests/integration/tests/optout_flow.rs` (`:160`, `:340`, `:389`, `:414`), so neither changes: in the delivery's transaction the route queues one `core.task` of a new kind (payload: the inbox row ID, her contact ID, her language code and which follow-up; IDs and codes only; dedupe key per inbox row and follow-up), and its handler, in `optout.rs`, finds the opt-out event by its `inbox_id` (`messaging.optout_event`, migration 0128), reads her email through the vault only (never logged or put in a payload) and calls T360's function. It is registered in `worker_registry` in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` (`:456`) beside `register_notice_senders` (`:582`), built from the `ID_SECRET` and `Settings::postal_address` (`app/core/src/settings.rs:365`, T313, D-3098) as `notice_senders` (`:556`) reads it, not in `register_handlers` (`:382`), which takes no settings; it is registered on every path so `tests/integration/tests/task_registry.rs` (TD-OPS-36) finds the kind: with no postal address (dev and CI) it sends nothing and ends done, and the tests run it with a fixture postal address. No new customer copy here (the consent text exists; the emails are T360's). Tests in `tests/integration/tests/optout_followups.rs` (TD-CON-33) through the served route, each failing on today's `main`: open request, STOP, then START with `OptOutType=START` gives one `consent` outbox row for the START inbox row and no intake answer holding "START"; a suspended line, a phrase opt-out and an email on file give one queued follow-up task and, once its handler runs, one queued confirmation email, and no outbox text; CANCEL with a waiting pick gives an `intake.homeowner_pause` row and one queued `intake.opted_out_live_job`; a listed homeowner's plain text gives, once the follow-up runs, one queued email (email on file) or one `messaging.optout_wrote_again` audit row. Every TD-TXT, TD-CON and TD-SEC-52 case passes unchanged. Update the `server` and `intake` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: messaging: the Canadian area codes for the HELP roaming line come from the quiet-hours table, which gains the four new Ontario codes
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, messaging F6 (D-2630; CON-018, QH-002, D-100): the two area-code tables disagree. `CANADIAN_AREA_CODES` (`app/messaging/src/keywords.rs:25`) lists 382, 683, 753 and 942, which `app/messaging/area_codes.json` (the quiet-hours zone table) lacks, so a homeowner on one of those numbers gets the HELP reply and nothing else (`NotTextable`); and 257 (British Columbia) is in the zone table but not in the Canadian list, so its HELP reply misses the roaming line. Fix: the four Ontario codes join `area_codes.json` under their zone (each checked against the North American numbering plan's published assignment, cited in the decision), and the Canadian set is derived from the zone table's Canadian entries (one source; a code's country is read from its zone, the table's Canadian zones such as `America/Toronto` and `America/Vancouver`; no tag or other key is added to the file, since `AreaCodes::parse` (`app/messaging/src/rules.rs:70`, not owned) reads only `{zone: [codes]}` and refuses a key that is not a known time zone (`:74`), D-3094), so the two cannot drift. Tests in `app/messaging/src/tests/area_codes.rs` (TD-QH-06), each failing on today's `main`: every code of the Canadian set has a zone in the table; 257 gets the roaming line; 382, 683, 753 and 942 are textable inside 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. in both Arizona and Toronto time; a US code never gets the roaming line. Every TD-QH and TD-CON case passes unchanged. Update the `messaging` `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: payments: a successful charge writes its own charge ledger entry with the charge ID, stores the ID and queues its receipt; a fee-free job type's $0 entry is written at Confirm
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, payments F1, F3 and F5, second half, and the plan review's H2 and M2 (D-2623; FEE-013, FEE-028, FEE-030, FEE-031, FEE-042, FEE-045; D-1414, D-1419). After T352 (the charge ID on the adapter's `PaymentIntent`). A successful charge writes its attempt status and `payments.charge_evidence` (`write_evidence`, `app/payments/src/charge.rs:656`, from `effects`, `app/payments/src/handlers.rs:149`) but no `charge` ledger entry, since `record_fee_at_confirm` (`app/payments/src/service.rs:401`) has no caller. So a later job of the same customer is charged again (`free_wins::is_repeat` reads only ledger rows, FEE-013); the statement and money view show refunds with no charges (FEE-030); the reconcile would raise a High `payments.unknown_charge` alert for every charge; the evidence lacks the charge ID (FEE-042); and `queue_receipt` (`app/payments/src/receipts.rs:56`) has no caller, so no Laftly receipt is emailed (FEE-031). Also, for a fee-free job-type pick `waive_at_confirm` returns `NotWaived` and writes nothing (`app/payments/src/free_wins.rs:139`), so `no_fee_release` finds no $0 entry and the pick is never released (FEE-045). Fix: (1) the release proof's fresh fetch (`paid_release`, `app/payments/src/release_proof.rs:200`) requires a `ch_` `latest_charge` on a succeeded intent (missing: refused like any unreadable field, so Stripe's resend retries) and carries it to the success write; (2) in the transaction that writes the evidence (`migrations/0183_payments_charge_id.sql` adds a nullable `stripe_charge_id` to `payments.charge_evidence`, still append-only for the app role), the success path stores the charge ID, appends one `charge` ledger entry at the checked intent amount (`payments.pick_intent.amount_cents`; the press already refuses an intent whose amount differs from the stored `payments.pick_fee`, D-1871, so the two are equal whenever a fee row exists; if a fee row exists and differs, the entry still records the intent amount, the money Stripe took, so the ledger and statement stay true (FEE-028, `docs/spec/fees.md:32`; FEE-030, `:34`), and one High `payments.charge_fee_mismatch` alert names the pick (FEE-042: the stored fee stays in `payments.pick_fee` and the charged amount goes in `charge_evidence.amount_cents`; no new column, so `migrations/0183_payments_charge_id.sql` is not widened); a success with no fee row, as several DONE tests seed, writes the intent amount and no alert, D-3658) under a key derived from the pick, not from (job, business), so a second paid pick of the same business on the same job after a refund keeps its own entry; the reconcile's own-intent charge key (`key_and_id`, `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:534` once T334 is on `main`) uses the same per-pick key, so it converges instead of doubling or hiding a charge; and it calls `queue_receipt` when the evidence row was newly written; a replayed success writes nothing more; (3) `waive_at_confirm` writes the `fee-free-job-type` $0 entry (D-1419) when the pick's stored fee row says the pick is fee-free (FEE-045, fixed at the pick by T340), with no card and no `may_confirm` proof needed (FEE-036, BIZ-001), and answers so that `no_fee_release` clears it. (4) `is_repeat` (`app/payments/src/free_wins.rs:186`) counts a charge on another of the customer's jobs only when that charge was an actual introduction (FEE-013): a charge whose pick was refunded before any release, a late success auto-refunded with nothing released (T332's trigger) or an unreleased fraud-warning refund (`fraud-warning`), is not counted; refunds after a release (unreachable, no-show) still count; (5) `record_fee_at_confirm` (`app/payments/src/service.rs:401`, its key over job and business at `:428`) stays as it is and unused in production: the success path writes the charge entry and `waive_at_confirm` the $0 ones, and four done tests call it (`fee_mode_switch.rs`, `ledger_1000_jobs.rs`, `fee_at_pick.rs`, `fee_fixed_at_pick.rs`), so its doc comment says it is not the production writer and must not be called for a charge, whose key is per pick (D-2623). T261's Confirm route keeps calling `waive_at_confirm` then `no_fee_release` and needs no change. A success is usually recorded first by the synchronous confirm (`record` at `charge.rs:232`) or the check round (`:640`), and `handlers::record` returns early on a repeat (`may_become`, `handlers.rs:120`), so the webhook's `paid_release` (`release_proof.rs:347`) never runs the effects again: all three success writers carry the intent's `latest_charge` into `record` and `effects`, which write the ID, the ledger entry and the receipt for whichever records the success first; a writer holding a succeeded intent with no `ch_` ID leaves the attempt undecided, as an unreadable answer does, so a later fetch records it (D-3134). T340 is on `main` before this task, so any non-emergency job its own tests pick records its facts row first (`jobs::api::record_job_facts`, D-3118). Tests in `tests/integration/tests/charge_ledger_entry.rs` (TD-FEE-64), each failing on today's `main`: a success recorded by the confirm, by the check round and by the webhook each leave the `ch_` ID, one ledger entry and one receipt task; a stand-in success webhook leaves exactly one `charge` row with the `ch_` ID and the stored cents, the evidence row holds the same ID, and one `payments.receipt` task is queued; the replay adds nothing; a succeeded intent with no `ch_` ID releases nothing; `business_statement` totals equal the charges; after a released, paid pick a pick of the same business on another job of the same customer is waived as `Repeat`; after a late success auto-refunded with nothing released, or an unreleased pick refunded for a fraud warning, the next job is not waived; a charge, its full refund, a re-pick of the same business on the same job and a second charge leave two `charge` rows, and a reconcile over both appends nothing and raises no `payments.unknown_charge`; a fee-free job-type pick of a business with no saved card gets its `fee-free-job-type` entry from `waive_at_confirm` and `no_fee_release` clears it. Money: 95% branch floor; the overseer runs an independent money review of the hand-in. Update the `payments` `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md`. Plan change D-3658 (plan gap reported on attempt 1; TD-FEE-64, TD-FEE-52, TD-PICK-49, TD-PICK-50): two DONE tests pin "no charge entry" after a success this task now records, so this task becomes a harness task and also owns them, changing only that expectation: (a) `tests/integration/tests/payment_jobs.rs` (T433) `td_fee_52_check_round_stop_after_stripe_charges_once` (about :584) counts every ledger row and expects 0 after the check round records the success; it becomes exactly one row, of kind `charge`, the intent's 7500 cents (the `charged()` fixture's $75 intent, which seeds no `payments.pick_fee` row), under this task's per-pick key, which is what TD-FEE-52 means by "no second charge, refund or ledger row" (no refund row stays asserted as today); and before the restart, beside "stopped before the write", it also asserts 0 ledger rows, which shows the entry is written in the same transaction as the evidence; (b) `app/server/tests/release_recovery.rs` (T254) `no_fee_written` (about :408) expects `money_view(...).charges == 0`, but both callers (`td_pick_50_a_verified_success_settles_paid_and_releases_once`, `td_pick_49_a_failed_vault_read_recovers_and_shows_once`) first charge $25 through `paid()` and TD-PICK-49 asks for "one charge and no second fee"; it becomes `one_charge_no_second_fee(pool, pick)`, expecting `charges == 2500` (the $25 `paid()` charges, its stored fee and intent amount alike) and exactly one `charge` ledger row for the pick, so the release and every repeated delivery still write no fee of their own; its two call sites (about :556 and :749) pass the pick, and the doc comments change to match: the helper's "The ledger holds no charge: the release writes no fee (FEE-032)" TD-PICK-50's test comment (about :534) "... and no fee" and TD-PICK-49's (about :721) "one charge, no fee" become "one charge and no second fee". No other assertion, case or helper changes, and no zero-fee path is touched (the zero-fee and cancelled-pick cases never call that helper and keep expecting no charge).

tasks.title: jobs and server: every dead-lettered task alerts, and a daily backstop revives job timers that died so no job is stuck
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review batch 2, jobs F2 (D-2640; JOB-003, JOB-006, OPS-004, PRIV-007): a job timer that runs out of attempts leaves its job stuck for good, with no alert and its contact never purged. `fail` (`app/core/src/tasks.rs:262`) dead-letters after `DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (5, about 7.5 minutes of backoff) and `reap_expired` (`:318`) on a last-attempt lease expiry; `run_timer` (`app/jobs/src/service.rs:236`) turns every error into a retry; the dedupe key `jobs.timeout.<job>.<version>.<timer>` (`:226`) stays on the dead row, so the timer can never be queued again; a job left in Quotes ready never closes, and `sweep_closed` never purges it; `jobs.homeowner_text` and `jobs.check_in` dead letters drop silently; T327 alerts only on `NO_HANDLER` dead letters. Fix: (1) after T327, its dead-letter alert (`app/server/src/no_handler_alert.rs`) covers every dead-lettered task: one High alert per kind and day with the kind and count, no payload; (2) `app/jobs/src/timer_backstop.rs`: a daily `jobs.timer_backstop` task (registered in the shared worker, queued once a day) finds each non-final job whose current timer task is dead-lettered or missing and revives it (clears `dead_at`, resets attempts, `run_at` now, in one statement on that row, or re-queues under a revival counter in the key), at most a bounded batch per run, with one `ops` audit row of IDs per revival; a timer that dies 3 times raises a High alert and is left for Casey. The per-kind dead-letter count (1) and the one-row revive (2) are new public functions in the shared `app/core/src/api.rs`, next to T327's `dead_without_handler` (`:46`), because `jobs` and `server` may name no other module's schema, `core.` included, in SQL (`tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs:44`, `:250`); `app/core/src/tasks.rs` is not needed and stays unchanged (D-3094). Tests in `tests/integration/tests/timer_backstop.rs` (TD-OPS-38), clock advanced: `run_timer` failing 5 times on a Quotes ready job dead-letters it and raises one alert; the backstop revives it; with the fault gone the job reaches Closed and its purge stages are queued; a final job's dead timer is not revived; TD-OPS-36 and TD-OPS-37 pass unchanged. Update the `jobs` and `server` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: jobs, messaging, privacy, intake and payments: the daily sweeps queue tomorrow's run first, alert when a run dies, read only what is due, and use the worker's clock
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review batch 2, jobs F3 and F4 (D-2641; PRIV-007 to PRIV-009, TXT-020; D-1799, D-737, D-491, SEC-035). (1) The daily purge sweep stops for good after one dead-lettered run, with no alert: `run_sweep` (`app/jobs/src/purge_events.rs:97`) calls `sweep_closed` first and `schedule_sweep` after, so a run that fails 5 times never queues tomorrow's; its registration (`register_purge_handlers` in `app/server/src/lib.rs`) has no `alert_if_last`; and each run reloads every final job ever with three inserts per job inside the 120-second handler limit, so it eventually always times out. The same order is in `messaging::retention::run_cut` (`app/messaging/src/retention.rs:189`) and `app/messaging/src/purge.rs:139`. Each now queues tomorrow's run first (as `offdb_stream::schedule_verify` does, D-737), is registered with `alert_if_last` (shared `app/server/src/lib.rs`), and reads only final jobs with a purge stage not yet queued, in bounded pages. (2) Those sweeps read the wall clock, not the worker's injected clock: `purge_events.rs:100`, `retention.rs:192`, `app/privacy/src/handlers.rs:53`, `:88`, `:137`, `app/intake/src/purge.rs:284`, `:327`, `:347`, `app/payments/src/purge.rs:66` and the pause kind's registration. Each `(pool, task)` handler (`run_sweep`, `run_cut`, `run_request_sweep`, `run_purge`, `run_request_purge`, `run_purge_due`, `run_purge_due_after`, `run_complaint_hold`, `run_dispute_holds`) keeps its signature and behaviour, because done tests call them directly with `(pool, task)` (`tests/integration/tests/retention_purge.rs`, T094's, `:218` to `:516`) and register `run_purge` and `run_request_purge` as plain handlers (`tests/integration/tests/retention_purge_races.rs` `:146`, `:147`, `:509`, `:510`); each gains a twin taking the instant (`now`), which the plain one calls with the wall clock, and a clock-taking builder (`register_*(registry, clock)`, as `register_body_deletes` and `register_photo_deletes` take the clock, SEC-035) that `worker_registry`'s purge registrations in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` call instead of registering the plain handlers (plan change D-3106). Tests in `tests/integration/tests/purge_sweeps.rs` (TD-PRIV-25): a sweep handler that fails every attempt still leaves the next day's sweep row and raises one `privacy.purge_failed` alert; a run over 5,000 final jobs with stages already queued reads none of them again; with a `ManualClock` advanced 31 days in a worker run the stages are queued (fails today: the wall clock is read). Every TD-PRIV and TD-TXT purge case passes unchanged. Update the `jobs`, `messaging`, `privacy`, `intake` and `payments` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: businesses (harness): the capability checklist offers every job type the business's licenses or handyman standing allow, and follows the stored category switch
tasks.goal: Nov 11 code review batch 3, F1 and F5 (D-2701; BIZ-049, BIZ-004, BIZ-021, LIC-002, LIC-012, LIC-014, LIC-015, LIC-016, LIC-019, LIC-027, LIC-046, LIC-047). Tests in `tests/integration/tests/capability_offer.rs` (TD-BIZ-46, TD-LIC-27), each failing on today's `main`: a septage hauler, a certified inspector and a pest attester (general pest service and scorpions; termites only with the wood-destroying organism record category) get their job types pre-ticked and `save_capability` stores them; a city-list handyman gets faucet replacement and camera install unticked, never gas line work or a gas pool heater, and saving them stores them; an R-37 business's offer is unchanged; an R-11 business is not offered the handyman category; a city-list business with no license gets no pre-ticked row; a category switched off through `catalog::api::set_category_enabled` leaves `category_list`, the checklist and `reapply_license`'s offer, and switching it on brings it back.
