tasks.title: Performance: database pool and query measurements (PERF-004) and the national-size ZIP lookup measurement
tasks.goal: Performance track (D-3292, from Casey's performance review `docs/audit/performance-review-2026-11-12.md`), part 1: the database measurements the route benchmark (T417) and the war games (T234, T297) read, metrics only (PERF-004), and the national-size ZIP lookup measurement (PERF-003, measure only, no fix). Nothing here changes how a request behaves. (1) `app/core/src/db_metrics.rs`: a `tracing_subscriber` layer that keeps only numbers from sqlx 0.9's own events: each executed statement (target `sqlx::query`, turned on by `log_statements` on the app pool's connect options) adds one to a statement counter, and each pool acquire (target `sqlx::pool::acquire`, its `acquired_after_secs` field, turned on by `acquire_time_level`; count both of sqlx's acquire events, since an acquire over `acquire_slow_threshold` emits only the "exceeded slow threshold" event and not the ordinary one) adds to an acquire count, a wait sum, a wait maximum and fixed log-scale wait buckets from 0.1 ms to 5 s, so a reader can take a nearest-rank p95 from two snapshots' bucket differences. The layer never reads, stores or logs the SQL text, a bind value, the database URL or any field other than those numbers (SEC-001, PRIV-016); no `sqlx::query` event of any level reaches the JSON log layer: sqlx logs a slow statement at WARN by default with the full SQL text in `db.statement`, and the JSON layer passes INFO today, so the JSON layer's own per-layer filter drops the whole `sqlx::query` target and the metrics layer gets a separate per-layer filter (a global filter would hide the events from it too); per-acquire events stay out of the JSON layer as well. A slow acquire over 250 ms (`acquire_slow_threshold`) logs one WARN line through the existing JSON layer holding only the wait seconds. (2) `app/core/src/db.rs` `app_pool` turns those on and registers the pool so a snapshot can read its size, idle count and maximum (`PgPool::size`, `num_idle`); `max_connections`, `ASKHAVA_DB_POOL_MAX` and `ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` stay exactly as they are (no pool-size change). `app/core/src/logging.rs` installs the layer; `app/core/src/lib.rs` declares the module. (3) `GET /__test/perf/db` on the test-control router (`app/core/src/test_control.rs`, under the same feature, environment and bearer-secret rules as its other routes and the same 404 without them, SEC-035) is added inside `routes()` under the existing bearer `route_layer` (never beside it) and answers a JSON snapshot: statements, acquires, wait sum, maximum and bucket counts in microseconds, pool size, idle and maximum, and `"acquire_timeouts": "not exposed"` (sqlx emits no event for a timed-out acquire; the benchmark's error rate covers it). A caller takes two snapshots and subtracts; with one request in flight the statement difference is that request's queries. Its tests are `tests/security/tests/perf_db_route.rs`, in `control_router_absent.rs`'s early-return pattern so both builds pass: in the default build (what `Ci` runs) `/__test/perf/db` is 404 under every `APP_ENV`, even with the bearer; with the feature (`cargo test -p askhava-security --test perf_db_route --features askhava-core/test-control`, run in the session under "Run your tests") it answers the snapshot with the bearer, 404 without it, and the router refuses `test` and `live`. The default-build case proves in `Ci` that the release build has no such route; the feature-on cases run in `Ci` once T418 adds its E2e step for them (`ci.yml` is T418's), and T417 and T418's benchmark exercises the route end to end. (4) `tests/integration/tests/db_metrics.rs` against the CI Postgres: a known handful of statements moves the counter by exactly that many; with a pool of 1 and a held connection a second acquire's wait lands in the right bucket and the maximum; a slow-acquire WARN line and every log line written during the test hold no SQL text, no URL and no planted fake value (TD-OPS-41). (5) `tests/integration/tests/perf_zip_scale.rs` (PERF-003): builds a synthetic national-size markets file that passes `askhava_catalog::api::parse_markets` (the `markets` module is private) (about 41,000 ZIP codes over about 30,000 towns, made-up codes and town names) and times `town_for_zip` for the first, middle and last ZIP and an unknown one over a fixed number of calls, printing one JSON line with p50 and p95 per lookup in microseconds; it fails only when a lookup returns the wrong town or a town for the unknown ZIP, never on time (the targets are goals, D-3292), and is `#[ignore]` so `Ci` stays fast (T417 runs it). Update the `core` `CLAUDE.md`, the performance-measurement note in `docs/architecture.md` (found by grep for D-3292, never loaded whole) and `docs/decisions.md`. A harness task so the measurement layer is reviewed by Opus before anything is tuned from it.

Fake data only (BUILD_BRIEF.md:66, PRIV-019): names from a fixed fake list, phones 555-0100 to 555-0199, emails at `example.com`, streets such as "1 Test Way"; `scripts/pii_scan.py` scans `perf/` and `docs/audit/`. (1) `perf/seed.py` seeds, against the CI Postgres (`DATABASE_URL`, after `server migrate`), a deterministic Phoenix-metro-size background in one transaction: about 1,500 businesses across the open trades and the catalog's towns, 20,000 past jobs, 50,000 quotes and their picks (the exact counts are constants the report prints). tasks.title: calls (harness): TD-CALL-23's no-plaintext scan reads only text columns, so a digest or uuid never matches a 4-digit needle by chance
tasks.goal: Flaky test (D-3324; CALL-011, CALL-003, PRIV-002; D-2540, D-3049, BUILD_BRIEF.md:272): `td_call_23_a_blocked_call_that_connects_queues_one_notice_and_one_pending_link` in `tests/integration/tests/link_request.rs` (T390, DONE) failed on docs-only PR #621 (job 131511326334) at line 324, "calls.link_request_digest holds a value", left 1, right 0. Cause: `rows_holding` (line 217) counts rows whose whole row text (`t::text LIKE '%' || needle || '%'`) holds the needle, and two of the three needles are 4-digit runs (the blocked number's last 4 digits and the line's random 4-digit PIN), so a row's random uuid or bytea hex (`\\x` plus 64 hex digits) holds one by chance: about 78 four-character hex windows per digest row, two needles, (1/16)^4 each, about 1 run in 420 for the digest table alone and about 1 in 620 for `calls.link_request` (three uuids; a PIN of 2026 also matches its timestamps). No production code changes; nothing is weakened. (1) Make the plaintext-absence check deterministic: scan only the text-typed columns (text, varchar, char, json, jsonb, read from `information_schema.columns` or `pg_attribute`, or listed by name) of each scanned table and of the `core.task` subquery, so a uuid, bytea, timestamp or number column can no longer match by chance; a scanned table or subquery with no text column counts 0 for the text scan. (2) The digest table must still be proven to hold no plaintext: assert that no text column of `calls.link_request_digest` holds any needle, that every stored `digest` differs from each needle's own bytes (and from the needle's bytes zero-padded to 32), and keep the existing count of 1 digest row. (3) Every other assertion of the file stays exactly as it is (the notice payload, the pending link's times, the counts, the log-line scan, the `core.task` checks for the full number, every other TD-CALL-23 case). (4) Add a deterministic regression test in the same file: insert by hand (fake data only) a `calls.link_request` row and a `calls.link_request_digest` row whose 32 digest bytes are chosen so the row's hex text contains a 4-digit needle (for example bytes 0x01 0x87 for `0187`), assert that the old whole-row scan would count it (so the case really reproduces the flake) and that the new check counts 0 and passes. A harness task because it changes T390's finished test file, which is protected. Claimed first (`kit/runner.json` `claim_first`, D-2540, D-3049). Update `docs/decisions.md` with what changed and why.
tasks.acceptance: `cargo test -p askhava-integration --test link_request` passes; the plaintext-absence check scans only text-typed columns; the digest table is proven to hold no needle in a text column and no digest equal to a needle's bytes; the new regression case, a digest whose hex holds a 4-digit needle, fails under the old whole-row scan and passes under the new check; every other assertion in the file is unchanged; no file outside `tests/integration/tests/link_request.rs` changes except `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: --after refuses a hand-in whose head no Opus reviewer approved or whose commits no worker made
tasks.goal: Enforce the re-review of fix rounds (D-3475; D-584, D-1328, D-2506, D-3444; BUILD_BRIEF.md:250): `--after` (`runner/__main__.py` `after`, `runner/github_env.py` `collect_result`) records the hand-in head as `reviewed_sha` whatever ran last; it checks only that the reviewer transcripts ran on the reviewer model (`cycle.py` line 501). Before D-3444, 3 of 4 sampled fix rounds merged with no reviewer run after the fix commit (T249, T372, T423), and in T423 the Sonnet main session committed itself. Evidence available at `--after`: the worker and reviewer subagent transcripts (`find_transcripts`, `~/.claude/projects/*/*/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`), whose lines hold the model, the assistant text and each tool result's text; git on the runner's checkout; the hand-off file. The reviewer today states no verdict and no head, so: (1) `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml` step 4 (and 4c, 5b and 3c, which re-run it): the reviewer runs `git rev-parse HEAD` itself on the task branch before reading the diff and ends its report with exactly one line `REVIEW-VERDICT: APPROVED <40-hex head>` or `REVIEW-VERDICT: FINDINGS`; every worker and fix-round worker commits with plain `git commit` (no `-q`, output not filtered or redirected), so Git's `[<branch> <abbrev>]` line reaches its transcript; after any fix commit, including a worker redoing a commit after a (b) hold, the session runs a NEW reviewer that must approve the new head over the new head and passes every reviewer agent id to step 5. (2) New `runner/review_proof.py` (standard library; called from `collect_result` for outcome `submitted`, on the worker's head BEFORE `_hand_in_in_order`'s runner commit and the pre-hand-in gate). Rule (a), approval of the head: when the task has a reviewer (`cycle.reviewer_model`), some reviewer transcript must, counting only `subagents/agent-*.jsonl` paths from `--reviewer-agent`, never one also given by `--worker-agent` and never one holding a `[<branch> <abbrev>]` commit line (a reviewer that committed is no reviewer), in an assistant text block (never a tool result or a quoted prompt), have as its LAST verdict line `REVIEW-VERDICT: APPROVED H` with H the full hand-in head, must hold a tool result containing H (its own `git rev-parse`), and its own models must pass the same rule as `cycle._review_problems` (`runner/cycle.py:500-505`: `reviewer_model(task)` with `known_models`), so a D-2225 model-window or fallback reviewer passes; an approval of any earlier commit, a `FINDINGS` last verdict, or a verdict only in another role's transcript does not count. Since the approval names the exact head, any commit after the last reviewed one fails (a). Rule (b), who committed: for each commit in `git rev-list H ^<main base> ^<branch start>` (branch start: new hand-off field `branch_start`, the prepared branch's existing `base_sha` from `_prepare`, the local task branch tip at the claim; when it is missing, because `prepare_branch` returned `{}` (`runner/github_env.py:1966`, dry run or a git failure), (b) is skipped with a log line naming why (no `remote_at_start` fallback: it would judge the runner's own prepared merge); so the runner's own prepared merge and earlier attempts' commits are not judged), a non-merge commit needs a worker transcript (passed via `--worker-agent`, a `subagents/` path) whose tool result holds Git's commit summary line naming it (`[<branch> <abbrev>]`, abbrev at least 7 hex and a unique prefix of the full SHA); a merge commit passes when its second parent is on `origin/main` and its tree equals `git merge-tree --write-tree` of its parents (a clean, unedited merge adds no authored content), else it needs the same line. Commits made by the main session itself leave no line in any worker transcript, so they fail; this is the closest checkable rule: the evidence proves a worker subagent's tool ran the commit, not who asked for it, and transcripts are files on the runner's disk with the same trust as D-1328's model evidence. (3) Refusal: each rule may hold the hand-in once (`prehandin_holds` style, separate hand-off counters `review_holds_a` and `review_holds_b`, each at most 1), printing `runner: review_missing` with the unapproved or unproven commits, so the session runs a new reviewer (or has a worker redo the commit, after which a fresh reviewer must approve the new head, as the workflow text says) and `--after` again; a rule failing again after its hold fails the attempt as `tests_failed` with a log naming each commit (short SHA, subject) and the rule, nothing pushed, as any failed hand-in. A task without a reviewer skips (a) only. `collect_result`'s new parameter defaults to no check, so existing callers and tests keep their behaviour; `after()` always passes it. Failure drills and tests (new `tests/test_runner_review_proof.py`; no existing test changes, every existing runner test passes): T249's shape (fix commit after the approval) refused; T423's shape (a commit whose summary line is only in the main session's transcript) refused; approval of an earlier SHA refused; `FINDINGS` after an `APPROVED` refused; a verdict quoted in a tool result or in the worker's transcript ignored; a reviewer transcript on a non-reviewer model refused and a model-window or fallback reviewer accepted; a reviewer path also given as `--worker-agent` ignored; a reviewer transcript holding a commit line ignored; an approval without its `rev-parse` tool result refused; a clean main merge accepted and an edited merge without a summary line refused; an ambiguous or 6-hex abbrev refused; the decisions reorder commit and the runner's prepared merge not judged; no `base_sha` skipping (b) with its log line; (a) and (b) each holding once on their own counter, then `tests_failed`; the happy path (worker commit, fix commit, new reviewer approving the head) accepted and `reviewed_sha` set; the workflow step text. Update `docs/decisions.md` and add one bullet to the "Keeping this file true" list of `docs/architecture.md` (`grep -n 'Keeping this file true' docs/architecture.md`; read only the bullets near yours, never the list whole; D-3620).

tasks.title: runner (harness): a failed nightly on an older head keeps the stages the last green nightly proved, and a re-staged task's stage follows kit/tasks.json
tasks.goal: Runner robustness (D-3563 (e); D-486, D-1126, D-3499, D-3531). (1) On November 13 a one-in-a-hundred property-test miss failed `named-mutants` on nightly-main; a failed `kit/nightly.json` makes `scripts/stage_exit.py` `_nightly_problems` fail every stage, so `passed_stages` (called by `runner/__main__.py` `build`'s `gate`) is empty and no task is claimed until a green nightly, about 2 hours, even after main had moved on and was green; `main_red` already ignores a failed nightly on an older head (`runner/cycle.py` `_nightly_red_on_head`, about line 1264). Make the gate do the same: `.github/workflows/nightly-main.yml`'s `record` step also writes `last_green` (`{"sha", "ran_at"}`): this run's when it is green, else the `last_green` of the `kit/nightly.json` it replaces (absent when there is none), and `failures_since_green`: 0 on a green run, else the replaced file's value plus 1 (1 when the replaced file has none or there is none); every other key and the commit line stay as they are. A new pure `stage_exit.gate_nightly(nightly, main_head, is_ancestor)` returns the record unchanged unless its `conclusion` is `failure`, its `sha` is not `main_head` and is an ancestor of it (`is_ancestor` answers `True`), it carries a `last_green` with a `sha`, and its `failures_since_green` is exactly 1 (the first failure since the last green run; the nightly runs about once a day while `main` moves all day, so almost every failure is on an older head, and a second failure in a row is no longer chance: the gate closes); then it returns `{"conclusion": "success", "sha": <last_green sha>}`, so a stage whose merges that green run contained stays passed and a stage that needs a newer merge waits for a newer green nightly. `gate` passes `gate_nightly(env.read_nightly(), env.main_head(), git_is_ancestor(ROOT))` to `passed_stages`; `evaluate`, `passed_stages`, the command line, `runner/proof.py`'s stage proofs and `main_red` read the raw record as today. A failed nightly on main's current head always closes every stage (and sets `main_red` as today), whatever the counter says, and so does any second or later failure in a row. (2) `runner/state.py` `sync_graph` (about line 99) copies a changed `stage` onto every entry not DONE or SKIPPED, as it does `deps` (D-1126), so a plan change that re-stages a queued task takes effect (the parked D-3498 re-stage of T111 and T121 needs it). (A worker stop opening `MAIN RED:` that the runner confirms is left out: it would add `runner/cycle.py`.) Tests first, in the new `tests/test_runner_stage_robustness.py`: `gate_nightly` returns the last green record for a failure on an older head, the raw failure on main's head, on a SHA that is not an ancestor or when `is_ancestor` answers `None`, and with no `last_green`, and when `failures_since_green` is missing or 2 or more; two consecutive failed nightlies on older heads close every stage (`passed_stages` over `gate_nightly`'s answer is empty for a stage the last green run had passed); a success passes unchanged; `passed_stages` over the substituted record keeps a stage whose merges the last green SHA contains and closes one whose merge it does not; the `record` step's Python (read from the workflow file and run on fake records) keeps `last_green` across a failure and moves it on a success, and counts `failures_since_green` up across failures and back to 0 on a success; `sync_graph` moves a QUEUED entry's stage and leaves a DONE entry's. (3) Plan change D-3619 (a stale-graph claim): on November 14 a run whose own checkout's `kit/tasks.json` predated main's (before #730 added T302's dependency T450) smoked main's head and claimed T302 from its older graph. Before any claim, `build` (`runner/__main__.py`) compares the run's `kit/tasks.json` with the one at the `origin/main` head it just fetched (`git show <head>:kit/tasks.json`); when they differ it reloads the whole parsed kit from main's file before claiming (the graph, the stage gate, the pacer's task list, `models`, `protected_paths`, `shared_paths` and the `plan_health` checker, everything `build` reads from `kit/tasks.json`), and when main's file cannot be read it claims nothing this cycle and logs why. A merge to main between that fetch and the claim can still slip through; that narrow race is accepted (the next cycle reloads, and the claim's own smoke and checks run on main's head). Tests (in the same new file): a checkout graph without a dependency that main's graph has never claims the task whose dependency is not DONE; a protected or shared path or a model that differs on main is the one the claim uses. Every existing test passes unchanged.
tasks.acceptance: `tests/test_runner_stage_robustness.py` holds every listed case and passes; `python3 scripts/stage_exit.py --stage N` and every existing test (including `tests/test_stage_exit.py`, `tests/test_failure_drills.py`, `tests/test_runner_proof.py`) pass unchanged; the nightly `record` step writes `last_green` and `failures_since_green` and nothing else new; only the first failure since the last green run, on an older head, is replaced; a failed nightly on main's current head, or two failed nightlies in a row on older heads, leaves `passed_stages` empty.

tasks.goal: Plan change D-3674 (T300 plan gap; A11Y-002, SEC-004, PRIV-002; D-1311, D-1516, D-1788, D-2029): the suite's web binary (`tests/e2e/webserver.ts`, `appEnv`, :52 to :70) runs in `ci` with no Twilio settings and no vault keys, so `app/server/src/business_signin.rs:129` falls back to `NoVerify` and `vault_from` (`app/server/src/lib.rs:321`) gives no vault: no page that sends a Verify code, reads the vault or seals a contact can run in a browser. Giving the suite's own binaries the keys is not safe: `tests/a11y/j1_keyboard.spec.ts` and `tests/e2e/j1_reduced.spec.ts` rely on it serving no page pick (D-1516), and a worker holding vault keys would run the outbox sender over rows that `tests/e2e/j1_homeowner.spec.ts`'s own binary sealed under other keys. So, as `j1_homeowner.spec.ts` does for itself (D-2029): (1) `tests/e2e/webserver.ts`'s setup also starts a second web binary (no second worker), the keyed binary, from the same build on `webPort() + 19`, with the suite's environment plus fake values made at run time: `ASKHAVA_TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` (`AC` and 32 zeros, the stand-in's account), `ASKHAVA_TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ASKHAVA_TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID`, `ASKHAVA_TWILIO_VERIFY_BASE_URL` on the stand-in, `ASKHAVA_MASKED_POOL_SIZE` 1 and `ASKHAVA_MASKED_NUMBERS` (`TwilioConfig::from_settings` needs the pool, `app/adapters/src/config.rs:230`), its own `ASKHAVA_ID_SECRET`, and `VAULT_KEY` and `VAULT_INDEX_KEY` (`1:` and the base64 of 32 random bytes); the same test-control secret and clock file as the suite's binaries; no `ASKHAVA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, so it serves no webhook. The setup waits for it like the first binary and the teardown stops it. The suite's own web binary and worker keep exactly the environment they have. The keyed values reach the test processes the way `controlSecret()` does (set in the Playwright main process's environment before the workers start), under names that do not start with `ASKHAVA_`, so `appEnv` never passes them on. (2) A new `tests/e2e/keyed.ts` exports the keyed binary's base URL and ID secret, and `seal(table, column, id, plain)` and `blindIndex(purpose, value)` in the vault's own formats (`app/privacy/src/vault.rs`: AES-256-GCM under the run's `VAULT_KEY` version 1 with a random 96-bit nonce, stored as the 2-byte big-endian version, the nonce, then the ciphertext with its tag, associated data `<table>|<column>|<id>|v1`; the index HMAC-SHA256 under the key HMAC(`VAULT_INDEX_KEY`, `<purpose>|v1`)), with node's `crypto` only. (3) `tests/a11y/fixtures.ts`: a seed may return `{ url, cookies }` instead of a path: an absolute URL on the keyed binary or a path, and cookies (name and value) that `open` adds to the page's context for that URL's origin (`Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, host-only, path `/`, as a `__Host-` cookie needs) before `page.goto`; `PageEntry.seed`'s type in the shared `tests/a11y/page_states.ts` widens to match and every existing entry stays as it is; `open` keeps its 200 check and its token masking. `NOT_PAGES` gains `/b/billing/statement.csv` (T300's CSV statement, a download checked through `/b/billing`). No other check, tag, width, state or route rule changes. (4) `tests/e2e/keyed_server.spec.ts` proves it: a fake active business whose owner has a texting staff phone (555-01xx) sealed with `seal` into `privacy.staff_phone` (`privacy.staff_phone|number|<line>|v1`, `migrations/0188_privacy_business_contacts.sql`) and a `portals.login_link` row for a token the spec chose, seeded through `psql` on `DATABASE_URL` as `tests/e2e/j1_reduced.spec.ts` seeds; opening `/b/sign-in/{token}` on the keyed binary and pressing Sign in sends a Verify code to that phone (the stand-in's `/_stand_in/twilio/code?to=` hook answers for it) and typing it signs the browser in; and a cookie a seed returns reaches the keyed binary on the next request (read from that request's `Cookie` header). tasks.title: portals, businesses and messaging: public paths for sign-up's email code and its sign-in link at activation
tasks.goal: Plan change D-3743 (the T461 plan gap a scout found; BIZ-040, SEC-004, SEC-018, SEC-025, SEC-026, PRIV-016; D-1725, D-1837, D-3186, D-3262, D-3676): T461 must email the sign-up's email code (BIZ-040: verified "by a single-use link or 6-digit code sent to it") and, on activation, the owner's normal sign-in link, but neither has a public path. A link is minted, stored and emailed only inside `portals` (`send_one` is private, `app/portals/src/business_auth.rs:694`; `models::new_link_token` and `admit_link` are `pub(crate)`, `app/portals/src/models.rs:28`, `:71`), and `SignInMail::send_link` (`business_auth.rs:138`) only emails a link it is handed. `start_signup_check` returns the code and emails nothing (`app/businesses/src/email_verification.rs:134`), `businesses::api` has no reader for the sign-up's mailbox ID, which `confirm_mailbox` (`:363`) needs, and nothing in the app emails a mailbox code. This task adds three thin public paths over code that exists; T461 composes them. (1) `app/portals/src/business_auth.rs`: `pub async fn send_sign_in_link<M: SignInMail>(db, mail: &M, to: SignInAddress, now) -> Result<(), PortalsError>` (one `pub use` line in the shared `app/portals/src/api.rs`). The body of `send_one` moves into a private function that takes the mailer instead of the `SignIn` state; `send_one` and the new function both call it, the new one with no next job: the same current-member check (nothing sent for a mailbox that is not a current member of `to.business`), the same `LINKS_PER_LIFE` cap under the member's lock (`admit_link`, D-1725, D-1837) and the same `{site()}/b/sign-in/<token>` link through `M::send_link`; its `///` comment says that `M` delivers the link only to `to.mailbox`'s own address, never to another (SEC-004). No other behaviour of `business_auth.rs` changes. (2) `app/businesses/src/email_verification.rs`: `pub async fn signup_mailbox(conn, business) -> Result<Uuid, EmailCheckError>` (one name in the shared `app/businesses/src/api.rs` export), the `businesses.signup` row's `mailbox_id` as `start_signup_check` reads it, `EmailCheckError::Database` for an unknown sign-up; `start_signup_check` and `confirm` keep their signatures. (3) `app/messaging/src/mailbox_code_mail.rs`: `MailboxCodeSender<E>`, built as T280's `SignInLinkSender` is (`app/messaging/src/signin_mail.rs`: the key secret, the provider, the checked postal line and the `DailyLimit`), whose `send(db, (mailbox, address), code, now)` queues one business email through `queue_account_email` from a new template `business_mailbox_code` (English, and Spanish marked draft, in the shared `app/messaging/templates/en.json` and `es.json`: the subject "<brand short name>: Your email code", the 6-digit code, that it works for the next 30 minutes (`CODE_LIFE`), and that a person who did not sign up can ignore it) and sends it at once with `send_email`. The code is a credential, so the stored row holds `CODE_MARK` (`[email code]`) in its place and the code goes in only on the way to the provider, through a wrapper like `signin_mail.rs`' `WithLink`; the row's key is the account-email key over the template, the mailbox and one ID keyed from the code and the send time (a repeat of one send is one email, SEC-018; a resend is a new one); the code is never logged. The sender counts nothing itself: its `///` comment says the caller admits every send first under SEC-014's per-IP and per-business limits (T461 does, where the client IP is known). `MailboxCodeSender`, `CODE_MARK` and the template ID are exported through the shared `app/messaging/src/api.rs` and `lib.rs`. The caller opens the address (`server`, under `privacy::api::BusinessPurpose::AccountEmail`, on a bare connection), as T280's sender is handed it; this task names no vault read. Tests, fake data only, in `tests/integration/tests/signup_mail_paths.rs` against PostgreSQL: `send_sign_in_link` stores one link for the owner and hands a recording `SignInMail` one `/b/sign-in/` link on the brand's site for that `SignInAddress`, sends nothing for a mailbox that is not a current member, and sends no more once `LINKS_PER_LIFE` links went in `LINK_LIFE`; `signup_mailbox` answers the mailbox `sign_up` stored and refuses an unknown business; `MailboxCodeSender::send` gives a recording `EmailAdapter` one email to the address whose text and HTML hold the code, a refusing provider leaves the stored row holding `CODE_MARK` and never the code, and a repeat of the same send queues and sends nothing more. tasks.title: harness: clearing a red main counts a failed attempt against the blamed task only when FIX-MAIN actually reverted its files
tasks.goal: Red `main` clearing blames only a real revert (plan change D-3752; docs/governance.md section 5.3 and 5.4; D-1099, D-551, D-584, D-3747). Today `runner/cycle.py` `clear_main_red`, once a green smoke on main's head (and a successful nightly for that head when kit/nightly.json is for it) clears `main_red`, always calls `record_failure` on `main_red.task`, the task `offending_merge` blamed only because it was the latest DONE merge, with the reason "reverted by FIX-MAIN (...)". On November 14 that moved T437 from DONE to BLOCKED (attempts 4), although FIX-MAIN #795 merged only its D-3747 entry (FIX-MAIN's `files` in kit/state.json: `docs/decisions.md` alone) and T437's merge c97c4d0fe stayed on `main`; the red came from T357 (D-3747), and the BLOCKED T437 held its dependents. Change, in `runner/cycle.py` only: (1) A pure helper `fix_main_reverted(red, fix, shared)` (under 50 lines, a docstring citing D-3752) says whether the merged FIX-MAIN changed the offending task's work back. `red` is `main_red`, whose `files` are the offending merge's files (`set_main_red`); `fix` is the FIX-MAIN entry, whose `files` are the merged FIX-MAIN pull request's changed files, recorded when it went DONE. FIX-MAIN merges are squashed, so its revert commit is never in `main`'s history and the squash message proves nothing (#795's message says "Revert T437 merge" though its tree reverted nothing): the merged files are the signal. The offending task's own paths are its `files` not under a shared path (`Config.shared`, a prefix entry such as `.sqlx/` covering what it contains, matched as `runner/verify.py` matches shared paths). Reverted: FIX-MAIN's `files` include one of those own paths, or the offending merge had no own path and FIX-MAIN's `files` include one of its files other than `docs/decisions.md` (append-only; every FIX-MAIN adds an entry). Not reverted: FIX-MAIN went DONE as an empty hand-in (`empty_handin`), or its `files` are known and none of them is such a path. Unknown, kept as today (reverted, the safe side): FIX-MAIN's `files` missing or empty without `empty_handin`. (2) `clear_main_red` stores `outcome` (`reverted` or `fixed_otherwise`) and `fix_files` (FIX-MAIN's merged files) on the record it appends to `main_red_history`, and calls `record_failure` with today's reason text only when the outcome is `reverted`; on `fixed_otherwise` the offending task keeps its status, attempts, `merged_sha` and `files`. Nothing else about a red `main` changes: the smoke and nightly checks, `revert_landed_red`, `blocked_fix_main`, `clear_false_red` and `offending_merge` stay as they are, and the state schema needs no change (`main_red_history` records are not constrained). Tests in the new `tests/test_runner_fix_main_clear.py`, driving `cycle.run_cycle` with a fake env as `tests/test_failure_drills.py` does: a FIX-MAIN that merged only `docs/decisions.md` clears `main` and leaves the DONE offending task DONE with its attempts and `merged_sha`, history outcome `fixed_otherwise` with `fix_files`; one whose files include an own path of the offending task re-queues it with attempts + 1 and the "reverted by FIX-MAIN" reason, outcome `reverted`; one at `MAX_ATTEMPTS` - 1 is BLOCKED only on a real revert; an overlap only in shared paths (`docs/architecture.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, a file under `.sqlx/`) is `fixed_otherwise`; an empty-hand-in FIX-MAIN is `fixed_otherwise`; a FIX-MAIN with no recorded files keeps today's outcome; and unit cases for `fix_main_reverted` itself, including an offending merge with shared paths only. Every existing test stays unchanged and passing, `tests/test_failure_drills.py`'s review-red drill among them (its FIX-MAIN pull request records no files, so it keeps today's outcome). Update the `docs/architecture.md` line on clearing a red `main` (found by grep, never loaded whole) and add your entry to `docs/decisions.md`. Runner logic: an Opus worker, an Opus review, and two review rounds (the second on the head the first round's fixes produce).
tasks.acceptance: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_runner_fix_main_clear.py` passes and the whole runner suite passes, every existing test unchanged; `fix_main_reverted` exists in `runner/cycle.py` under 50 lines; a cleared `main_red_history` record carries `outcome` and `fix_files`; `record_failure` runs on the offending task only for `reverted`; a FIX-MAIN that merged only `docs/decisions.md` leaves a DONE offending task DONE with unchanged attempts; no other runner file changes (D-3752).

tasks.title: Runner (harness): an ancestor's running smoke finishes and counts when main moves, instead of restarting
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4180 (Casey, Nov 17: "We can run more lanes if you are able"; the lanes stay at 7 and the idle time is attacked instead; evidence in D-4180): stop throwing away a valid smoke verdict when `main` moves mid-smoke. Today `settle_background_smoke` and `_background_smoke` (`runner/github_env.py:1370`-`1393`) stop this job's background smoke of an older head A as soon as `main` is at a new head, and the start routine smokes the new head from scratch (13 to 22 minutes each), so frequent merges keep lanes in `smoke_pending`. New rule, with no proof rule changed: when this job's own smoke is for an ancestor A of the head and A would be a valid D-3058/D-3156 ancestry-reuse base for the head once green, the smoke is kept, its verdict is recorded as a real run on A, and the head then claims through the unchanged ancestry reuse. (1) Qualifying, pure, in `runner/state.py` beside `ancestry_smoke` and sharing its per-commit loop rather than copying it: `ancestry_pending(state, chain, sha, merged, limit, proven) -> bool` is True only when `main` is not red, `limit` >= 1, `sha` is `chain[d]` for some 1 <= d <= `limit` (`chain` is `main_first_parents(head, limit + 1)`, starting at the head), `sha` passes `_clean_commit` (no `main_red_history` entry, no `smoke_env_problems` strike, no red or timed-out run), and every commit `chain[0:d]`, the head included, has no real run of its own, passes `_clean_commit` and is a DONE task's squash merge (`done_merges`) or `proven` returns exactly True for it (`green_twin_tree`, asked only after the cheaper tests): exactly the tests `ancestry_smoke` applies, so it would take `sha` as its base the moment a fresh real green is recorded on it. The cycle adds `_head_doubted` on every commit `chain[0:d+1]`, as `_ancestry_reuse` does; any error is False. (2) Env, `runner/github_env.py`: a reader of this job's own smoke whatever its SHA (the `job` check of `_pre_result` kept; the SHA check dropped only in this reader) giving its SHA, whether its background process still runs and its finished result (pre-session or background) if any; and a wait on a kept smoke of A that is `_await_background(A, pid)` itself (it sets `smoke_pending` while A runs, uses a result as `_use_pre_smoke` does, and is `_background_lost(A)` when A ended with no result, `runner/github_env.py:1423`-`1428`). `settle_background_smoke` and `_background_smoke` stay byte-for-byte unchanged: the cycle keeps A by returning before it calls them, so a lost-race retry in the same call (`runner/cycle.py:1713`) judges A afresh and can never reach the stop at `github_env.py:1390` through a keep flag left over from the first pass; nothing else in `smoke_main` changes. (3) Cycle, `runner/cycle.py` `_start_smoke`, before `settle_background_smoke`: when this job's own smoke is for A other than the head, there is no own result for the head, the head has neither a same-head reuse nor an ancestry reuse standing now (if it has one the ancestor smoke is stopped as today, `tests/test_runner_smoke_reuse.py:594`) and A qualifies under (1): (a) still running: wait as in (2); still running then is `smoke_pending` with nothing recorded, nothing claimed and no second smoke started (one smoke per smoke tree and database, `github_env.py:1386`-`1388`); (b) finished green: append a real run on A to `smoke_runs` (`sha` A, `ok` true, `at` the result's own `at`, written when it finished, `github_env.py:1525`, when it parses, else now; `seconds` when known; `why` "start routine (<source>, ancestor of <head[:12]>)", no `reused`, no `base`; no new key, so `kit/state_schema.json` is unchanged; a result already recorded on A with that `at` is not recorded again, which keeps the 6-hour window honest and spares the 20-row `smoke_runs` cap, `runner/cycle.py:1158`), then the ancestry reuse for the head runs as today and, when it stands, is recorded and the claim proceeds in the same call; when it does not stand (something became doubted meanwhile) the head is smoked as today; (c) finished red: recorded on A (`ok` false, `at` as in (b), so A is doubted and no ancestry reuse passes through it), nothing claimed, and the head is smoked in the same call exactly as today (`_smoke`); a red head then sets `main` red or makes a D-498 strike through the unchanged `_next_step` code (`runner/cycle.py:1723`-`1732`). A red on A never sets `main` red by itself: later commits may have fixed it, and `offending_merge` would blame the latest DONE merge, so FIX-MAIN would revert or charge the wrong task; (d) finished with no result, or timed out: recorded as a timed-out run on A (D-1178; `at` as in (b)), `smoke_timeout`, no strike, nothing claimed; the next call smokes the head. A finished own pre-session result for a qualifying A (`main` moved during the job's warm-up) is collected the same way. tasks.goal: Plan change D-4180, choice (5) (merge-line lag; evidence in D-4180): when a task merges, the next turn holder of the D-3418 merge line gets its update merge only inside some lane's session cycle, after the cache, warm-up and smoke steps; the early `--resolve-merges` step (D-3141; `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml` "Close merged tasks before the smoke (D-3141)", `runner/cycle.py` `resolve_merged`) marks the merged task DONE but pushes no update. So the turn and its order are exactly the cycle's: `_merge_line` (FIX-MAIN first, then hand-in order, then task id), `_line_place`, `_mark_turn`, the late tasks taken last, the red-`main` guard (only FIX-MAIN moves while `main` is red), and every open-PR rule of `_open_pr_step` and `_update_step` (the update merge is `env.update_branch`, built by `_built_update` and pushed only after `UpdateMerge.is_update_merge` proves it is exactly the reviewed head plus `main`, union-aware, a fast-forward never forced, refused as "moved" when the branch tip is not the reviewed head; a conflict goes to a resync, D-891; push failures and waits count as today; auto-merge already on stays on, but the early pass never turns it on, see (2)). Each outcome goes through `_lane_outcome` as in the cycle. Nothing else changes (apart from the merged-or-absent tasks above, left as read, and auto-merge, left to the session's cycle): with nothing merged to close it still returns `NO_MERGED` and writes nothing, touches no update merge, inbox, smoke or claim; a lost race still changes nothing in the state (an update merge already pushed is then adopted by the cycle's existing `update_merge_of` path as "adopted", D-584/D-620); the result string stays `MERGES_RESOLVED` so `runner/__main__.py`'s early-row and refill logic (D-3141) is unchanged. No lease is taken or needed: `_update_step` checks no lease today (verified, `runner/cycle.py:846`), any lane's cycle updates any task's branch, and auto-pr's lane-lease rule (`verify.auto_merge_reason`) is unchanged. Keep `resolve_merged` and each helper under 50 lines (split as needed). Confirm, at that point of the job, that `RUNNER_PUSH_TOKEN` (already in the step's env), git's identity and fetch of `main` and the task branch are what `GitHubEnv.update_branch` needs (the cycle's later steps run it today) and add only what is missing; keep `continue-on-error: true` (a failure leaves the update to the session's cycle, as before) and keep `timeout-minutes: 5` unless the report shows an update merge needs longer. `enable_auto_merge` runs `gh pr merge --auto` first with `RUNNER_PUSH_TOKEN` (D-519); if that is refused, `run_command` retries with `GH_TOKEN`, which in this step is `github.token`, not the Claude App's token the session has (D-502). tasks.title: harness: Ci skips a compile its job already passed on a proven parent with the same compiled inputs (proven-parent pass)
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4281 (Fable's merge-speed decision, Nov 18, 2026, about 00:30Z, `main` 7f322437, under Casey's standing rule: speed is the goal, quality must not decline). Task P, the proven-parent pass (Fable item 2). The merge line is the limit: about 50 merges a day, and 79% of occupied lane time is MERGE_PENDING. Every update merge recompiles everything in `Ci` even when `main` moved only by plan or docs files (runs 44202683133 and 44199070725: Checks 19.5 to 20.5 min, Coverage 17 to 18, Lint 7 to 8, E2e 4 to 6; a plan-only branch's `ci` takes 3 to 4; 11 of 26 update merges in 24 hours brought in only plan or hand-off files). D-489 compiles only when compiled inputs changed against `main`; this extends it to "against a commit already proven green". What changes: in each of the four `changes` steps of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Checks: `rust` and `npm`; Lint and slow tests: `rust`; Coverage: `rust`; E2e: `run`), after today's rule has set a flag true on a branch run, a new standard-library script `scripts/ci_proven.py` may set that flag back to false, only when ALL of these hold for a candidate commit C: (1) C is HEAD^1, HEAD has exactly two parents, and HEAD^2 is on origin/main's first-parent line (`git rev-list --first-parent origin/main` over the depth the step already fetches); that is the runner's update merge (`runner/update_merge.py` `commit`: parents the reviewed head, then main; after an update the reviewed head is the previous update merge, whose own `ci` ran); (2) every run of this repository's `.github/workflows/ci.yml` workflow on C (Actions REST, matched by the workflow's id or its exact `path`, `event == push`, and the run's `repository.full_name` and `head_repository.full_name` both equal to `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`; every attempt) has the same job, by its exact name, completed with conclusion `success`, and at least one such job exists; (3) `git -c core.quotepath=off diff -z --no-renames --name-only C HEAD` (NUL-separated, so no path is quoted or split) matches neither that flag's own rule regex (the very string the step already uses, passed to the script, never a second copy) nor `tests/coverage_floor.json`, `scripts/coverage_floor.py`, `.cargo/`, `.github/workflows/` or `scripts/ci_proven.py`. Anything else means unproven and the flag stays true: a HEAD with one or three parents; HEAD^2 off main's first-parent line or beyond the fetch; a run queued or in progress; any conclusion but `success` (skipped, cancelled, neutral, timed_out, failure); a missing job; an HTTP error; a timeout (10 s per call); a page that may be incomplete; malformed JSON; a git error. The script prints exactly one line, `proven=<40-hex sha>` or `unproven: <why>`, and always exits 0; a step trusts only an exact `proven=` line. Schedule, workflow_dispatch and `main` runs keep their early exit (always compile). No step outside the four flags changes: the sources fingerprint, gitleaks, the PII scan, conflict markers, plan lock and change rules, the delete guard (`ci.yml:146`, still before the Checks changes step), the Rust source rules, approved crates, the compiled-in-file check (D-1867), every other Python step and the whole Python job still run on HEAD. Permissions: the job token needs `actions: read` in `ci.yml`, nothing more; `nightly-main.yml` calls `ci.yml` with `contents: read` only, and a called workflow cannot ask for more than its caller grants, so the nightly's `ci` call gets `actions: read` too (otherwise the nightly fails to start, and a red nightly stops every claim, D-3795); actionlint reports nothing new on either file. DONE-rule guarantee, for the reviewer: `git diff origin/main -- runner/` is empty, so `verify.check_done` is unchanged; `Ci`, `Twin` and `Ally` still run on every pushed head (no `paths:` filter, no job-level `if`; only step-level skips inside jobs, as D-489 already does), so DONE still needs every Ci, Twin and Ally run on the head green and the squash tree equal to the head tree; a skip happens only when the same job already passed on a commit whose compiled inputs for that job are byte-identical, and that commit's own success was in turn a compile or such a proof, down to a full compile. The decision entry lists, for each step a flag can now skip, every input it reads, including what it reads from origin/main (the named mutants' `--base origin/main`, Coverage's floor comparison), and why the regex or the extra paths cover it; an input outside them is added to the extra paths, never left out. Tests: `tests/test_ci_proven.py` builds real temporary git repositories and fakes only the REST answers, one parametrized planted case per rule: proven (a docs-only move of main); a compiled path in the diff (one path for each job's regex, a rename from `docs/` into `app/`, a deleted compiled input); `tests/coverage_floor.json`, a workflow file and `scripts/ci_proven.py` in the diff; HEAD with one and with three parents; HEAD^2 not on main's first-parent line; the job failed, cancelled, skipped, in progress or missing; two runs on C, one red; a run of another workflow path or event, or of another repository or head repository; a path with spaces or non-ASCII bytes; HTTP 403, 404 and 500, a timeout, bad JSON, a full page; a git failure. `tests/test_ci_workflow.py` adds: each of the four steps passes its own rule string to the script and treats only `proven=` as proof; the schedule, dispatch and main early exit is unchanged and comes first; the delete guard precedes the Checks changes step; no scan, lock, change-rule or Python step gains a `steps.changes` condition; the nightly's `ci` call grants what `ci.yml` asks; every existing test there and `tests/test_prehandin.py` pass unchanged. `docs/architecture.md` section 12 gets a "Proven-parent pass (D-4281)" bullet beside "Compiled-in files".

tasks.title: harness: Ci handles the merge train's throwaway refs and counts a green train tip as proof for the real update merge
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4281 (Fable's merge-speed decision, Nov 18, 2026, about 00:30Z, `main` 7f322437, under Casey's standing rule: speed is the goal, quality must not decline). Task Q, part 1 of 2: the merge train's `ci` side (Fable item 2; split from the runner side, T641, because one task owning `runner/cycle.py`, `runner/github_env.py` and `ci.yml` measured 71% of the window against the harness limit of 50). The train (T641): while turn holder A's head A' has Ci, Twin or Ally pending, the runner pushes X, the update merge of the next line task B's reviewed head with A', to a new throwaway ref `claude/train/<B>-<A' first 12 hex>` (never B's task branch, never main, never forced). This task makes `ci` and the other push workflows handle such refs and lets X's green runs prove B's later real update merge. (1) `scripts/ci_proven.py` (T638): on a `claude/task/T###-` branch, besides HEAD^1, every tip of a `claude/train/T###-*` ref of the same task (read with `git ls-remote` and the job token; an error, or a name not exactly `claude/train/T###-<12 hex>`, drops only those candidates and HEAD^1 is still judged) is a candidate, proven by T638's rules (2) and (3) unchanged; X is not an ancestor of B' and the shallow checkout lacks it, so before the diff the script fetches each accepted train ref's tip (`git fetch --no-tags --depth=1` from the plain repository URL, the job token passed to git through `http.extraheader` set from the environment or `GIT_ASKPASS`, never in the URL or argv) and a failed fetch drops only that candidate, whose `unproven:` line says `fetch failed (exit N)` and never carries git's stderr; a train candidate needs no parent relation, because rule (3) compares the job's compiled inputs byte for byte, and its runs are found by SHA like HEAD^1's. On a `claude/train/` ref the script proves nothing; D-489 applies to X as on any branch. (2) `ci.yml`: "Plan lock and change rules" is today the only Checks step that fetches origin/main (`ci.yml:128` to `:136`), and the delete guard (`:146`, `git cat-file -e origin/main:$f`, which passes when origin/main is missing: it fails open), the merge-base at `:166` and the named mutants' `--base origin/main` (`:297`) all need it. So the main fetch moves into its own unconditional step before the delete guard, on every ref; the delete guard is made to FAIL when origin/main cannot be read; and on a ref whose `github.ref_name` starts with `claude/train/` only the two commands `check_plan_lock.py` and `check_pr_change.py` are skipped (X carries A's and B's changes under no task branch, so the change rules would fail and turn Checks red, and a red X proves nothing; both heads are checked by those rules on their own branches); every other step runs. (3) `twin.yml` and `a11y.yml` add `!claude/train/**` to their push branches (their results on X prove nothing; skipping them keeps Actions load down, peak near 40 jobs); `governance.yml` skips a `claude/train/` head as it skips `claude/kit-state` (no pull request has it). `auto-pr.yml` (only `claude/task/**`) and the backup gate (only `claude/task/` heads) already ignore such refs. Expected: when A's squash tree equals A' (the DONE rule) and the merge bases agree, B''s compiled inputs equal X's and B's round is bounded by Ally, 5 to 8 minutes on any head (measured Nov 17 to 18; Ally has no change filter and is not touched here), so about 8 minutes, not Fable's 4; otherwise B runs a full round as today. DONE rule, for the reviewer: `runner/` is untouched; Ci, Twin and Ally still run on every task-branch head; X's runs never count for DONE (`verify.check_done` reads checks on the pull request's head SHA only) and only shorten a later head's compile when that head's compiled inputs equal X's. Tests: `tests/test_ci_proven.py` adds planted cases: a train tip with the same compiled inputs proves B'; another task's train tip and a malformed ref name are ignored; a red, cancelled or pending train run is unproven; an ls-remote error drops the train candidates and HEAD^1 is still judged; nothing is proven on a `claude/train/` ref. a clone that lacks X until the script fetches it still proves B' (planted), and a failed fetch drops only that candidate. `tests/test_ci_workflow.py` adds: origin/main is fetched in an unconditional step before the delete guard, on every ref; the delete guard fails (not passes) when origin/main is missing (planted with a repository that has no origin/main); only the two plan-lock and change-rule commands carry the `claude/train/` condition, and every other step of every job is the same on a train ref; twin.yml and a11y.yml exclude `claude/train/**` and still run on `claude/**` otherwise; governance skips `claude/train/` heads. (2) `wake_after`: when free_slots is above 0 and `last` (the arming cycle's own result) is neither in NOTHING_CLAIMED nor in `runner/__main__.py` REFILL_STOP (copy the names, with a test that the two sets are equal), it returns IDLE_MINUTES with why `free lanes: <n> with claimable work`, before the live-lease branch. `on_wake` gets the same guard: the keeper step reads `kit/runner_log.jsonl` (as the arm step does) and passes the last cycle result to `on_wake` (`--log`), so a lease-length sleep that follows a REFILL_STOP result does not wake into the short path; an unreadable log means no short path. tasks.title: recovery: the monthly test restore into a throwaway cluster, with its High alert
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4293 (split from T109; OPS-013, OPS-051, D-232, D-492): `recovery`'s monthly test restore, in the new `app/recovery/src/restore.rs` (declared in the shared `lib.rs` and exported through the shared `api.rs`). Each run takes a fresh `pg_dump -Fc` stream through T109's `ASKHAVA_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL` and T109's path helper (before any encryption), and restores it on a separate throwaway PostgreSQL 16 service, never the live database: it connects through a new `ASKHAVA_RESTORE_ADMIN_URL` (that service's admin role; a `SecretString`, never logged; it joins `KEYS` in the shared `app/core/src/settings.rs`; a missing key fails the run closed in dev and stops start-up in test and live), creates its own database there under a name it makes, runs `scripts/bootstrap_roles.sql` first (embedded with `include_str!`, since the runtime image holds no `scripts/`, `Dockerfile` runtime stage; with no role passwords set, so every role stays `NOLOGIN`), then `pg_restore --single-transaction`, then the ownership and append-only grant check (every restored object owned by `askhava_migrator`; `askhava_app` holding no `UPDATE` or `DELETE` on an append-only table), and drops the database whatever happened. It then checks the latest nightly export from its record, not its object: the newest `recovery.backup_check` row of kind `export` (T109's migration 0198: `ok`, `object_bytes`, `object_sha256`) is `ok`, finished within the last 26 hours, and has its size and hash recorded; a missing, failed, stale or incomplete row fails the check (D-4835: PRIV-029 keeps the export prefix's storage key write-only, `app/adapters/src/storage.rs:39` to `:44`, so the object cannot be read back, and an x25519 `age` header does not name its recipient; no private key on the host, PRIV-024). Each result is one `recovery.backup_check` row of kind restore (T109's migration 0198) and one `ops::api::audit` entry, which T524's digest reads through `ops::api::latest_audit`; a failed restore raises one High alert (`ops::api::raise_alert`) that starts no safe mode, even unacknowledged for 48 hours (TD-OPS-22). The handler registers in `worker_registry` (the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs`; `tests/integration/tests/task_registry.rs`), and the first run is queued by one line in `schedule_start` (the shared `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs`) under a dedupe key, each run queuing the next a month on, through this task's own monthly scheduler in `restore.rs` with its own dedupe key; the first run is queued for after the next nightly export (its due time later than that export's), so a fresh environment never raises the High alert before any export row exists (T109's `schedule_export`, `app/recovery/src/backup.rs:315`, is fixed to the export kind and is not reused). `tests/recovery/tests/export_restores.rs` (TD-OPS-26): CI's one PostgreSQL already has the roles (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:80` to `:86`), so the test makes a throwaway cluster with PostgreSQL 16's own `initdb` and `pg_ctl` (found by name on `PATH` through T109's path helper, which accepts only a binary whose `--version` major is 16; on `Ci` T724's preflight puts `/usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin` on `PATH` of the `ubuntu-24.04` jobs, D-4708; the test names no PostgreSQL directory itself) in a temporary folder on a free local port (`initdb` refuses root: the test runs it and `pg_ctl` as an unprivileged user, e.g. through `runuser` to a user it creates when it is root), points `ASKHAVA_RESTORE_ADMIN_URL` at it, restores without and then with `scripts/bootstrap_roles.sql` (without: fails and leaves no object), plants an object owned by another role and an `UPDATE` grant to the app role on an append-only table (each fails the check), checks a job number texted out is never reused after the restore (TD-JOB-06), and stops and removes the cluster; missing binaries fail the test with a message, never a skip. Update `app/recovery/NOTES.md`, `docs/architecture.md` section 9 if anything there changes, and `docs/decisions.md`. Fake data only. Budget 450 lines. Review round 1 (D-4293): (a) `ASKHAVA_RESTORE_ADMIN_URL` is an optional key with an accessor returning `Result<&SecretString, SettingsError>` like `migration_database_url` (`app/core/src/settings.rs:523`): only the worker's restore handler reads it, only the worker refuses to start without it in test and live (dev and `Ci` fail the run closed), and it is set on the `worker` service only, never on `web` (SEC-052's pattern); this replaces the start-up sentence above. (b) `scripts/bootstrap_roles.sql` is a `psql` script (`\set`, `\getenv`, `\if`, `\gexec`), so sqlx cannot run it: the embedded text is piped into `psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f -` (T109's path helper's `psql`, version-checked) against the new throwaway database, with no role passwords in its environment. Plan change D-4835 (Opus pre-claim scout): (1) run the test as `PATH=/usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin:$PATH cargo test -p askhava-recovery-tests --test export_restores` (the prompt's "Run your tests" line without that prefix finds no PostgreSQL 16 `initdb` here); the worker runs as root, so the test's `runuser` branch runs, and the temporary cluster folder must be `chown`ed to the user it creates before `initdb`; (2) `tests/recovery/Cargo.toml` (a shared path) has no `[dependencies]` yet: add `askhava-recovery`, `askhava-core` and `askhava-ops` path dependencies and the workspace's `sqlx` and `tokio`; `tests/recovery/tests/` is new. Plan change D-4852 (attempt 1's plan gap): T764 adds `scripts/bootstrap_roles.sql` to the Rust path rules, so the `include_str!` passes `scripts/check_include_paths.py`; this task waits for it. Budget: attempt 1 measured about 900 lines (551 in `restore.rs`, 348 in its test), over the old 450; the declared budget is now 600, the build ceiling, and an overage with no scope creep is accepted and logged in this task's decision entry (D-4673's precedent): keep `restore.rs` to the restore, the checks and the scheduler (no second copy of T109's helpers), and the test to TD-OPS-26's cases; the restore and its test stay one task because neither is useful alone. Never write a script with `std::fs::write` and exec it from the same test process: a concurrent fork can hold the write descriptor and the exec fails with "Text file busy" (D-4864). Create any fake binary through a waited-on child process (`/bin/sh` with the arguments `-c`, `printf %s "$2" > "$1" && chmod 755 "$1"`, `sh`, the path, the text), as `write_script` in `app/recovery/src/backup.rs` `mod tests` does; that helper is private to its file, so write your own few-line copy in your own test file.

tasks.title: messaging and payments: mark a replayed text sent from the carrier's log, and rebuild a lost charge from Stripe's record
tasks.goal: Plan change D-3753: T110's replay (OPS-015 to OPS-017) must mark an outbox row sent with the SID it found in Twilio's sent log and rebuild charges from Stripe's records, but `messaging::models::mark_sent` (`app/messaging/src/models.rs:278`) is `pub(crate)` and moves only a `sending` row, and `payments` has no charge rebuild (`book_success`, `app/payments/src/charge.rs:687`, is `pub(crate)`). (1) `app/messaging/src/replay_sent.rs`, through `messaging::api`: `mark_replayed_sent(conn, row, listed, sent_at)` (exported through `messaging::api` and so callable by any higher crate, but its one intended caller is T110's replay in `recovery`; its doc says so) marks an outbox row that is not yet `sent` (`queued`, `sending`, `unknown` or `failed`; never `blocked` or `expired`) sent with the listed message's SID, its body cleared, under the row's lock, once (a second call or a row already sent changes nothing and says so); it refuses a SID already stored on another outbox row and a listed message whose `To` is not the row's recipient (resolved as the sender resolves it, through `privacy::api`) or whose `From` is not one of Laftly's sending numbers, and writes one `ops` audit row of IDs only; it sends nothing. (2) `app/payments/src/charge_rebuild.rs`, through `payments::api`: `rebuild_charge(conn, charge, at)` takes one succeeded charge as `list_charge_page` lists it (`app/adapters/src/payments.rs:435`) and, when its PaymentIntent's label names a pick and try (`pick-<id>-try<n>`, `intent_label`/`attempt_label`) that `payments` holds and its PaymentIntent ID equals the one stored for that pick in `payments.pick_intent`, books it through `book_success` under its derived `charge_key` (one evidence record, one `charge` ledger entry, its receipt task), never calling Stripe to charge; a charge already booked answers `AlreadyBooked` and changes nothing; one whose pick is unknown or whose PaymentIntent ID differs answers `Unmatched` with its `ch_` ID, for T110 to refund and flag (TD-OPS-04); a charge Stripe shows refunded (fully or in part) answers `Refunded` and books nothing, for T110 to list. Money code: 95% branch coverage. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/replay_helpers.rs` against PostgreSQL and the stand-in Stripe, fake data only: each status marked once, a `blocked` row, a SID already on another row and a wrong recipient refused; a lost charge rebuilt once with exactly one ledger row, a second rebuild adding nothing, an unknown pick and a mismatched PaymentIntent answered unmatched, a refunded charge booked nowhere. Update the `messaging` and `payments` `NOTES.md` and `docs/decisions.md`. Plan change D-3844 (the overseer's pre-claim scout, Nov 15, 2026): corrects the matching above. Stripe's charge list returns no idempotency key or `pick-<id>-try<n>` label (`ListedCharge`, `app/adapters/src/payments.rs:171` to `:185`, carries only the charge, its PaymentIntent and `metadata[pick_id]`), so `rebuild_charge` matches on `pick_id` and the PaymentIntent stored for that pick in `payments.pick_intent` only, and takes `try_no` from the pick's newest `payments.charge_attempt` row. `book_success` (`app/payments/src/charge.rs:687`) books nothing and still returns `Ok` when `write_evidence`'s join on that attempt (`:761`) finds no row, so a pick with no attempt row (lost in the restore) answers `Unmatched`, never a silent success, and the rebuild reports booked only when the evidence record was written. Money work: an Opus review in two rounds (the second on the head the first round's fixes produce). Plan change D-3877 (Fable's pre-claim check of stage-5 wave 0, Nov 15, 2026): `mark_replayed_sent` also takes the vault and the sending lines (`mark_replayed_sent(conn, vault, lines, row, listed, sent_at)`); it calls `privacy::api::read_contact` directly and does not copy `homeowner_phone` (`app/messaging/src/outbox_sender.rs:207`). T481 defines the listed-message struct (SID, To, From) in `replay_sent.rs`. Plan change D-3889 (Fable's pre-claim check, Nov 16, 2026, revised after the plan change's review): (3) for T110's replay, which can read neither `messaging.outbox` nor the vault, and with no recipient number ever leaving `messaging`: `messaging::api::replay_window(conn)` gives the sending numbers and the earliest and latest send time of the outbox rows not yet `sent` (the statuses `mark_replayed_sent` takes), with no recipient; `messaging::api::replay_match(conn, vault, listed)` takes the messages T110 listed from Twilio (SID, `To`, `From`, body, send time; a `messaging` type) and, inside `messaging`, matches each unsent row by its recipient (resolved under `messaging`'s send grant), sender, the body's SHA-256 (a redacted body matches on recipient, sender and send time within the window) and send time, answering only row IDs with a matched SID, ambiguous or none; no number is returned or logged. `tests/integration/tests/replay_helpers.rs` covers both.

tasks.title: picks: a job that reaches a final status ends its pick awaiting Confirm or in Payment pending and cancels the PaymentIntent
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4748 (Fable's decision (4); FEE-021, PICK-038; D-4361, D-4349, D-1576). After T681, `jobs::service::move_to` queues one `jobs.final_status` task `{job, status}` when a job enters a final status and its handler in `app/picks/src/aftermath.rs` sends `no_longer_active` (`:319`); a pick still awaiting Confirm or in Payment pending on that job is left as it was, so its Confirm window, reminders and open PaymentIntent outlive the job and a late payment is caught only by the Left-and-refund path (FEE-021). This task, after T681: (1) the new `app/picks/src/final_status_end.rs` `end_for_final(tx, job, status, at)`, called by that handler in the same transaction before `no_longer_active`, sends every waiting, not-ended pick on the job (`awaiting_confirm` and Payment pending alike) through T663's `picks::api::end_pending` with a new reason `job_final` (added in `app/picks/src/connect.rs`), which ends the PaymentIntent through `payments`' own pick end so it is cancelled at Stripe and a charge that still succeeds is refunded (FEE-021, D-2958); an `awaiting_confirm` pick can have a PICK-048 auto-confirm charge in flight (`charge_off_session`, `app/picks/src/auto_confirm.rs:280`), and with no PaymentIntent the cancel is a no-op; its queued Confirm reminders and window end then act on nothing, as `cant_take` leaves them. `picks.pick.end_reason` is CHECK-constrained (`pick_end_reason_check`, last replaced by `migrations/0189_picks_fee_terms_changed.sql:7` to `:11`), so the new `migrations/0214_picks_job_final_end.sql` (after T745's 0213 and before T729's 0215 in the runner's serial order, which is why this task also waits for T745) replaces it the same way (NOT VALID, then VALIDATE) with every value the check allows on `main` at claim (re-read the newest migration that replaces it) plus `job_final`; re-check the number at claim against the migration-order rule; a pick already `paid`, `free` or ended is untouched; the job is not moved again (it is already final) and no backup is offered (the job is over). T681's `tests/integration/tests/aftermath_notices.rs` passes unchanged. Money: Opus worker, Opus money, privacy and security review, two review rounds. tasks.title: businesses: an unknown ROC license status warns at 24 hours, pauses at 72 and resumes on a later Active standing
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4310 (Fable's decision on the licensing spot review of `main` 4fee847d, finding 2's second half and finding 3; D-941 named this work with no owner; review R1 B1 to B3). `licensing::api::unknown_standing` (`app/licensing/src/handlers.rs:96`) has no production caller, nothing writes a `license` pause except `lift_no_cover`'s re-hold (`app/businesses/src/license_reapply.rs:218`), and nothing ever lifts one, against LIC-008 ("a pause that clears when the list loads needs no review"). After T654 every recorded ROC list writes each active business's daily `license_check`, and cards stop at the latest Active check's `checked_at + pause_after`. (1) `app/licensing/src/daily_lists.rs` (after T654): a public `roc_standing(conn, business, run_hour)` exported through `licensing::api`, giving the latest check (status, `checked_at`) and the ROC list's failure start (`recorded_failure_start`) when the list is failing and that check is before it; nothing for a business with no check row (no ROC number). (2) New `app/businesses/src/license_standing.rs`, a daily task chain `businesses.license_standing`, queued like the other chains and registered on the worker clock in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` (`now` from the worker's clock, as `register_purge_handlers` does), run after the ROC list's run hour and again each LIC-039 retry slot. One clock for both tasks (B3): for an active business whose latest check is `active` and whose list is failing, the pause moment is that check's `checked_at + pause_after` (LIC-008's 72-hour setting, `FailureLimits`), the instant T654 stops its cards, and the warning moment is the earlier of `failure start + warn_after` (24 hours) and the pause moment; `unknown_standing` is applied with `unknown_since` the failure start and its answer capped by those two moments. LIC-008's "stays as it was for up to 72 hours" holds: the latest Active check is never after the failure start, so the pause comes at most 72 hours after the status became unknown, never later. Warned: one `license_unknown` notice email to the owner, once per unknown spell (keyed by the business and the failure start), with its audit row; its words name the pause moment. Paused: the business is paused with reason `license` through the status machine (system actor, audit row in the same transaction), and if no `license_unknown` notice exists for this spell it is queued in that same transaction (B2: never a pause without a warning). Before the resume step, the chain records `check_license` against the latest ROC list for each business paused with reason `license` (a database-only read of the recorded list, never a lookup; review R2), because the daily list run checks only `active` businesses (`businesses::api::active_license_numbers`, `app/businesses/src/api.rs:239`, behind `server`'s `ActiveRoc`, which stays unchanged) and a paused business would otherwise never get a newer check; a business already checked against that list's date is skipped. Then, for each business paused with reason `license` whose latest check is `active` and later than the pause, with no pest report holding it (`pest_reported`), it resumes with `Event::Resume` and no review, unless a complaint hold or an earlier self-pause applies, in `lift_no_cover`'s order (complaints, then self). This is also the exit for `lift_no_cover`'s `license` re-hold (finding 3); `license_reapply.rs` changes only in that function's doc. A known Inactive or Not-listed check is not paused here: T654 stops its ROC cards and Confirm refuses it (PICK-020). Each pause and resume is a system-actor status audit row, which T524's weekly digest counts as automatic pauses and license-unknown counts (OPS-030, D-3882) and which is Casey's count (D-199); this task adds no digest code. (3) `app/businesses/src/notice_emails.rs` (after T490, which also changes it): `license_unknown` joins `NOTICE_KINDS`, to the owner's account address like `license_change`, with its English and Spanish words here (BIZ-018): Laftly could not check the ROC license on the state list since <date>; if it still can't by <the pause moment, Arizona time>, job cards pause until it can; nothing is needed if the license is Active. No license number, contact value or link in the payload; never "verified" or "vetted". Deferred: LIC-009's end and bond dates (the ROC list has no such column, D-902). Tests, fake data only, on PostgreSQL, in `tests/integration/tests/license_standing.rs` (TD-LIC-05): with the list failing from the day after a check, the warning at failure start + 24:00:00 and not at 23:59:59; kept at pause moment minus 1 second; paused at the pause moment, the same instant at which T654's `latest_check_allows_card` turns false (both asserted in one case); a first run only at the pause moment sends one notice and pauses in one transaction; a check old enough that the pause moment precedes failure start + 24 hours warns at once; one email per spell; a `license`-paused business with a fresh list showing its license Active gets a check row written by the run itself (not planted) and resumes with no review; the pause cleared with no review by a later Active lookup too, kept on an Inactive check, a pest report or a complaint hold; `lift_no_cover`'s re-hold cleared the same way; a system-actor status audit row for each pause and resume. Update `app/businesses/NOTES.md`, `app/licensing/NOTES.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: payments: rebuild_charge reports Booked inside a caller's transaction and takes its locks in record's order
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4292 (spot review of money, verified on `main` 67827d85; both latent, as today's only caller passes a bare connection). (a) `rebuild_charge` (`app/payments/src/charge_rebuild.rs:63` to `:82`) opens `conn.begin()` and then decides `Booked` by `xmin = pg_current_xact_id()::xid` on the evidence row; inside a caller's transaction that `begin` is a savepoint, the row's `xmin` is the subtransaction's ID while `pg_current_xact_id()` returns the top-level one, so a charge this call just booked is reported `AlreadyBooked` (TD-OPS-04: `Rebuilt` must say whether this call booked). Decide it without `xmin`: `held_try` has already seen no evidence row under the `pick_intent` row lock, and every writer of `payments.charge_evidence` (`charge::book_success` through `record`'s effects after `hold_pick`, `reclear`) takes that row's lock first, so the row existing after `book_success` means this call wrote it; check each writer, list them in the doc, and report a plan gap if one does not take the lock. (b) Lock order: `rebuild_charge` locks `pick_intent` `FOR UPDATE` and then inserts evidence whose foreign key to `charge_attempt (pick_id, try_no)` takes a key-share lock on the attempt row, while `record` (`app/payments/src/handlers.rs:126` to `:131`, then `hold_pick`) locks the attempt row `FOR UPDATE` and then `pick_intent` `FOR SHARE`; run together on one pick (a restored 30-minute check or a Stripe resend during a replay) they deadlock (40P01). Make `rebuild_charge` take the newest attempt row `FOR UPDATE` before `pick_intent`, the order `record` uses, and re-check under the `pick_intent` lock that it is still the newest (`max(try_no)`; a newer attempt made meanwhile answers as `held_try` does today), after checking the order of every other path that locks both (`confirm_and_pay`, `end_pick`, `end_intent_unless_charging`, `late_success`) and naming it in the doc. Correct the function doc at `app/payments/src/charge_rebuild.rs:41` to `:42`, which says the webhook does not take the pick's lock: `record` takes it `FOR SHARE` through `hold_pick`. `payments::api` and `Rebuilt` keep their shape. (3) Tests, fake data only, in `tests/integration/tests/rebuild_charge_locks.rs` on PostgreSQL: every case of TD-OPS-45; the payments branch coverage floor holds (95%). T110 depends on this task. Update `app/payments/NOTES.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.
