tasks.title: Runner (harness): free the backup job's disk and cap the smoke build cache
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4071 (8 `backup` jobs lost their VM mid-session from Nov 16 19:06Z on a full root disk; evidence in D-4071): keep `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`'s `backup` job off a full `/dev/root`. Only that job and `runner/cache.py` change; nothing the smoke or a task worker runs changes. (1) Free the disk: a new step `Free the runner disk (D-4071)` (`continue-on-error: true`, `timeout-minutes: 10`) right after `Close merged tasks before the smoke (D-3141)` and right before `Rust build cache (D-514)`, so every cache restore lands on the freed disk and the merge resolution still runs within a minute of the start. It prints `df -h / | sed 's/^/disk before: /'`, removes `/usr/local/lib/android /usr/share/dotnet /opt/ghc /usr/local/.ghcup /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL /usr/share/swift` with `sudo rm -rf` (one background job per path, then `wait`; a missing path is no error) and prints `df -h / | sed 's/^/disk after: /'`. First grep `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`, `scripts/` and `runner/` for each path's tools (android, dotnet, ghc, ghcup, cabal, stack, swift, codeql) and leave out any path the job uses; the report gives each grep's result. Node, Python (`setup-python`'s `/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python`), Go (gitleaks' fallback `go install`), rustup and cargo, Docker and its images (the Postgres service), the Playwright browsers and the claude-code-action runtime stay. (2) Cap the smoke entry, in `runner/cache.py` (stdlib only, functions under 50 lines, `key=value` lines alone on standard output): `bound(smoke, cap)` deletes the profile-level `incremental` folders (`smoke/*/incremental` and `smoke/<triple>/*/incremental`; the smoke runs with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, `runner/github_env.py:230`, so this rarely frees anything and the cap does the work), then sums the tree's apparent size (`github_env._tree_size`) and prints `save=yes` when it is at most `cap`, else `save=no` plus a `::warning::` line on standard error naming the size and the cap; a tree it cannot measure also gives `save=no`. Standard error gets one line with the bytes before and after. `SMOKE_CAP` is 24 GiB; the CLI is `python3 -m runner.cache bound --smoke <dir> [--cap-gib N]`. Nothing else under `target/smoke` is deleted. Workflow: a step `Bound the smoke build entry (D-4071)` (id `smoke-bound`, the same `if` as `smoke-drop`, `continue-on-error: true`, run as `cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/keeper" && python3 -m runner.cache bound --smoke "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target/smoke" | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`) right after `Stop a background smoke before the cache save (D-2560)` and right before `Drop the superseded smoke build entries (D-3143)`; the save's `if` gains ` && steps.smoke-bound.outputs.save == 'yes'` right after ` && steps.smoke-drop.outputs.save != 'no'` and before the final ` && steps.bg-smoke.outputs.stopped != 'stopped'` (which `tests/test_runner_smoke_reuse.py:508`, not owned here, pins as the ending). It fails closed: a step that crashed (bash `-e` without pipefail, so `tee` hides the exit) writes no output and the tree is not saved; the bound step runs under the drop's `if`, so an empty output can only mean the tree was not measured. The drop step's `if` is unchanged, so an entry over the cap is still dropped and nothing replaces it: the next job builds the smoke cold and saves a fresh, small entry. The cap heals itself that way, at the cost of one cold smoke build each time the entry outgrows it. Why 24 GiB: the entry held 4,970 MB compressed (about 23 GB on disk) through Nov 16 07:39 with no loss, and the observed ratio is about 4.7 to 1 (46 GB on disk for 9.4 to 9.7 GB), so the cap is about 5.1 GB compressed, inside D-3143's 10 GB repository budget beside `Ci`'s entries; with the worker's `target/debug` (26 GB seen), `target/tests` (1.7 GB) and llvm-cov (about 6 GB) it leaves over 25 GB free on the 145 GB disk (60 GB used by the image) even if step (1) frees nothing. (3) Disk lines: `df -h / | sed 's/^/disk at session start: /' || true` at the end of `Pick the session's model (D-2225)` (the last step before the session) and `df -h / | sed 's/^/disk at hand-in: /' || true` right after `set -u` in `Hand in for a session that stopped without handing in (D-503)` (`backup-runner.yml:624`); neither writes to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`. (4) Tests in `tests/test_runner_cache.py`, on fake trees only: `bound` deletes profile-level `incremental` folders and keeps everything else, answers `save=yes` at or under a small cap and `save=no` with the warning over it, and `save=no` when the tree cannot be measured; `bound` joins `test_standard_output_holds_only_key_value_lines`. The workflow tests pin the two new steps' names, ids, conditions and order (the free-disk step after `Close merged tasks` and before the first `actions/cache/restore`; bound right after the background-smoke stop and right before the drop, the drop still directly before the save) and the two disk lines; `test_the_smoke_entry_is_saved_only_from_main_alone_after_its_older_entries_are_dropped` pins the save's new `if` exactly as `save["if"] == drop["if"].replace(" && steps.bg-smoke", " && steps.smoke-drop.outputs.save != 'no' && steps.smoke-bound.outputs.save == 'yes' && steps.bg-smoke")` (stricter, not looser); `tests/test_runner_smoke_reuse.py` passes unchanged; nothing else in an existing test changes. Update `docs/architecture.md`'s build-caches line (D-3143) with the cap and the free-disk step.
tasks.acceptance: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_runner_cache.py tests/test_workflow_shell.py` passes with the new cases, the `bound` cases failing on `main` (no `bound` there); every other `tests/test_runner_*.py` and `tests/test_safety_hand_in_release.py` passes unchanged; the report holds the greps of step (1); `actionlint` on `backup-runner.yml` reports nothing new.

(1) `jobs`: a new `categories_of(conn, &[Uuid]) -> Result<BTreeSet<String>, FactsError>` in `app/jobs/src/job_facts.rs`, re-exported by one line in the shared `app/jobs/src/api.rs`: one statement reading each listed job's latest facts row (`SELECT DISTINCT ON (job_id) category FROM jobs.job_facts WHERE job_id = ANY($1) ORDER BY job_id, seq DESC`); a job with no row adds nothing, as `job_facts`' `None` does today. WEB-028 holds unchanged: no hand-typed number, nothing below the threshold. tasks.title: Docs tooling (harness): lossless compaction check and writing standard
tasks.goal: Plan change D-3856 (Casey, Nov 15, 2026: at the end of phase 1 every document needed for upkeep is "simplified and organized in a way that's most efficient", nothing left out, nothing "wordy for no reason"). Following `scripts/split_crate_doc.py --verify` (D-3474) and `scripts/split_arch_notes.py --verify` (D-3620). (1) `scripts/check_doc_compaction.py --map FILE [--base REF]`, standard-library Python. The map records `base` (the SHA it was made against, the default REF). For every file the map names, each line present at the base and gone or changed now must be listed (by SHA-256) with targets `path:start-end` that exist now. Each fact token of the old line must appear inside those ranges, not merely somewhere in the file. Fact tokens are requirement, TD-, D- and task IDs, paths, backticked names, numbers and amounts, quoted text, and the words never, not, no, only, must, may, unless, except, before and after. A line with no fact tokens needs a target range sharing at least 60% of its content words. A removed line that is blank, or that occurs as a whole line, byte for byte, inside its target range, passes without the token or word test (so blank lines and byte-identical section moves pass); map entries are a list, so identical removed lines are each listed or share one entry with several targets (D-3892). A byte-identical move (`moves`: old path to new path) passes when the bytes match. A map entry for a line that was not removed fails. The map may carry a `left` list (work deferred to T142), which the check ignores; the script's docstring states the map schema (`base`, the removed-line entries, `moves`, `left`), because T507 to T514 do not read the script. Across the whole tree, any backticked `path:N` or `path:N-M` cited outside `docs/decisions.md` (spec `Source:` lines, `kit/tasks.json`, crate `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/test-design.md` and the rest) whose text at those lines differs from the base fails; a citation of a path listed in `moves` is compared at its new path, and a cited line missing at both the base and now is not a difference (stale citations past a file's end exist, for example `app/jobs/CLAUDE.md:44`, a 29-line file). (2) The decision-digest check is T720's (D-4447). (3) Tests in `tests/test_check_doc_compaction.py`: each failure above, including a tokenless deletion, a token found only outside its range and a changed cited line, plus passing cases (among them a section with blank and repeated lines moved byte-identical to a new file), one of them a branch that merged a cited-line change from `main`, and one that runs the step on a merged commit on `main` carrying a map. (4) A `Ci` step runs `check_doc_compaction.py` on every map under `docs/reviews/doc-maps/` that the pull request adds or changes. A retry branch merges `main` in, so `Ci` takes the base as `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`, requires the map's recorded base to be its ancestor, and compares only the changes between that merge base and HEAD. Lines or cited code changed on `main` since the recorded base are not flagged, and a merged map never breaks later runs. On a run whose HEAD equals origin/main (a run on main: the nightly calls `Ci` through `workflow_call`, and `ci.yml` pushes only `claude/**` and `dependabot/**`), the base is HEAD^1, the commit before the merge. If no map changed in that commit, the step is skipped. (5) `docs/code-docs.md` gains a short writing standard: say a fact once, in the shortest clear form, where its reader looks first; link, don't repeat; keep IDs and cited lines stable; respect the size budgets T514 adds. Rewrite `kit/plan.lock`; the new scripts are covered by its `scripts/*.py` glob. Plan change D-4447 (Casey, Nov 18, 2026, about 7:40 am MST, asked "Start the digest early?", answered "Yes, start it now (Recommended)"): the digest check, its tests and the digest plan moved to T720 so the digest pieces run during stage 5; this task keeps the compaction check, its `Ci` step and the writing standard after T126.

Its range is set at claim time, not in the plan (D-3891): it starts at the number after the digest header's `Through` and ends at the highest number whose entries total at most 300,000 bytes (`wc -c`) of `docs/decisions.md`, as T720's digest-range table forecasts (re-measure: the log grows). An entry is a line starting `- **D-n**` or `**D-n**` (D-1552 to D-1561 have no leading `- `); numbers compare as integers whatever the zero padding, and the log is not in numeric order (D-516 precedes D-515), so select by number, never by file position, for example `awk -v a=620 -v b=999 'match($0, /^(- )?\*\*D-[0-9]+\*\*/) {n = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); gsub(/[^0-9]/, "", n); n += 0} n >= a && n <= b' docs/decisions.md` (pipe it to `wc -c` to measure, or read its output in chunks); never read the log or the digest whole. Each piece reads at most 300 KB of the log (about 38% of the window) beside its prompt and the 24 KB digest plan. Each entry still in force that sets a rule a later change must respect gets one rule line under its area (`- D-a[, D-b] (area) text`, at most 300 characters; a later decision that refines it goes on the same line); a reversed or replaced one goes under `## Superseded` as `D-a -> D-b`, with the pair added to `kit/superseded_decisions.json` when missing; one about how a single task was built goes on that task's `- T###: D-a, D-b` line under `## Task-scoped`. Lines from earlier pieces are kept, except that a piece whose range reverses, replaces or refines an earlier number moves that number to `## Superseded`, or adds its own number to that line; each number stays counted once. The header moves to the last number covered, and the digest stays within T720's size target: if it would pass it, shorten this piece's own lines first; if it still passes, hand in and state the overage in the report body (not as a `PLAN GAP` opening) for T514 and T142 (D-3892). Reading the range is this task's input, not tool output: read it in chunks of up to about 25 KB per call (the `awk` output piped to `cut -c1-25000`, then the rest of each long line), an exception to Output discipline 6. After adding a pair, regenerate prompts and commit only `kit/prompts/*`, never `kit/tasks.json`. Plan change D-4447 (Casey, Nov 18, 2026, about 7:40 am MST, asked "Start the digest early?", answered "Yes, start it now (Recommended)"): this piece runs during stage 5, beside build tasks, not after T126. Decisions keep landing meanwhile, so it also takes in, in their areas, any entry at or below the header's `Through` that the digest does not count yet (a number reserved earlier and merged after the last piece; `check_decision_digest.py` names it); a pair whose newer number is above the new `Through` stays pending. Once the new `Through` reaches a pending pair's newer number, this piece moves the older number's rule line to `## Superseded` as that pair (the check names any pair left as a rule line). `Ci` runs the digest check only once T514 wires it, and then only on a branch that changes the digest or `kit/superseded_decisions.json`.
tasks.acceptance: `python3 scripts/check_decision_digest.py` passes (it checks through the header's `Through` number); the task report shows the range taken and the command measuring it at no more than 300,000 bytes of entries; `python3 scripts/gen_prompts.py --check` passes after regeneration; the Opus review samples 30 rule lines and 30 task-scoped entries (all, when fewer) against their entries, finds none that misstates a choice, and checks every pair this task added to `kit/superseded_decisions.json`.

Fake data only (BUILD_BRIEF.md:66, PRIV-019): every persona's name, phone (555-0100 to 555-0199), email (example.com) and street comes from the fixture generator, and no real number, key or person is ever used; signing secrets and test keys are read the way T129's sandbox mode reads its credentials (from the build environment's secrets, never printed, logged or committed); an entry point whose secret this session cannot reach runs on the local lane only and the run log says so; `docs/phase2/money-war-game.md` records the jobs, the totals by entry type and the reconciliation result. On the test site the AI-008 switch is on during the money run and the rounds, so real Claude calls are made on fake data from the test project's Console key (T137's), and the campaign's AI spend is capped at $40 in all (a test-project daily AI-call cap, AI-021, of 600 calls, and the Console spend limit Casey set at the account checkpoint, whichever is lower); outbound texts use Twilio's test credentials and magic numbers only, so no real phone receives anything (BUILD_BRIEF.md:190). The money runs cover the pentest matrix's MONEY-01 to MONEY-05 and HOOK-02 to HOOK-04 cases (`docs/reviews/war-games-inputs/2026-11-09-pentest-matrix.md`) or state the skip (D-2350).
tasks.acceptance: At least 60 jobs run to a confirmed pick and charge in Stripe test mode, covering every tier edge, a free first win, a $0 repeat customer, each refund path and a dispute; `python3 -m wargames reconcile` reports zero differences between the ledger, Stripe test mode, the owner portal's money view and every statement CSV, to the cent, and `tests/wargames/test_reconcile.py` proves it reports a planted one-cent difference, a missing refund and a charge with no ledger row; the counts and totals are in `docs/phase2/money-war-game.md`.

tasks.title: AI-call budgets per conversation and per job, and no AI call before the area check
tasks.goal: Credit-drain defense for the war games (D-1154): AI-021's global daily cap stays, and below it AI-028's per-step budgets apply: no AI call before the consent text and the area check; 2 readings per inbound message, 1 reword per bank question (at most 8), 1 follow-up, card and project file 1 each plus 1 per EDIT (at most 3), 4 concept prompts, 2 screening calls a photo for at most 3 photos; backstops of 40 calls per conversation per Arizona day and 60 per job, with the card call always reserved so no budget lands on it; a verified web-chat session shares its phone's budget and an unverified one makes no call; quote reads 3 per business per job, outside the job's budget; only the first 1,600 characters of a scrubbed message are sent, while the AI-off card keeps her full scrubbed words. Past a budget the step runs on the AI-off path (INT-021) with nothing said and an `ai.call_stat` row with outcome `budget`; `models::calls_today` (`app/ai/src/models.rs`) excludes `budget` rows as it excludes `daily_cap` rows, so refused calls never use up the AI-021 cap. `IntakeCall` carries the conversation, job, step and (for quote reads) business it is for; the caller in `intake` passes them; the budgets are settings in `AiConfig`; the migration adds the `budget` outcome and the conversation, job, step and business columns to `ai.call_stat`. The global daily cap (AI-021, D-811) becomes an atomic admission: before the provider call, one statement reserves a slot for this Arizona day (a counter row per day updated with `... WHERE used < cap RETURNING`, or an equivalent single-statement reservation) on its own short transaction, so concurrent calls past the cap never reach the transport; a retry of one logical call uses its reservation, an abandoned or timed-out reservation still counts for that day, and the `ai.daily_cap` alert is raised once a day under the same race (D-1757). No database connection or open transaction is held across an AI provider await (AI-029, D-2038): the entry the app calls takes the pool, reads the AI-008 switch and makes the admission and the budget reservations each on its own short connection and releases it, awaits the provider (up to AI-023's timeout, retries and backoff included) with no connection held, then takes a connection again to record the call. With no connection held, every AI-028 budget check is a single-statement reservation like the AI-021 admission (only while the budget has room), so concurrent readings of one message (a duplicate or replayed webhook) cannot pass its 2-reading limit, the 1-reword limit or the per-day and per-job backstops together; a refused reservation makes no call and records outcome `budget`. Intake has no caller that applies a reading yet (`app/intake/src/question_bank.rs` calls only `accept_question`), so this task builds the first one in `app/intake/src/service.rs`: it reads one inbound message through the gated `read_intake` and applies the reading only if the step is still current on the new connection, which means the conversation has no inbound message and no `intake.intake_answer` row newer than the message the call was made for; otherwise the reading is recorded and discarded. Calling that function from the text and web-chat paths is T299's (IC-23, D-2065); the AI writing calls are IC-53's (no owner yet). `app/ai/src/switch.rs` (the gated `read_intake`) is this task's for that change. Other tasks' tests call `read_intake` with a `&mut PgConnection` (`app/ai/src/tests/adapter_calls.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/ai_zero_retention.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/prop_prompt_injection.rs`) and are not this task's to change: keep that form compiling for them as a thin wrapper that no app code calls. AI-029's other half, the inbound-text webhook committing before any AI call, is T299's, which wires the AI reading into the text path (IC-23, D-2065); that path makes no AI call yet. Ordering only: runs after T370, which changes one call in `app/intake/src/service.rs` (D-2703); its migration is `0210_ai_call_budget.sql` (V9, D-2707). Plan change D-3675: the migration is numbered 0209 (it was 0202; D-3881 moved it up one more, so T527's 0208 fits before it; D-3675 made it 0204, D-3722 moved it up one more, D-3750 one more, after T470's `0207_messaging_email_lease.sql`, D-3753 one more, after T480's `0208_messaging_spanish_switch.sql`, and D-3779 one more, because T486 took `0190_catalog_switched_on.sql` and every queued migration from 0190 up moved up one) because T456's `0205_picks_hold_away.sql` and `0206_businesses_away_busy.sql` run before this task in the serial order (`scripts/validate_tasks.py` V9). Plan change D-3883: this task's migration moved up one, to `0210_ai_call_budget.sql`, for T529's `0197_payments_refund_owner.sql` (V9); earlier numbers in this goal are history. Plan change D-4292: this task's migration moves to `migrations/0212_ai_call_budget.sql` for T645's `0210_messaging_web_chat_optout.sql` and `0211_intake_web_chat_language.sql`, which run earlier (V9); earlier numbers in this goal are history. Plan change D-4310: this task's migration moves to `migrations/0213_ai_call_budget.sql` for T653's `0212_licensing_btr_typed_unchecked.sql`, which runs earlier (V9); earlier numbers in this goal are history. Plan change D-4727: this task's migration moves to `migrations/0216_ai_call_budget.sql` for T729's `0215_update_email_choice.sql`, which runs earlier (V9); earlier numbers in this goal are history.

tasks.title: server and intake: the AI client built once per process and the AI reading called from texts and web chat
tasks.goal: IC-23's second half (D-2065): T236 builds the first intake caller of the AI reading (in `app/intake/src/service.rs`, through the gated `read_intake` taking the pool, with no connection held across the provider await, AI-029) and T298 the AI endpoint settings and the real Claude client, but nothing builds the client in a running process (`app/server/src/main.rs` and `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs` build no AI client today) or calls the reading from a homeowner's text or web chat, so the app would run AI-off for ever and the war games would never exercise the AI. (1) In `app/server/src/ai_client.rs`, build from the settings one `ai::api::AdapterTransport` over T298's client (one reused HTTP client) with its `ai::api::AiConfig` (the AI-023 reply budget T296 set, the AI-024 model, the AI-021 cap), once per process at start-up and shared by reference: in the web process, and in the worker if the text path's AI turn runs there (below); a settings error stops start-up naming the key, except T298's AI-off endpoint in live (no key set), with which the process starts, every step takes the AI-off path with no request made, and one high owner alert and one log line name the missing setting, never a value (D-2065); with no AI keys in dev and ci it is the stand-in; start-up makes no AI call. (2) The text path: in `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs` the webhook's transaction commits its durable record of the text before any AI call is made for it and never awaits the AI inside it (AI-029's webhook half, which T236 left to this task); the AI turn then runs off that transaction, either in the request after the commit or in a `core.task` queued in that transaction and run by the worker. Choose, log the reason in `docs/decisions.md`, and make sure a process stopped between the commit and the turn never loses the step (at worst it is asked on the AI-off path). The homeowner's wait is end to end: if the worker runs the turn, the queue and poll wait before it counts inside AI-023's 3-second reply budget (the AI call gets only what is left, and none left means the AI-off path at once) and inside the time to the next question that T234 and T297 measure, never only the AI call's own time. The AI-008 case through the real inbound route needs the route to know its environment: use the `Environment` T317 adds to the route's state (`Webhooks` in `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs`, set from the settings in `main.rs`; D-2206) and pass it to the gated entry; add no other field to `Webhooks`, since the done tests that build it are T317's (D-2206). The turn (`app/intake/src/ai_turn.rs`) calls T236's caller at each step of the INT-043 order that makes an AI call as the code then stands (the intake reading today) and sends the next step through the outbox: the one the applied reading leads to, or the fixed question-bank question at once (INT-021, INT-039) when the AI-008 switch is off, the AI-023 budget runs out, an AI-028 budget or the AI-021 cap refuses the call, or the reading fails or is discarded; steps that make no AI call never wait on one. (3) The web-chat path (T103's `app/intake/src/web_chat.rs` and `app/site/src/chat.rs`): no AI call before the session's phone code is verified (AI-021); after it, the same turn, the page showing the next question within the reply budget (AI-023). On both paths only `ScrubbedText` reaches `ai` (AI-004), no call is made before the consent text went and the ZIP and area check passed (AI-028), and no database connection or open transaction is held while the AI is awaited (AI-029). The AI writing calls (reword, follow-up, card, project file; D-990) are not this task's: IC-53 tracks them. Update `app/server/CLAUDE.md`, `app/intake/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/architecture.md` (shared), and name in the hand-in the commit and the tests that close IC-23 for the next plan change. Plan change D-4292: this task now depends on T645 (the web chat's opt-out words, INT-038 stop and stored first-message language) and T646 (the chat's client IP for the new-request limit). In `chat_message` keep T645's order: the opt-out check first, then the 911 check and the under-18 stop, and only then the AI turn; no AI call is made for a chat message that opted out or that the INT-038 stop closed, and the turn uses the session's stored language. Plan change D-4326: ordered after T656, which first changes `app/site/src/chat.rs`'s failed-submit page (the focused error summary, `aria-invalid` and the refilled words and number, A11Y-030); this task keeps them. Plan change D-4360: the INT-043 order is walked by `app/intake/src/order_dispatch.rs` (T671 to T675), whose trade check uses the stored keyword reading (the AI-off path). The dispatcher runs inside `reply_in`'s and the webhook's transaction, so it never awaits the AI: at a step that makes an AI call it hands the step to this task's AI turn (after the commit or in the queued task chosen above, AI-029) and takes the turn's result as the step's answer when it lands; this task owns that file after T675 and runs after it. Plan change D-4360: T672's dispatcher rebuilds the question bank's position on each text by replaying the stored answers keyed on their question IDs; an AI follow-up or reworded question must be stored under its own question ID so the replay stays in step with the AI on.

TD-PRIV-21 cases here: sign-in by phone and texted code, a number not on file getting the same answer as one on file; the portal home shows only her own record; the texts-off switch puts her number on the suppression list at once; another homeowner's session, a business or owner session and none each get a 4xx with a link to `/h/sign-in` and no detail on these routes; every response `no-store`; a cross-site `POST` or a wrong CSRF token is refused, changes nothing and is logged as a security event; a sign-in code send past `admit_code_send`'s limit (an unknown number too) sends nothing and a code check past `admit_code_try`'s limit calls no Verify. (1) `app/server/src/homeowner_portal.rs` builds them: sign-in by phone and texted code (SEC-008), a 30-day session per device; a number not on file gets the same answer as one on file; the portal home, the texts-off switch (one suppression entry at once, CON-035), "Download my data" with only her own items (PRIV-031), the delete or copy request and its code step; none or another realm's session gets a 4xx with a link to `/h/sign-in` and no detail; every response `no_store` (SEC-034); every `POST` passes `refuse_cross_site` and the CSRF check, a refusal a security event; merged in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs`. (2) Tests: `app/server/tests/homeowner_portal_route.rs` (TD-PRIV-21) and `tests/e2e/homeowner_portal_served.spec.ts`, the code computed from the stand-in Verify's rule as TD-BIZ-42 does. Every page's `PAGE_STATES` entry goes in the shared `tests/a11y/page_states.ts` (D-1239, D-1788) and its rows in `docs/architecture.md` section 13 are marked `yes` once T284 has added the table. Update the `server` and `portals` `CLAUDE.md` files, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md`. The sign-in and data-code sends call `portals::api::admit_code_send` first (the IP, then her contact when on file, so an unknown number spends the IP limit and sends nothing) and their code checks `admit_code_try` (D-1951; fourth external audit F12, D-2206). The data-request code step also offers "Send the code again", served through T346's `resend_request_code` (behind `admit_code_send` like every send), because a request's code challenge lives 10 minutes while the request stays open 30 days (D-2348). The homeowner sign-in and data-request functions take the router's `&PgPool`, not a connection, after T346 (D-2349): the routes pass the pool and hold no connection of their own across those calls. Its routes pass T348's doors unchanged: `tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs` classifies each and `app/server/tests/door_matrix.rs` probes each `yes` row of `docs/architecture.md` section 13 over HTTP (D-2440); this task edits neither, and a route whose path parameter the probe cannot fill is reported, not worked around. The vault and ID secret are the webhooks' (`inbound_text::Webhooks`, `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs:146`, `:148`). The Verify client is a new optional `RouterParts` builder that only `main.rs` and this task's own tests pass; without it a code send sends nothing and answers the same page, and a code check calls nothing and answers the wrong-code page, never a 5xx (D-4173: `app/server/tests/door_matrix.rs:460` to `:465` require an admitted `POST` to answer below 500, and `POST /h/sign-in/code` is a sign-in door every actor passes; `route_wiring.rs` and `door_matrix.rs` pass no Verify part). `route_wiring.rs` and `door_matrix.rs` pass no new part. (4) `GET /h/my-data` answers a file, so it gets a reasoned `NOT_PAGES` line in the shared `tests/a11y/fixtures.ts`, not a `PAGE_STATES` entry; each `POST` checks CSRF before the realm and the realm before parsing required fields (`app/server/tests/door_matrix.rs:418` to `:441`, `:512`). Plan fix D-4025 (T307 attempt 1 stopped on a plan gap): `server` may not name any `privacy::api` plaintext read (`tests/security/tests/vault_readers.rs:19`, `:23`; the runtime refusal at `app/privacy/src/api.rs:247`), and the suppression list is keyed by her number (`app/messaging/src/optout.rs:289`), which only `portals` holds (`OnFile::phone` is crate-private, `app/portals/src/homeowner_portal.rs:97`). So this task also owns `app/portals/src/homeowner_portal.rs` and adds one associated function on the already-exported `HomeFacts`, `HomeFacts::read(db, vault, proof, spanish) -> Result<Option<Self>, VaultError>`, mirroring `OnFile::read` (`None` when no phone is on file): `privacy::api::read_own_contact` with her `HomeownerSessionProof` for `Field::Phone` and `Field::Address` only (SEC-046, PRIV-021), `phone_last4` the number's last four digits, `address` as read, `texts_on` from the new `held_messages.rs` suppression reader called inside `portals` with that number, and `spanish` as `server` passes it: `OnFile::contact()` to `intake::api::conversations_of_contact` (`app/intake/src/api.rs:183`, oldest first), her latest request through `intake::api::conversation` (`app/intake/src/service.rs:778`, re-exported at `app/intake/src/api.rs:124`), `spanish` when its `language` is `"es"` (`ConversationRow::language`, CON-026), `false` when she has no request. The suppression reader derives the list's digests itself with `privacy::api::normalize_phone` and `Vault::blind_index(IndexPurpose::HomeownerPhone, ..)`, as the private `digests` in `app/messaging/src/optout.rs:419` does; this small re-derivation is accepted (D-4025) because `optout.rs` is owned by T321, which is queued and can run beside T307. The reader answers an error (`OutboxError::BadPhone` or `OutboxError::Database`, as `digests` does when no digest can be computed), never "not listed", so `HomeFacts::read` fails and the home page shows its error state, not "texts on". `held_messages.rs` carries an in-crate round-trip test: `messaging::api::suppress` on a fake number, then the new reader answers texts off for it (and on for another number), so a drift from `optout.rs`'s digests fails the build. The line budget (550) holds: the reader and its test add about 40 lines. `server` names no vault read and never holds her number or address beyond the rendered page; no allow-list or test changes, and `app/portals/src/api.rs` is unchanged. Its in-crate test proves another homeowner's proof never reads her facts and `Debug` prints none of them (PRIV-016). Budget: 550 lines (D-3967).

tasks.title: picks, businesses and portals: Twilio Verify's "too many tries" is a cooldown, never an error page
tasks.goal: Nov 11 vendor-double review batch 4, F10 (callers' half; D-2769; PICK-013, SEC-004, SEC-008, BIZ-002, TXT-038). A Verify resend within the code's 10-minute life reuses the pending verification and its check attempts, so after the app allows a new code's tries Twilio can answer a check with 60202 (HTTP 429, too many attempts), and a send with 60203; the app counts tries per code row (`CODE_TRIES`, `app/picks/src/rules.rs:13`; `app/portals/src/business_auth.rs:88`) and maps any check error to `PicksError::Verify` (`app/picks/src/service.rs:790`), so the homeowner or business sees an error, not "try again in 15 minutes". After T131 (whose adapter returns a typed too-many-tries error) and the queued owners of these files: each caller (`app/picks/src/service.rs` and `app/picks/src/email_code.rs` for the pick code, `app/businesses/src/identity.rs` for the identity code, `app/portals/src/business_auth.rs` for sign-in) maps that error to its own cooldown (`CodeCheck::CoolingDown(at + COOLDOWN)` for the pick code; the existing lock-out of the other two), which outlasts the 10-minute verification so the next send starts a fresh one; any other adapter error keeps today's answer. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/verify_max_tries.rs` against the served stand-in (T131's faithful attempts): three wrong tries, a resend, then two more wrong tries; the third check after the resend (Twilio's sixth attempt on that verification, 60202) answers the cooldown, not an error (fails before the fix), for each of the three flows. Update the `picks`, `businesses` and `portals` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`. Plan change D-3999: it follows T564, which also edits `app/picks/src/service.rs` and `app/picks/src/email_code.rs`. Plan change D-4338 (night spot review of the business side and quotes on `main` d662af7e5, confirmed in a second pass and re-verified on `main` 9aeca6f95): (quotes 3; SEC-014, D-2206) `notice_post` (`app/portals/src/business_auth.rs:633` to `:663`) sends a sign-in link with `send_one` and never runs `admit_sign_in_link` (per IP and per business), which only `server`'s `SignInMailer::admitted` (`app/server/src/business_signin.rs:230` to `:247`) calls for the sign-in form, so anyone holding a valid notice URL can send the member about 480 sign-in emails a day from the shared daily limit (only `LINKS_PER_LIFE`, `:779`, caps it). This task now owns `app/server/src/business_signin.rs`: the `SignInMail` trait (`app/portals/src/business_auth.rs:136`) gains a provided method (a default body, documented as answering `true`) that admits a notice link's request for the notice's business and the client IP, so the ten test implementors of the trait (in `app/server/tests/`, `tests/integration/tests/` and `tests/security/tests/`) compile unchanged; only the server's mailer overrides it, with its existing `admitted` (`business_signin.rs:230` to `:247`); `notice_post` calls it before `send_one`, and when it refuses, shows the same "check your email" page a sent link shows and sends nothing, as the sign-in form already does on a refusal (`business_signin.rs:271` to `:275`), so nothing reveals the refusal. Tests in the new `app/server/tests/notice_signin_limit.rs` (TD-SEC-78), fake data only, through the assembled router: notice-link sign-in requests from one IP past the per-IP limit, and for one business past the per-business limit, each answer the same page as a sent link while no new row reaches `messaging.email_outbox` (nothing is sent); one under the limits queues exactly one sign-in email; the sign-in form's limits are unchanged. Ordered after T121, the other queued owner of `business_auth.rs` (already a dependency through its deps).

Fix: `final_pick` and "Send a new code" call `admit_code_send(pool, (ip, None), (now, threshold))` and "Finish my pick" calls `admit_code_try(pool, (ip, None), now)`, with the client IP from `ClientIpPolicy`, each before any Verify call; a refusal shows the existing daily-cap line and sends nothing. After T441 (the last earlier owner of `pick_flow.rs`, D-3497). Tests in `tests/integration/tests/pick_code_limits.rs` (TD-SEC-63): 11 code sends from one IP across different jobs give exactly one refusal and no eleventh send; tries over the per-IP limit are refused before Verify; another IP is unaffected. On a send, this file's own query on `portals.login_link` (as `action_links.rs:315` reads it) looks up the signed-in member's records for the current bucket and the two before it (each binding's `token_sha256`, `member_id`, `expires_at` after now): a live, unused one is reused without resetting its tries, whatever token the request sent or left out; `used_at` is set both by a right code (`use_link`) and by tries running out (`use_up_link`), and the two are told apart by a `portals.code_try` row of that record with `outcome = 'right'` (`migrations/0167_portals_code_tries.sql:20`, `:24`; the app role may SELECT it, `:33`); a live one used up by 5 wrong tries (no `right` row) refuses the send until it expires, because Verify still holds that code (D-2348: truly 5 tries per code); the current bucket's record used by a right code means the member is still within the 5-minute step-up, and the page says so and sends nothing; only when none of these exists does it mint the current bucket's record with its own `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (token_sha256) DO NOTHING` on `portals.login_link` (not `models::insert_link`, whose plain insert fails on the UNIQUE `token_sha256`) and then reads the record again, so of two simultaneous sends minting the same bucket the losing one reuses the winner's record (and its one send) and never answers 500 (a step-up passes for 5 minutes, so a member never needs a second record in the bucket of a right code). Every send also passes the SEC-014 per-IP and per-member limits, and is reserved and recorded with `reserve_code_send` and `finish_code_send` (`portals.code_send`, `migrations/0167_portals_code_tries.sql:14`; a reused record whose code was sent sends nothing again, as business sign-in sends once per link); (b) a check is refused before Verify is called unless the same lookup finds a live, unused record of the signed-in member whose send is `sent` (`code_sent`); (c) each try is reserved with `reserve_try` before the Verify call, capped at 5 per record (`portals.code_try`, `:20`), and finished with `finish_try`; the fifth wrong try uses the record up (`use_up_link`); (d) a right code uses the record with `models::use_link` on the same transaction as `businesses::api::record_step_up`, so a code confirms one step-up once. The server gets Verify through a new optional builder `RouterParts::with_step_up` in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` (as `with_sign_in`, `lib.rs:111`), which `main` (shared) sets from `Settings` as `ServedSignIn::from_settings` builds its Verify client (`app/server/src/business_signin.rs:109`); without it (the done route tests, dev and `Ci`) the step-up routes are still merged and the code step sends nothing and answers below 500, so `door_matrix.rs` and `route_wiring.rs` need no change. TD-SEC-64 is amended in place to match. The cites `email_verification.rs:200` and `:305`, `team.rs:339` and `:384`, `backup_address.rs:256`, `lib.rs:111` and `business_auth.rs:186` to `:211` above are now `:212`, `:317`, `:429`, `:474`, `:280`, `:124` and `:192` to `:219`. tasks.title: messaging and server: the worker task that sends queued emails through the email provider
tasks.goal: Plan change D-3750 (D-3263, D-3186; SEC-025, OPS-038, SEC-018, PRIV-016, BIZ-019): emails stored in `messaging.email_outbox` by `queue_email` (`app/messaging/src/email.rs:343`) and by the business notice sender (job cards, pick and money notices, `app/messaging/src/business_notices.rs`), the receipts and the homeowner emails are never sent: only the account mailers call `send_email` (`app/messaging/src/email.rs:454`), for their own row, and no task sends a queued row to a provider (D-3263 parked T222's email checks for it). Only the account mailers store a credential mark in place of a credential (`LINK_MARK`, `app/messaging/src/signin_mail.rs`; T468's `CODE_MARK`) and add it only on the way to the provider; business notices store real per-recipient sign-in links in their bodies (`app/messaging/src/business_notices.rs:24`, `:389`), so a stored notice is itself a credential for its recipient. (1) `migrations/0207_messaging_email_lease.sql` (headed `messaging`): `messaging.email_outbox` gains `claimed_at timestamptz` (the drain's lease) and the status `dropped` (a row never to be sent; its subject and bodies are cleared in the same statement, as a sent row's are, so the status CHECKs extend to it); no old migration is edited. Its number follows T456's `0205` (T470 depends on T456 for that order only, V9; each moved up one by D-3779) and T236's migration moves to `0208`. (2) `app/messaging/src/email_due.rs` (new; exported through the shared `api.rs` and `lib.rs`): the `messaging.email_due` worker task. Each run, at the worker clock's now, leases a bounded batch, oldest first, in one short committed statement under `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` that sets `status = 'sending'` and `claimed_at = now` together: it takes `queued` rows whose `not_before` passed and whose `claimed_at` is null or stale, plus `sending` rows only when their lease is stale (`claimed_at` older than `STALE_AFTER`, 5 minutes, as `outbox_sender`'s, or unset 5 minutes past `not_before`), because `claim_email` itself takes `queued` or `sending` (`app/messaging/src/models.rs:764`) and a non-429 provider error leaves a row `sending` (`app/messaging/src/email.rs:494`). A row a worker leased is therefore `sending` with a fresh lease, which no second lease takes, whether the two runs overlap or follow one another, so each row gets one provider call per lease, under its stored idempotency key (SEC-018: a retry after a stale lease is the same email to Resend). `app/messaging/src/models.rs` (owners done): `hold_email` (`:819`), which puts a row back to `queued`, also clears `claimed_at` and never touches a `dropped` row (`status NOT IN ('sent', 'dropped')`), so a held row is leased again once its `not_before` passes. Each leased row is then sent through `send_email` with the provider, email key and `DailyLimit` it is handed (T469's `EmailProvider`), so OPS-038's bulk hold and the daily quota (SEC-025) hold as for every other email. It takes only templates no other code sends: never a template whose own handler calls `send_email` (the sign-in link, the email code, the welcome and phone-stopped, the coverage notice and the business event emails), listed by template ID in one constant; and, as a backstop, a leased row whose subject or body holds `LINK_MARK` or `CODE_MARK` is `dropped` with one High alert naming the row ID only and never sent, so a literal mark never reaches anyone. A homeowner row's address is read through `EmailTo::Homeowner` (the vault, under `messaging`'s send grant); a business row's comes from a resolver trait the composition supplies, which answers the address, or `Gone` when the row's business has left (BIZ-051: leaving stops all notices) or its mailbox is no longer a current member's (a removed member, SEC-024), and a `Gone` row is `dropped` unsent, since it holds that person's sign-in link. With no provider handed in, a run does nothing: it leases, sends and marks nothing and queues no next run; with one, it queues its next run, as `send_due` does (`app/messaging/src/outbox_sender.rs`). No transaction is open during the provider call, and no address, body or key is logged (PRIV-016). (3) `app/privacy/src/business_contacts.rs`: `BusinessPurpose::Notice` ("the business notice and card emails: the address only"), in `ALL`, with its audit label (SEC-047). (4) `app/server/src/email_due.rs` (new): the resolver (the current-member and left-business checks through `businesses::api`, then `read_business_mailbox` under `BusinessPurpose::Notice` on a bare connection) and the handler, registered in `worker_registry` (the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs`) always, with T469's provider when it exists and with none otherwise, so `tests/integration/tests/task_registry.rs` (TD-OPS-36, built from the dev stand-in pairs with no Resend key) passes unchanged; the first run is queued at start only when a provider exists. (5) Tests, fake data only, in `tests/integration/tests/email_due.rs` against PostgreSQL with a recording `EmailAdapter`: a queued homeowner email and a queued business notice email each go once to the right address; two workers' leases over the same rows, run both at once and one after the other (the second after the first committed its lease but before its send finished), leave the adapter with exactly one call per row; a `sending` row with a fresh lease is not taken and one with a stale lease is, under the same key; a row `hold_email` put back to `queued` has no lease and goes once its `not_before` passes, and a `dropped` row is never held or sent; a row whose `not_before` is later waits; a bulk row waits above the hold share while a job card still goes; a refused send goes on a later run under the same key; a row of a self-sending template is never taken; a row holding `LINK_MARK` or `CODE_MARK` is dropped with one alert and never sent; a notice to a removed member or a business that left is dropped unsent; with no provider nothing changes and no next run is queued; no address appears in any log line. Update `app/messaging/CLAUDE.md`, `app/privacy/CLAUDE.md`, `app/server/NOTES.md` and `docs/decisions.md`. Plan change D-3883: this task's migration moved up one, to `0207_messaging_email_lease.sql`, for T529's `0197_payments_refund_owner.sql` (V9); earlier numbers in this goal are history. Plan change D-3889 (Fable's pre-claim check, Nov 16, 2026): a leased row whose address read answers `EmailError::NoAddress` (`app/messaging/src/email.rs:536` to `:542`) is `dropped`, not left `sending` to be leased again forever; `messaging::api::unsent_business_mailboxes` (`app/messaging/src/api.rs:290`, the shared file) gains `AND status <> 'dropped'`, so a dropped row keeps no removed member's address; if `schedule_start` (`app/server/src/bin/worker.rs:74`, 47 body lines) would pass 50 lines, this task moves its calls into a helper first. `app/server/CLAUDE.md` is at its 8,192-byte cap, so server notes go in `app/server/NOTES.md`. If the change outgrows 600 lines, the natural split is the `messaging` drain versus the `server` resolver and handler: report it. Plan change D-4196 (Casey's outside audit of Nov 17, 2026, finding 1, verified on `main` 2f2fa8c): a row of a self-sending template that `send_email` held on a 429 or a full daily quota is never sent today: `models::hold_email` (`app/messaging/src/models.rs:812`, called from `app/messaging/src/email.rs:539` and `:573`) puts it back to `queued` with a later `not_before` and `waiting_for` set to `provider_limit` or `daily_limit` (the column's only values, `migrations/0089_messaging_retries_email.sql:49`), its own handler turns `EmailSent::Waiting` into a `HandlerError` (`app/businesses/src/account_emails.rs:165`, `app/businesses/src/coverage_notice.rs:138`, `app/businesses/src/notice_emails.rs:608`), and `core::tasks` gives up after 5 tries with a 30-second doubling backoff (`app/core/src/tasks.rs:43`, `:164`), about 8 minutes, long before the midnight-UTC reset (`next_reset`, `email.rs:462`). So the drain also leases a self-sending template's row whose `waiting_for` is not null once its `not_before` passes, and sends it once like any other leased row (a race with that template's own handler retry is the same email under the same idempotency key, SEC-018). A held row of the sign-in link or the email code still holds `LINK_MARK` or `CODE_MARK` and is `dropped` unsent with no alert, because its link or code has expired; the High alert stays for a marked row of any other template. T204's owner alert emails (`owner_alert_push` and `owner_daytime_push`, `app/messaging/src/alert_emails.rs:44`, `:46`) join the self-sending list and are never taken, held or not: their address is the owner alert address, not a member's mailbox (the resolver would answer `Gone`), and `push_alerts` records a push only after its send (`alert_emails.rs:269`), so it tries them again itself. The coverage notice (OPS-041) is stored with the recipient `messaging::api::OWNER_INBOX` (`app/messaging/src/coverage_email.rs:29`, `:115`) and sent to the owner inbox setting (`app/businesses/src/coverage_notice.rs:135`), not to a member's mailbox: the server resolver answers the owner inbox address (the setting `run_coverage_notice` sends to) for a row whose recipient is `messaging::api::OWNER_INBOX`, never `Gone`, so a held coverage notice goes there once after its `not_before`. Add to `tests/integration/tests/email_due.rs`: a welcome row held with `daily_limit` is not taken before its `not_before` and goes once after it; a coverage notice row held with `daily_limit` goes once to the owner inbox after its `not_before`; a held sign-in link row is dropped unsent with no alert; an owner alert row is never taken. Cites now: `send_email` is `email.rs:501` (was `:454`), `hold_email` is `models.rs:812` (was `:819`). This adds about 40 lines; the budget stays at the 600-line cap for a build task, and D-3889's split still applies if the change outgrows it. Plan change D-4327 (night spot review of outgoing email, Nov 18, 2026, re-verified on `main` d662af7e5; round-1 review applied): a leased row never loops for ever and is never sent twice. `send_email` (`app/messaging/src/email.rs:501`; this task now owns `email.rs` for this change) turns every provider error but a 429 into `EmailError::Provider` and leaves the row `sending` (`:542`), so under the 5-minute stale lease a refused email would be sent again every 5 minutes for ever, and Resend keeps an idempotency key only 24 hours, so a retry later than that can deliver twice (SEC-018). (i) Answers are sorted by what they prove. A 400 or 422 is Resend refusing this one email: `send_email` marks the row `dropped` (subject and bodies cleared), raises one High `messaging.email_refused` alert naming the row ID only, and returns a new `EmailError::Refused`; it is never sent again. A 401, 403 or 404 is an account or setup fault (a bad or rotated key, an unverified domain), never a fault of the email: the row backs off as below, and one High `messaging.email_provider_setup` alert is raised through `ops::api::raise_kind_once`, so a wave of such answers opens one alert, not one per row. A 429 keeps today's hold. A 5xx, 408, 409 (Resend's idempotent request still in progress), timeout or connection error has an unknown outcome (the email may have gone): the row backs off as below. (ii) Backing off: the drain puts the row back to `queued` with `claimed_at` cleared and `not_before` raised by 1 minute doubling on each such answer in a row, capped at 60 minutes (`lease_count smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, added by migration 0207, counts them and only sets the delay; no number of leases ever drops a row; a successful send, a 400 or 422 drop, and a 429 or quota hold reset it to 0). (iii) Migration 0207 also adds `first_unsure_at timestamptz`: set once, to the time the unsure call began, never the time an answer came back: after a 5xx, 408, 409, timeout or connection error it is set to that lease's `claimed_at`, and when a stale `sending` lease is taken again (the crash case) the retaking statement sets `first_unsure_at = COALESCE(first_unsure_at, claimed_at)` from the old lease before it overwrites `claimed_at`; it is never cleared, `hold_email` included (a 429 or quota hold proves only that the held call sent nothing, not an earlier unsure one). A row whose `first_unsure_at` is 23 hours or more before now (inside Resend's 24-hour key window) is never handed to the provider again: the next run marks it `dropped` with one High `messaging.email_given_up` alert naming the row ID only. The expiry pass touches only rows the run would otherwise lease (`queued` rows whose `not_before` has passed), never a `sending` row under a fresh lease. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/email_due.rs`, with the recording adapter answering as planted: a 400 and a 422 each drop the row after one call with one alert and a later run makes no call; 500s on runs spread over 22 hours 59 minutes keep the row (backing off, never dropped, same key each call) and once `first_unsure_at` is 23 hours old the row is dropped with one alert and no call; a 409 and a timeout back off like a 500; a 401 on three rows backs all three off and opens one setup alert, and the rows go once the adapter answers 200; a row held on a 429 or the daily limit gets no `first_unsure_at`, and a held row that had one keeps it; a stale `sending` row whose lease began 23 hours before and is only retaken now is dropped with one alert and no provider call (its `first_unsure_at` is the old lease time); a 500 answer stores the lease time, not the answer time; a row answered only 401 whose `queued_at` is 72 hours old is dropped with one expiry alert and at 71 hours 59 minutes is not; a success after back-offs resets `lease_count`. tasks.title: Stand-ins (harness): sticky vendor faults for the J4 outage journey
tasks.goal: Plan change D-3844 (the overseer's pre-claim scout, Nov 15, 2026; D-492, D-2821): J4 (T119) needs failing vendors, but the stand-in server has no way to make them fail: `stand_ins/server.py`'s `ROUTES` (`:378` to `:410`) hold no fault control, the AI stand-in fails only on an `x-stand-in-fault` header (`:373`, `stand_ins/ai.py:214`) the app never sends, and `stand_ins/` is protected. (1) `stand_ins/server.py`: `POST /_stand_in/faults` (no credentials, like the other `/_stand_in/` paths) sets sticky faults, held in the server's state under its lock until changed: `twilio` `fail` (every message send answers a Twilio 500 error body and stores nothing) or `suspended` (every message send is refused with Twilio error 21606, HTTP 400, the body `stand_ins/twilio.py:137` already returns for a sending number Twilio no longer lets send, and stores nothing); `stripe` `unavailable` (every `/stripe/v1/` request answers a Stripe-shaped 503 and creates nothing) or `drop` (the connection is closed with no answer); `ai` `529` (every `/anthropic/v1/messages` request without its own `x-stand-in-fault` header answers as if it carried `529`); `null` clears one. `DELETE /_stand_in/faults` clears all and `GET /_stand_in/faults` shows them. An unknown vendor or value is a 400 that changes nothing; the `/_stand_in/` control routes, Verify, Resend and Lob never fail; `stand_ins/twilio.py`, `stripe.py` and `ai.py` are not changed (their existing error helpers and fault table are reused). (3) `tests/contract/test_stand_in_faults.py`: each fault answered as above with nothing stored while it holds, a cleared fault serving normally again, the header-driven AI faults unchanged, control routes unaffected, and an unknown value refused. No AI settings are added to `tests/e2e/webserver.ts`: no process builds an AI client before T299, whose stand-in default serves the end-to-end run once it does. Fake data only. tasks.title: server and site: a same-site web chat POST passes its CSRF check, and the request page says 18 or older (fix of T489)
tasks.goal:
Plan change D-4174 (the Opus triage of T594's attempt 1, Nov 17, 2026, checked on `main` f911c8f): T489's chat layer refuses every same-site `POST /request`, and the request page lacks CON-025's 18-or-older line, so T594's end-to-end spec cannot pass; this task fixes both in T489's files (T489 is done) and adds the route test that would have caught the first. (1) SEC-042: `posted_csrf` (`app/server/src/chat_codes.rs:186` to `:201`) re-reads the buffered body through `Request::builder()` with no method, so the rebuilt request is a `GET`, axum's `Form` reads a `GET`'s form from the query string (empty: the builder's URI is `/`), the posted `csrf` is always empty, `csrf_matches` (`app/portals/src/session.rs:327` to `:330`) is false and `check_token` (`chat_codes.rs:171` to `:172`) answers 403 with a `csrf_rejected` event to every `POST`, a right token included. The fix is `.method(Method::POST)` on that builder (`Method` is already imported, `:35`), nothing else in the layer: the order of checks (cross-site refusal outermost, then the token, `POST` only, D-4120 trap (a)), the 403 and its one event per refusal (SEC-048), the body limit, `no-store`, the pre-session cookie and the `ChatCsrf` hand-off stay as they are, and the refusal function is still not spelled `refused(` (D-4120 trap (b)). The bug fails closed: the empty string never equals the 64-hex token, so no forged or missing token was ever accepted, and after the fix a missing, empty, wrong or other-cookie token is still refused. (2) CON-025 (`docs/spec/consent.md:29`: "the start screen says the user must be 18 or older"; TD-CON-10, `docs/test-design.md:349`): `app/site/templates/request.html` shows the line `You must be 18 or older to use {{ brand }}.` (the `brand` already bound at `:10`) in its own `

` right after the English consent text (`:17`) and above the chat box, on every step, outside `lang="es"`; it is plain copy (no `data-fixed`: CON-025 fixes the fact, not the wording), so `scripts/check_copy.py` measures it and reports 0 problems; no Spanish copy is added (WEB-006 covers only the consent draft). Nothing else on the page changes, so the `/request` `PAGE_STATES` entries in `tests/a11y/page_states.ts` stay valid and are not edited, and `Ally` stays at 0 violations. (3) Why T489's tests missed it: `app/site/src/chat.rs`'s unit tests call `chat_routes` directly, without `server`'s guard (`chat.rs:524`); `app/server/tests/door_matrix.rs` only proves refusals (`probe_csrf`, `:1263`, a cross-site and a wrong-token `POST`) and accepts any answer below 500 for a Public `POST` with the actor's own token (`judge`, `:448`), so a 403 passed; `app/server/tests/route_wiring.rs` probes with a bodiless `PROBE` request. So this task adds `app/server/tests/web_chat_route.rs` (TD-SEC-72; fake data only, no real number, the router built with `build_router` and `RouterParts::from((None, None, None, None))` as `app/server/tests/business_signin_route.rs:142` to `:143` does, so no code is sent and the code step answers below 500, D-3744; security events counted from the captured log lines as `app/server/tests/owner_signin_route.rs:290` does): a `GET /request` sets the pre-session cookie, shows the token in the form's `csrf` field and shows the 18-or-older line before the form; a same-origin `POST /request` with that cookie, that token and a job message is not a 403, is `no-store`, records no `csrf_rejected` event and answers below 500 with the posted words in the page's chat list (the `

    ` T594's spec reads); the same `POST` with no `csrf` field, an empty one, a 64-zero token or the token of another pre-session cookie is a 403 with exactly one `csrf_rejected` event for `/request` and changes nothing; a cross-site `POST` (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`) with the right token is still a 403 with one event. Two traps in that test: (i) the accepted `POST` must carry what `chat.rs`'s `post` handler needs, or it answers 400 with no chat list: the form is `Posted` (`app/site/src/chat.rs:131` to `:141`, `deny_unknown_fields`, so no field outside `csrf`, `chat`, `message`, `g`, `said`, `step`, `words`, `number`, `code`), `chat` a 32-hex key not all zeros (`Turn::posted`, `:176` to `:188`), `message` a UUID (`Uuid::try_parse`, `:292` to `:295`), `step=message` and `words` that are not empty after scrubbing (fake job words with no name or number, `:318` to `:321`); (ii) `is_cross_site` (`app/portals/src/security.rs:334` to `:341`) treats a `POST` with neither `Sec-Fetch-Site` nor `Origin` as cross-site, so every same-site request in the test sends `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` (or an `Origin` of `https://` plus the request's `Host`), as `door_matrix.rs`'s `request` does (`:347` to `:379`); a refusal case differs from the accepted one only in its token or its site header. The test fails on `main` today (the first case) and passes with fix (1). `door_matrix.rs`, `route_wiring.rs`, `tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs`, `security_event_cap.rs` and `chat.rs` are not changed and still pass. tasks.title: Tests (harness): the PICK-046 email's no-amount check ignores the random link token (flaky test fix)
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4196 (a flaky test, not from the outside audit; it cost T479's attempt 1 on Nov 17, 2026; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:272`): `tests/integration/tests/pick_lapsed_email.rs:273` (T446, DONE; PICK-046) asserts `!plain.contains("190") && !plain.contains('$')` on an email body that also holds the homeowner's quote-page link `https://<domain>/q/<token>`, and the token is an HMAC-SHA256 in 64 hex characters over a random salt (`link_token`, `app/core/src/ids.rs:254`), so the check fails by chance whenever `190` turns up in it (62 places times 16 to the minus 3, about 1.5% of runs). Fix, keeping the check at least as strict: take the `/q/` token out of the body first (cut each `/q/` followed by 64 hex characters down to `/q/`; the test already checks the body starts with the link's prefix), then assert the rest holds no `190` and no `$`, so the fake quote's 190 dollars (19000 cents, `:119`) written anywhere in the words still fails the test, and assert the cut removed exactly one token, so the check cannot pass on a body whose link changed shape. Asserting only `$190` or `190.00` was rejected: it would let a bare `190` through. tasks.title: privacy: the inbound email signature check refuses an out-of-range timestamp without overflow
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4196 (Casey's outside audit of Nov 17, 2026, finding 4, verified on `main` 2f2fa8c): `privacy::reader`'s Svix check `verify` (`app/privacy/src/reader.rs:276`) parses the unauthenticated `svix-timestamp` header and, before the signature check, computes `(now.as_second() - sent).abs()` (`:281` to `:282`); a stamp of `i64::MIN`, or far enough from now, overflows: a panic in debug, test and CI builds, wrapped arithmetic in release (the release profile sets no `overflow-checks`), where one stamp, `now.as_second().wrapping_add(i64::MIN)`, gives a gap of `i64::MIN` whose `abs()` wraps to a negative number, so it is not over the tolerance and passes on to the signature check. No production route reaches it yet (`read_inbound_email`'s only caller is `tests/integration/tests/read_inbound.rs`). Fix as the sister check `fresh` does (`app/adapters/src/signatures.rs:343` to `:350`): `now.as_second().checked_sub(sent).map(i64::unsigned_abs)`, and `None` or a gap over `WEBHOOK_TOLERANCE_SECS` (300) is `InboundError::Stale` (PRIV-026, SEC-016); nothing else in the file changes. Tests in the new `app/privacy/src/tests/webhook_stamp.rs` (one `mod` line in the shared `tests/mod.rs`; `verify` may become `pub(crate)` for it): the stamps `i64::MIN`, `i64::MAX`, `-1` and `now.as_second().wrapping_add(i64::MIN)` are `Stale` and nothing panics, a stamp 300 seconds away goes on to the signature check and one 301 seconds away is `Stale`. Update the `privacy` notes and `docs/decisions.md`.

DESIGN_SPEC now allows a polish layer within fixed limits: the layered `paper-shadow` and `paper-lift` (`docs/design/DESIGN_SPEC.md:44`, `:77`), 20 px cards with 12 px inner boxes (`:76`), tabular figures and `text-wrap: pretty` (`:62`, `:70`), one italic serif accent a page (`:53`), small capital labels with +0.05em tracking (`:68`), one `aria-hidden` arrow inside a primary button (`:105`), a CSS-drawn external-link mark after the ROC, Google and Yelp links (`:109`), hover, press and motion rules (`:123`, `:124`, `:128`), the speed limits (`:129`) and the checks (`:152` to `:154`); WEB-029 (motion, depth, arrow) and WEB-030 (speed) are the requirements. Limits every polish task keeps (WEB-029, WEB-030): CSS only, no script added to any site page; movement is `transform` alone and no element that holds text starts below full opacity (so axe's contrast, the design-token test and the first-screen measurements see the resting page); entrance motion only on the first render of the quote page's cards (D-4252 dropped the home page's), at most 12 px, staggered with `:nth-child` (the CSP allows no `style` attribute, SEC-013) and capped so the sixth card and every later one share the last delay, every animation's end time (delay plus duration times iterations) within 900 ms; no view transition between pages (D-4246 dropped it); hover and press under 350 ms; no animation repeats more than 3 times; every animation and transition inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so A11Y-009's test (`tests/a11y/reflow_spacing.spec.ts`) passes unchanged; colors only as section 2's tokens (shadows as `rgba(30,41,38,a)` or `rgba(36,88,73,a)`, the primary button's inner highlight as `rgba(255,255,255,a)`, no other hex), no font size under 16 px or in a unit other than px, no `linear-gradient(` (an axe incomplete on a gradient button would fail TD-A11Y-01), and no class name containing the words badge, pill, chip or tag (`docs/ai_smell.yaml`'s badge-or-pill rule is a `\b` match, so `quote-tag` fails; D-4246 declines chips and pills). Every word stays as it is: markup and classes change, text does not; capitals (`text-transform: uppercase`) never go on text a test reads through `innerText`, which returns the shown case (for example `tests/e2e/business_portal_served.spec.ts:114` and `tests/e2e/pick_flow.spec.ts:106`, whose page text must keep its case), and `scripts/check_copy.py`, `scripts/check_ai_smell.py` and every existing test that reads page text pass unchanged. T607 has brought `site.css` up to the reference V6; this task adds the polish on top, so the template tasks after it (T608 to T611) only add classes. (1) Tokens in `:root`: `--paper-shadow` and `--paper-lift` (section 2's new values), the primary button's edge, highlight and tinted shadow, the request box's focus glow, the corner radii (cards 20, inner boxes and controls 12, the 911 note 14), the press scale 0.975, the durations (150 ms color fade, under 350 ms hover and press, the entrance), and `--spring`, the `linear()` easing from Casey's brief (`linear(0, .0697 4.6%, .2533 9.6%, .5164 15.4%, .7547 21.4%, .9081 27.2%, .9927 33.2%, 1.0279 39.8%, 1.0297 46.6%, 1.0136 56.6%, 1.0012 70.4%, .9989 86%, 1)`). (2) Depth and type on T607's components: the layered shadows, 20 px cards with 12 px inner boxes, the primary button's highlight (`inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.14)`), drop and tinted shadow, the request textarea's focus glow (the `focus` ring stays 3:1 or more on it, section 2), tabular figures, `text-wrap: pretty`, the heading tracking of section 3, the price block's raised half-size `$` at 24 px or more, the `band` "In their words" panel, and the small-label and italic-accent classes. (3) Motion, all inside one `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` block, with no `@view-transition` (D-4246 dropped it): the press scale, the primary button's arrow nudge (3 px, `(hover: hover)` only), the lift for `a.card` only (a whole-card link; no reading card lifts), and a `rise` keyframe (transform only, at most 12 px) that runs only on an element carrying the class `rise`, with `:nth-child` delays of about 90 ms; outside the block nothing moves. The header stays not sticky (A11Y-026). (4) The italic accent's font: Gelasio 500 italic, the same SIL Open Font License family as the Gelasio files in `docs/design/fonts/` (whose `OFL-Gelasio.txt` covers it), taken with `npm pack @fontsource/gelasio@5.3.0` (a download, not a dependency: `package.json` does not change); before using it the task checks that the package's `package.json` says `"license": "OFL-1.1"` and that its `LICENSE` text equals `docs/design/fonts/OFL-Gelasio.txt` (stop and report if either differs), and records the tarball's npm `integrity` value and the font file's SHA-256 in its decision entry; its latin subset `files/gelasio-latin-500-italic.woff2` is copied unchanged as `gelasio-latin-500-italic.woff2`, stored in `docs/design/fonts/` and served from `app/site/static/fonts/` through `app/site/src/assets.rs`'s fixed list as `font/woff2` (D-3144: bytes compiled in, no `.route(` line), with a `@font-face` (`font-style: italic`, `font-display: swap`) and no metadata (the PII scanner passes); a unit test in `assets.rs`'s test module asserts that the served bytes equal `docs/design/fonts/gelasio-latin-500-italic.woff2` byte for byte. It is not preloaded. The small-label style (capitals through `text-transform: uppercase`, +0.05em tracking, 16 px or more) and the external-link mark (an `.out a::after` of about 0.6em, the class on the link's parent element drawn from `currentColor` top and right borders with a short diagonal, no `url()`, no image and no character in `content`, so `tests/a11y/design_tokens.spec.ts`'s fonts-only `url()` rule holds and the links' markup never changes) are classes the template tasks apply. (5) `tests/e2e/site_polish.spec.ts` fetches the served `/static/site/site.css` and fails when: its size is over 60 KB as bytes or its gzipped size (Node's `zlib.gzipSync`) is over 25 KB; any `@keyframes` changes a property other than `transform`; any `animation` or `transition` sits outside a `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` block; `@view-transition` appears at all; a transition lasts 350 ms or more; an entrance animation's delay plus duration passes 900 ms; any iteration count is `infinite` or above 3; or `linear-gradient(` appears; each with a planted stylesheet string that fails it. The site and portal pages that link the stylesheet today keep rendering: `tests/a11y/design_tokens.spec.ts` and the whole Ally suite pass unchanged with motion on. Plan change D-4252 (Fable's UI and accessibility review of the D-4246 tasks; Casey, Nov 17, 2026: "make it exceptional and meet all of the ADA requirements"): (a) the `rise` stagger is capped: `:nth-child(n+6)` shares the fifth delay, so with any number of cards every end time stays within 900 ms (`:128`), and `site_polish.spec.ts` fails a stylesheet whose `rise` delays have no such cap or whose largest delay plus duration passes 900 ms (planted case); card gaps never go under 16 px, so a rising card never overlaps its neighbour in `tests/a11y/reflow_spacing.spec.ts`'s overlap checks. (b) The size check is both measures (`:129`, WEB-030): the served `site.css` 60 KB or less as bytes and 25 KB or less through `zlib.gzipSync`, each with a planted case. (c) The home page's first-view weight check moves here from T612, so every task after this one is held to it: at 390 by 844 the bodies of every response until the load event (decoded, uncompressed) total 280 KB or less (`:129`), with a planted list of sizes that fails through the same sum. (d) Metric-matched fallback faces (`:53`): two `@font-face` blocks, a serif one from `local("Georgia"), local("Noto Serif")` and a sans one from `local("Arial"), local("Roboto")`, each with `size-adjust`, `ascent-override` and `descent-override` tuned to Gelasio 500 and DM Sans 400 (computed from the woff2 files' metrics; the figures go in the decision entry), named in the font stacks right after the web fonts; `local()` is not `url()`, so `tests/a11y/design_tokens.spec.ts`'s fonts-only `url()` rule holds; the first-screen run with every font request blocked is T612's. (e) Small details (`:70`): `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent` with the press scale as the touch feedback and `touch-action: manipulation` on buttons, `text-underline-offset: 0.18em` and `text-decoration-thickness: from-font` on links, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the business name and on typed text; no `content-visibility`. (f) (Casey, Nov 17, 2026, about 2:55 pm MST: "Do whatever fable says") one `@media (prefers-contrast: more)` block (`:47`): card, row and section edges take `field-edge` in place of `line`, `ink-soft` text takes `ink`, and every shadow drops; T612 checks it in the browser.

tasks.title: site: strong per-coding ETags with 304 revalidation, a one-year cache for the hash-pinned fonts, and gzip or Brotli for the stylesheet and the mark
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4252 (Fable's UI and accessibility review of the D-4246 tasks; Casey, Nov 17, 2026: "make it exceptional and meet all of the ADA requirements"). DESIGN_SPEC section 7's speed rule (`docs/design/DESIGN_SPEC.md:129`, WEB-030): site files are served with `public, max-age=3600` and no validator (`app/site/src/routes.rs`, the `asset` handler), and nothing is compressed, so a returning visitor fetches the fonts, the photo and the stylesheet again every hour, at full size; the long cache exists only for `/static/portals/` (`app/server/src/static_files.rs`, `LONG_CACHE`). This task: (1) `app/site/src/assets.rs` computes each listed file's SHA-256 once (the allowed `sha2` crate, `std::sync::LazyLock`). (2) Every answer of the `asset` handler carries a strong `ETag` that differs per content coding (`"<first 16 hex>"` for the plain bytes, `"<first 16 hex>-gzip"` and `"<first 16 hex>-br"` for the compressed ones), and a matching `If-None-Match` gets 304 with no body. (3) The addresses never change: `base.html`'s `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/site/site.css">` stays byte for byte as `app/site/src/routes.rs`'s own test asserts, and no template changes. The font files are cached `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, which is safe only because a font's name is fixed to its bytes: a unit test pins each font file's SHA-256 next to its name, so changing a font's bytes without a new name fails the build (`:129`); `site.css` keeps `public, max-age=3600` with its ETag, unchanged from today (D-3901: the one-hour cache together with the body stylesheet link made A11Y-030's autofocus run pass 96 of 96, and each alone still failed, so the stylesheet is never sent `no-cache`); the photos, the mark and the icons, which may change under the same name (the licensed photo included), are sent `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so a repeat visit costs a 304. (4) Compression for static files only, never a page (a compressed page holding a CSRF token invites a BREACH-style attack): enable tower-http's `compression-gzip` and `compression-br` features in the workspace `Cargo.toml` (tower-http is allowed; the features add transitive crates, so the task's decision entry records each new crate's purpose, license, `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` result, and if either fails the task stops with a plan gap) and wrap the `asset` service inside `site_routes()` in `app/site/src/routes.rs` in a `CompressionLayer` whose predicate admits `text/css` and `image/svg+xml`, adding `Vary: Accept-Encoding`; the text `nest_service("/static/site"` stays exactly as it is (`tests/a11y/fixtures.ts:41` lists it in `NOT_PAGES`), and the server's mount in `app/server/src/lib.rs` is not touched. (5) `app/site/src/tests/asset_cache.rs` covers: the cache header of a font, of `site.css` (`max-age=3600`) and of the photo, mark and icons (`no-cache`), the font hash pins, a different ETag for each coding, the 304, gzip and Brotli answers decoding to the same bytes for `site.css`, a WebP or woff2 never compressed, and a page never compressed. The first-view weight check (T613) and every existing test pass unchanged.
