tasks.title: Harness: a 4-hourly advisory watch on main that alerts Casey before a new advisory fails hand-ins
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4269 (SEC-021; D-4070, D-4141, D-4223, D-693, D-3795): a new RustSec or npm advisory against a locked dependency turns `Ci`'s "Checks" red on every hand-in that touches Rust or npm inputs at once, and each time the lock fix came only after attempts were lost (D-4070 pulldown-cmark; D-4141 actix-http, T202/T489/T204 attempts; D-4223 picomatch, 35 tasks). The nightly (`nightly-main.yml`) runs the same audits once a day, and a red nightly blocks claims (T445, D-3795), but nothing alerts. Build a watch that only reports. (1) New workflow `.github/workflows/advisory-watch.yml`: triggers `schedule` (cron `23 */4 * * *`) and `workflow_dispatch` only, never `push`, `pull_request` or `workflow_call`, and nothing calls it, so it is never a required check, never part of the nightly and never writes `kit/nightly.json`; top-level `permissions: contents: read`; workflow-level `concurrency: {group: advisory-watch, cancel-in-progress: false}`; every `uses:` pinned to a full 40-character commit SHA. No job is named `Ci`, `Twin`, `Ally` or `Checks` (`runner/verify.py:11`). Job `scan` (read only, `timeout-minutes: 20`): checks out `main` with `persist-credentials: false` and, read only, `claude/kit-state` into a second path, also with `persist-credentials: false` and `fetch-depth: 0` (the commit times `pending` reads); installs cargo-audit 0.22.2 and cargo-deny 0.20.2 with exactly `ci.yml`'s step "Prebuilt tools (cargo-audit, cargo-deny) from pinned musl release tarballs (D-693)" (same versions, URLs, SHA-256 sums, crates.io fallback and version check), the pinned toolchain `--profile minimal` only because cargo-deny reads `cargo metadata`, and Node with `ci.yml`'s pinned `actions/setup-node` step and `node-version: "22"` so `npm audit` matches `Ci`; no build, no rust-cache, no `npm ci` (`npm audit` reads `package-lock.json`). It runs `cargo audit --json >audit.json`, `cargo deny --format json check advisories 2>deny.json` (cargo-deny writes JSON Lines to standard error) and `npm audit --json >npm.json`, keeping each exit code (a found advisory exits non-zero and is not an error), then `python3 scripts/advisory_watch.py scan --cargo-audit audit.json --cargo-audit-exit N --cargo-deny deny.json --cargo-deny-exit N --npm npm.json --npm-exit N --kit-state <kit-state path> --out found.json`, which prints `new=<n>` and `pending=<n>` into `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` (the job's outputs `new` and `pending`) and is uploaded with `found.json` as an artifact. Job `report` (`needs: scan`, `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && (needs.scan.outputs.new != '0' || needs.scan.outputs.pending != '0')`, `permissions: contents: write, actions: write`, `concurrency: {group: kit-state-writer, cancel-in-progress: false}`): only this job joins `kit-state-writer`, and only when there is something to write or send, because GitHub keeps one pending run per concurrency group and a newly queued one cancels the pending one, so an always-running writer every 4 hours could cancel a pending nightly `record` (a stale `kit/nightly.json`) or a pending `notify`. It checks out `claude/kit-state`, downloads `found.json`, runs `python3 <main checkout>/scripts/advisory_watch.py report --found found.json --kit-state .`, which recomputes both `new` and `pending` from this job's own fresh checkout (the scan's outputs only decide whether the job runs) before it writes or dispatches anything, commits the new and re-stamped `outbox/*.md` files as github-actions[bot] and pushes with the nightly `record` job's loop (5 tries, `git fetch` and `git rebase` between, with `git rebase --abort` after a failed rebase before the next try, never force; exit 1 after the fifth). Because a push made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts no other workflow, `notify.yml` gains `workflow_dispatch:` (its only change) and the report job then runs `gh workflow run notify.yml --ref main` whenever the recomputed `new` or `pending` is non-zero, so a lost dispatch or a cancelled pending `notify` heals whatever it carried; before each dispatch it sets a front-matter line `dispatched: YYYY-MM-DD` (today, UTC; added or replaced, nothing else in the file changed) in every new and pending file, committed in the same push (`parse()` in `.github/workflows/notify.yml` keeps unknown keys and sends only the body), so a file stuck in `outbox/` (one notify fails to parse) is dispatched at most once per day and no new state file exists. (2) `scripts/advisory_watch.py` (stdlib only, functions under 50 lines, module docstring per `docs/code-docs.md` recording the JSON shapes read from the pinned tool versions): `scan` writes a sorted, deduplicated list of `{id, ecosystem, package, version, title, patched}` holding exactly what fails a hand-in, no more: cargo-audit's `vulnerabilities.list[]` (`advisory.id`, `package.name`/`version`, `versions.patched`; its informational warnings do not fail `cargo audit` and are skipped); cargo-deny's error-severity advisory diagnostics, parsed one JSON line at a time, skipping lines of `type` `log` and `summary` and exiting 2 on a line that is not JSON or has another unknown `type` (vulnerability, unmaintained, unsound; a yanked crate, which has no advisory id, as `yanked-<crate>-<version>`); both tools apply `.cargo/audit.toml` and `deny.toml` ignores themselves. npm: `npm_audit.parse_report` then `npm_audit.judge(vulns, npm_audit.EXCEPTIONS)` imported from `scripts/npm_audit.py` (not edited, not copied), so `Ci`'s verdict and the watch's agree and an excused advisory (D-4223) never alerts; each problem becomes one entry, its GHSA id when it has one, else `npm-<package>` cleaned to the id character set; `npm_audit.AuditError` exits 2; `fixAvailable`/`range` give the fixed version when known. It fails loudly (exit 2 with a `::error::` line naming the tool, nothing written) when a report is missing, empty, not JSON or of an unknown shape, or when a tool exited non-zero with zero raw entries (an empty npm `vulnerabilities` map, an empty cargo-audit `vulnerabilities.list`, no cargo-deny error diagnostic): a crashed tool never reads as clean, while a non-zero exit whose raw entries are all excused (npm exits 1 on the D-4223 picomatch advisory) is clean. Every id must match `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` (`kit/outbox_format.md`); one that does not (a `/`, a `+`) makes the run exit 2 and is never silently dropped. `new` counts ids with neither `outbox/advisory-<ID>.md` nor `outbox/sent/advisory-<ID>.md` in the kit-state checkout (the outbox id is the dedupe record; no new state file); `pending` counts each `outbox/*.md` there, of any kind, that is not in `outbox/sent/`, whose last commit on `claude/kit-state` (`git log -1 --format=%ct -- <file>`) is more than 30 minutes old (so a file notify is about to send is left to it), and whose `dispatched:` line is not today's date; a file whose front matter does not parse (as `parse()` in `notify.yml` reads it) is left out of `pending` and never stamped, since notify already fails loudly on it. `report` writes each new id in the outbox format: `id: advisory-<ID>`, `title: Advisory <ID> on <package> <version>`, `kind: info`, a body naming the package, version, advisory id and title, the patched version or "no patched release yet", and the line "Nothing needs you; the next plan change updates the lock (D-4141, D-4223)." Neither subcommand touches `kit/nightly.json`, `kit/state.json` or any path but `outbox/*.md` (new advisory files and the `dispatched:` line). A found advisory exits 0: the watch reports, it never fails because an advisory exists. (3) `tests/test_advisory_watch.py`, planted reports only (written by the test into `tmp_path`): a cargo-audit report with a new RustSec id gives `new=1` and `report` writes exactly one outbox file with the fields above; the same id again (in `outbox/` and, separately, in `outbox/sent/`) gives `new=0` and writes none; a clean report writes none; npm exiting 1 with only the D-4223-excused picomatch advisory exits 0 and writes nothing, and an unexcused one writes one; an npm problem with no GHSA id becomes `npm-<package>`; a truncated, empty or non-JSON report, and a non-zero exit with zero raw entries, each exit 2 with nothing written; an id with `/` or `+` exits 2; cargo-deny JSON Lines with one error and one warning diagnostic give one entry; `pending` counts an unsent non-advisory `outbox/*.md` committed over 30 minutes ago, not one committed 5 minutes ago, not one in `outbox/sent/`, and not one whose `dispatched:` is today (but again when it is yesterday), and not one whose front matter does not parse (left unstamped), and the re-stamp changes only that line, using a scratch git repository with planted commit dates; cargo-deny `log` and `summary` lines are skipped and a non-JSON or unknown-`type` line exits 2; a run leaves `kit/nightly.json` and `kit/state.json` byte-identical. The YAML (via `yaml.safe_load`): only `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers; `scan` has no write permission and no `kit-state-writer` group; `scan`'s two checkouts set `persist-credentials: false`; `report` alone has the group, `contents: write`, `actions: write` and the `if` on `new`/`pending`; no `git push` with `--force`; every `uses:` is a 40-hex SHA; the tool versions and SHA-256 sums and the setup-node pin equal `ci.yml`'s; no reference to `kit/nightly.json`; `notify.yml` has `workflow_dispatch` beside its unchanged `push` trigger. (4) `docs/architecture.md` section 12: one bullet after the T445 claim-gate bullet naming the workflow, its schedule, that it only reports through `outbox/advisory-<ID>.md`, why its writer joins `kit-state-writer` only when needed, and why it is outside the nightly (D-4269).

tasks.title: Runner (harness): merge train depth 2, the next branch's update merge on the turn holder's head tested ahead on a throwaway ref
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4281 (Fable's merge-speed decision, Nov 18, 2026, about 00:30Z, `main` 7f322437, under Casey's standing rule: speed is the goal, quality must not decline). Task Q, part 2 of 2: the merge train's runner side, depth 2 (Fable item 2; after T640, which makes `ci` handle train refs and count a green train tip as proof). With T638 an update merge that brought in no compiled input runs a short round, but the next branch still waits for the turn holder's whole round. Here: while turn holder A's head A' (its update merge, or a head already current with main) has Ci, Twin or Ally still pending, the runner builds X, the update merge of B's reviewed head with A' (`UpdateMerge.commit(reviewed_B, A', branch)` and its own check `is_update_merge(reviewed_B, X) == (True, A')`; `runner/update_merge.py` used as it is), where B is the first task after A in `_merge_line` order whose `_line_place` is "line", and pushes X as a new ref `claude/train/<B>-<A' first 12 hex>` (a create: never to B's task branch, never to main, never a force push or a `+` refspec; an existing ref for the same pair is left as it is). The name carries A' so that a newer A' makes a new ref instead of a forced update (Fable named it `claude/train/<B>`; the no-force rule, BUILD_BRIEF.md:224, decides). When A squashes, B gets its ordinary update merge B' on the new main exactly as today (`_update_step`), and T640's proof does the rest. Deletion: every `_resolve_merges` pass (the cycle's and the early `--resolve-merges` step's, D-4235), even when `train_depth` is 1 or missing, lists `claude/train/*` and deletes a ref whose task is not MERGE_PENDING (merged, failed, resyncing), whose A' is no longer the head of a MERGE_PENDING or DONE task (A got a newer head or failed), or that is over 6 hours old by X's committer time, and the task's other train refs when it creates a new one; a failed delete is logged and retried next pass. `push_branch` refuses deletes by design (D-551), so deletion goes through a new `GitHubEnv.delete_train_ref(name)` that refuses any name not matching `re.fullmatch(r"claude/train/T[0-9]+[A-Za-z]?-[0-9a-f]{12}", name, re.ASCII)` and pushes exactly `:refs/heads/<name>`, nothing else. It is read through the Env (`GitHubEnv` under its root), not `runner/__main__.py`: owning that file too would put this task over the harness context limit, and an Env without the reader means off, so every existing fake Env keeps today's behaviour. tasks.title: portals (harness): a real browser's same-origin form POST passes the cross-site check, and the door matrix sends what a browser sends
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4292 (the D-4292 spot reviews, verified on `main` 67827d85; D-1250 named it on Nov 1 and no task took it): every page sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (`app/portals/src/security.rs:80`, SEC-012, SEC-026), and under that policy the Fetch standard's "append a request `Origin` header" sets the serialized origin of any non-`GET`/`HEAD` request whose mode is not `cors` (every HTML form post) to `null`, so a homeowner's, business's or owner's own form post arrives as `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` with `Origin: null`; `is_cross_site` (`app/portals/src/security.rs:334` to `:347`) reads that `Origin` as cross-site, and `refuse_cross_site` and `business_signup::same_site` answer 403 with a `csrf_rejected` event: no pick, Confirm, feedback, check-in, quote close, business sign-in or sign-up step, notice setting, action-link button, owner sign-in or web-chat turn works in a real browser. The tests hid it: twelve Playwright specs re-send each `POST` with a forged `Origin: https://<host>`, and the Rust route tests and the door matrix (`app/server/tests/door_matrix.rs:372`) send that same forged header. (1) `is_cross_site` decides like this, and its doc says so with the Fetch rule: when `Sec-Fetch-Site` is present it alone decides (`same-origin` is not cross-site whatever `Origin` says, since a page cannot set that header; `same-site`, `cross-site`, `none` or anything else is cross-site); when it is absent (browsers before Fetch Metadata), `Origin: https://<Host>` is not cross-site, `Origin: null` is not refused by this check and is left to the route's token check, and any other `Origin`, or none, is cross-site as today. The `Origin: null` case is safe only because every route behind `refuse_cross_site` or `is_cross_site` also checks the CSRF token bound to the `__Host-` session or pre-session cookie (`CsrfForm`, `csrf_matches`), and that `SameSite=Lax` cookie is not sent on a cross-site `POST`, so an attacker page that sets its own `no-referrer` policy still fails the token; check that every caller does check it, and report a plan gap if one does not. `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` stays on every response (SEC-012 and SEC-026 require it on every token page, and those pages are where the forms post), and the function's signature and `business_signup::same_site` stay unchanged. (2) `tests/security/tests/cookies_csrf.rs`: the test route gains the rows of TD-SEC-73 (browser shape `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` with `Origin: null` and the right token is 200; `same-site` and `none` with the right token are 403; no `Sec-Fetch-Site` with `Origin: null` and the right token is 200, with no or a wrong token 403), every existing row keeping its answer, and the event and log-line counts following the new refusals. (3) `app/server/tests/door_matrix.rs` (D-2440): `request` sends what a browser sends, `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` with `Origin: null`, for `Site::Own` and `Site::WrongToken`, and the cross row keeps `cross-site`; a new `Site` row sends a wrong token with no `Sec-Fetch-Site` and `Origin: null` and is judged by `judge_csrf` on every served `POST`: on the probed rows through `probe_csrf`, and on the `POST` rows `probed_rows` skips (`:243` to `:246`: `Door::SignIn` and `Door::Link`, sixteen today: the four `/q/*` posts, `/f`, `/c`, `/b/sign-in` and its token step, the eight sign-up steps, `/owner/sign-in` and `/owner/sign-in/passkey`) through a probe of their own using the fixture's links and tokens, so every served `POST` proves the token check backs the fallback. `judge_csrf` needs exactly one `csrf_rejected` event per refusal, and `admit_security_event` stores at most `SECURITY_EVENT_CAP_FLOOR` (50) events of one kind per route template per minute (and per client; the matrix sends no client header, so every probe is `0.0.0.0`) when nothing calls `configure_security_events`: count the refusals each template can get in one minute (today three rows for each of the six actors on a probed row, eighteen, and the new probe's on a skipped row), state the count in the test's doc, and if any template could reach 50, have the matrix fixture call `portals::api::configure_security_events` with a higher cap before it runs; and an own-site `POST` no longer passes on a fail-closed refusal: on the public door (`:446` to `:449`), an admitted realm `POST` (`:461` to `:465`) and `judge_opened`'s `POST` (`:483` to `:488`) it passes only when it is not a 403 and no `csrf_rejected` event was logged under its request ID (a route's own 4xx such as a 422 still passes, with no event), every other expectation staying as strict as it is (D-3706). With today's `is_cross_site` these rows fail, which is the planted proof. (4) `tests/e2e/pick_flow.spec.ts`, `tests/e2e/checkin.spec.ts` and `tests/e2e/feedback.spec.ts`: the `httpsOrigin` helper and its calls are removed, with the header comments that explain them, so each spec posts with the browser's own headers (`baseURL` is `http://127.0.0.1`, a potentially trustworthy origin, so Chromium sends `Sec-Fetch-Site`); any wait that relied on the re-send's `maxRedirects: 0` follows the browser's own redirect instead, and every assertion stays. tasks.goal: Plan change D-4327 (night spot review of intake and AI, each case reproduced against a copy of `app/privacy/src/scrub.rs` on `main` e64d06e02, re-verified on `main` d662af7e5; AI-002, AI-020, PRIV-005; it amends D-3314). `HOUSE_CUES` (`app/privacy/src/scrub.rs:380`) holds only the English "at", "live", "address" and "is" (D-3314), and with no cue `mark_bare_houses` (`:701`) takes a street word only when `titled` (`:723`), which needs a lower-case letter after the capital. So "vivo en 3301 palo verde", "estoy en el 3301 palo verde", "mi casa es 2150 mesquite" and "mi dirección es 3301 palo verde" pass unchanged, as do "WATER HEATER LEAKING 2150 MESQUITE LAKE HAVASU" and "2150 MESQUITE"; that text is kept as the job's description today (`app/intake/src/order.rs:174` to `:180`) and is the AI's input once T299 wires it. (1) Spanish cues: "vivo", "dirección", "direccion", "casa" and "es" join `HOUSE_CUES`, matched on the token before the number as today; "en" and "el" count as a cue only when "vivo" or "estoy" is within the two tokens before them ("vivo en 3301", "estoy en el 3301"), so "instalado en 2015 junto al garaje" keeps every word; `MEASURES` (with "cuadrados", "galones", "años", "voltios", "grados", "libras", "pulgadas", "millas" and "dólares" added where missing) still keeps a size ("la casa es 1500 pies cuadrados"). (2) All-caps text: in a message of at least 8 letters of which at least three quarters are capitals, an all-capitals word counts as a capitalised name for the no-cue rule exactly as `titled` counts "Mesquite" in ordinary text: letters only, not a common word, not in `MEASURES`, at most 2 after a 3- to 6-digit number (today's reach); a 1- or 2-digit number is never a house number, so "WATER HEATER 2 YEARS OLD" keeps every word. In mixed-case text an all-caps word ("YES", "AC", "GFCI") is still never a street name (D-3314's "YES" case). The all-caps rule also never takes a word on a fixed list in `scrub.rs` (a `const`, not the owner-editable common words) of the reply and command words the texting code reads, copied from the code: `businesses::consent`'s `COMMAND_WORDS` (`app/businesses/src/consent.rs:501` to `:520`: confirm, confirmar, yes, si, sí, hold, espera, away, ausente, pause, pausa, resume, reanudar, busy, ocupado, start, unstop, link), `messaging::rules::PROVIDER_OPT_OUT_WORDS` (`app/messaging/src/rules.rs:381` to `:394`: stop, stopall, unsubscribe, cancel, end, revoke, optout, quit, parar, alto, cancelar, baja), the help words (`app/server/src/inbound_text.rs:120`: help, info, ayuda), the card replies (`app/intake/src/summary_step.rs:80` to `:81`: send, ok, enviar, edit, cambiar), the check-in answers (`app/jobs/src/followups.rs:89` to `:97`: problem, problema, done, listo, no, later, mas, más, tarde, ongoing, continuo, other, otro), close and cerrar (`app/intake/src/rules.rs:669`) and list and lista (`app/intake/src/handlers.rs:385` to `:386`); `privacy` may not depend on those crates (`kit/layers.json`), so the list is a copy with a doc comment naming each source, exported as `privacy::api::REPLY_WORDS`; most sources are private, so the copy is deliberately not kept in sync by machine (drift fails safe: a word missing from the copy is only over-scrubbed, in all-caps text after a house-sized number, and never keeps an address), except for the two lists `messaging::api` exports: the new `tests/integration/tests/scrub_reply_words.rs` checks that `REPLY_WORDS` holds every word of `messaging::api::PROVIDER_OPT_OUT_WORDS` and `RESUBSCRIBE_WORDS`. So "CLOSE 1042 YES" (`app/privacy/src/tests/scrub.rs:221`, which must stay unchanged) keeps every word. All-caps text is thus treated as strictly as ordinary text, no more. (3) Optional, outside AI-002's letter: a phone number split by joining words ("928 and then 555 and 0100", "928 y 555 y 0100") may be joined like a spoken separator when the pieces are 3, 3 and 4 digits; if built, "2 and 3 bedrooms" and "between 100 and 200 dollars" keep every word. Tests in `app/privacy/src/tests/scrub.rs` (TD-AI-31), every line fake: must-scrub, each listed number and street word removed: "vivo en 3301 palo verde", "estoy en el 3301 palo verde", "mi casa es 2150 mesquite", "mi dirección es 3301 palo verde", "mi direccion es 3301 palo verde", "se me rompió el calentador, vivo en 3301 palo verde", "WATER HEATER LEAKING 2150 MESQUITE LAKE HAVASU", "2150 MESQUITE" and "AC OUT AT THE HOUSE 4410 SAGUARO PLEASE CALL" (the number and "SAGUARO"), each also added to the recall corpus (`CONTACTS`), which keeps at least 99% (TD-AI-09); must-keep, every word unchanged: "WATER HEATER 2 YEARS OLD", "50 GALLON WATER HEATER LEAKING", "TANK IS 120 GALLONS", "ROOF IS 1500 SQ FT", "ERROR CODE 41 ON THE AC", "instalado en 2015 junto al garaje", "la casa es 1500 pies cuadrados", "el calentador tiene 10 años", "YES PLEASE SEND SOMEONE", "My GFCI trips", "CLOSE 1042 YES", "HOLD 1042 BUSY", "CONFIRM 2150 SI", "el voltaje es 220 voltios" and "la cuenta es 1500 dólares"; every existing case passes unchanged. `app/privacy/` keeps its 95% branch coverage. Update `app/privacy/NOTES.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: server and messaging: the signed Resend webhook route marks bounced and complained business addresses returned
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4327 (night spot review of outgoing email on `main` e64d06e02, re-verified on `main` d662af7e5; BIZ-040, BIZ-055, SEC-025, SEC-050, SEC-051; D-1381). `messaging::api::receive_email_event` (`app/messaging/src/email.rs:723`, D-1381) and `businesses::api::mark_returned` (`app/businesses/src/email_verification.rs:512`) have no caller outside tests, and no server route verifies `WebhookVendor::Resend` (`app/adapters/src/signatures.rs:59`); `app/businesses/NOTES.md:222` says the webhook's call to `mark_returned` is not wired, D-1381 left it to a later task and none had it (T133 builds the signed adapters and the fake Resend's events, T490 the mailers, T379 only counts suppressed card emails). So a hard-bouncing or complaining business address keeps getting notices, BIZ-040's banner never shows, and once emails go out `check_webhook_silence` (`email.rs:811`, scheduled hourly) raises the High `messaging.email_webhooks_silent` alert 24 hours later and keeps it open for good. (1) `app/server/src/resend_webhook.rs` (new): `POST /webhooks/resend`, mounted in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` beside the other webhook routes and outside the CSRF layer as they are, reads the raw body and the `svix-id`, `svix-timestamp` and `svix-signature` headers and passes `adapters::api::verify_webhook(WebhookVendor::Resend, …)` with the signing secret from a new setting `ASKHAVA_RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (the shared `app/core/src/settings.rs`; a secret, never logged or printed); unset, the route is not mounted in Dev and CI (they answer 404) and the server refuses to start in Test and Live, as `stripe_webhook`'s secret does (`app/server/src/release_sink.rs:298` to `:302`); a refused delivery (bad signature, missing header, timestamp outside 5 minutes) answers `adapters::api::refuse(WebhookVendor::Resend, e)`'s 403 and stores nothing, and the router is mounted through the `refused(...)` wrapper (`app/server/src/lib.rs:404` to `:415`), so each 403 records one capped `webhook_signature_failed` security event (`app/server/src/webhook_refusals.rs`; SEC-016, SEC-048); every other failure answers 200 or 500, never 403, as that layer requires. A verified delivery is handled in one transaction the route opens and commits once: it passes `&mut *tx` to `receive_email_event` (which dedupes by the Svix ID, stores the event and raises SEC-050's complaint alert, D-1381), then to the returns lookup, `mark_returned` and `acknowledge_cleared` below, so each of their own `begin()` calls is a savepoint and a failure anywhere rolls the event back too; `Recorded`, `Repeat` and `Ignored` answer 200 after the commit and any database error answers 500 with nothing kept, so Resend's retry is a first delivery again, never a `Repeat` that skips the address (SEC-051: acknowledged only once stored). (2) For a `Recorded` event of type `email.bounced`, `email.complained` or `email.suppressed`, after the store, a new `messaging::api` lookup in `app/messaging/src/email_returns.rs` (new; not `models.rs`, which T470, T573 and T580 own) maps the event's email ID through `messaging.email_outbox.provider_id` to the row's `recipient_kind` and `recipient_id` (`migrations/0089_messaging_retries_email.sql:39` to `:50`); for a `business` row it finds the mailbox's businesses through `businesses::api::businesses_of_mailbox` and calls `businesses::api::mark_returned` once for each, at the event's signed `created_at` (read from the verified body, never the wall clock, so SEC-051's event-time order holds and BIZ-055's span is measured between events), with `Returned::Complaint` for `email.complained`, `Returned::Hard` for `email.suppressed` and for an `email.bounced` whose `data.bounce.type` is `"Permanent"`, and `Returned::Soft` for any other bounce (`"Transient"`, `"Undetermined"` or no type); the body fields are read in `email_returns.rs` (BIZ-055's 14-day rule is `mark_returned`'s, which queues `RETURNED_KIND`); a homeowner row, an unknown email ID or another event type changes nothing more, and a `Repeat` calls nothing. (3) A stored event of any type clears the webhook-silence alert: `messaging.email_webhooks_silent` joins `CLEARING_KINDS` (`app/ops/src/alerts.rs:396`) and the route calls `ops::api::acknowledge_cleared` (`:418`, OPS-023) with it after the store, so the alert resolves once webhooks arrive and a later silence opens a new one (`raise_kind_once`, D-3144). (4) Before Gate C only the stand-in and test secrets are used: no live Resend key, endpoint or webhook is created or registered (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:68`); registering the endpoint and its secret at Resend is a Gate C step, listed for Casey in `docs/for-casey-review.md`. (5) Tests in `app/server/tests/resend_webhook.rs` (TD-SEC-76), fake data only, through the assembled router with a test signing secret and bodies built by hand in Resend's event shape (the fake Resend's events, `stand_ins/resend.py:84` to `:85`, carry no bounce type, and `stand_ins/` is protected): a bad signature, a missing header and a timestamp 6 minutes old each answer 403 with nothing stored and exactly one `webhook_signature_failed` security event; a hard bounce, a complaint and `email.suppressed` for a sent business notice each mark its mailbox returned with one `RETURNED_KIND` task (the complaint also one complaint alert), and a replay of the same Svix ID changes nothing; two transient bounces whose signed `created_at` are 13 days apart do not mark it and 14 days apart do (BIZ-055); a bounce with an undetermined or missing bounce type counts as soft; a failure injected after the event store (for example a `mark_returned` error from a planted constraint) answers 500 and keeps no event row, and the same delivery sent again then marks the address returned; a bounce of a homeowner email, an unknown email ID and a `contact.created` event answer 200 and change nothing; a database failure answers 500; an open `messaging.email_webhooks_silent` alert is resolved by the next stored event; with no secret set the route is not served in CI, and building the composition for Test or Live with no secret is refused. Ordered after T133, T490 and T469 (the adapters, the fake's events and the provider wiring) and after T652, the other queued owner of `app/ops/src/alerts.rs`. Update `docs/architecture.md`, `app/server/NOTES.md`, `app/messaging/NOTES.md`, `app/businesses/NOTES.md` (its "Not wired yet" line), `app/ops/NOTES.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: jobs, intake, calls and server: a masked call line closes when the job is cancelled, on a check-in PROBLEM or NO, and after 30 days
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4338 (night spot review of `calls` and `jobs` on `main` d662af7e5, confirmed in a second pass and re-verified on `main` 9aeca6f95; CALL-009, CALL-010, JOB-005, JOB-015; closes D-1694's deferral). `calls::api::close_line` (`app/calls/src/lifecycle.rs:168`) has one production caller, the unreachable no-show path (`app/picks/src/unreachable_refund.rs:407`, `:471`), and `close_expired` (`:210`) none; routing and the dial gate check only `closed_at IS NULL` (`app/calls/src/routing.rs:459` `lines_on`, `app/calls/src/pins.rs:551` to `:583` `connect`). So after a homeowner cancels a Connected job, or answers a check-in PROBLEM or NO, the business can still call through the masked number to her real phone indefinitely, and is never told of the cancel (CALL-010). `jobs` and `intake` may not call `calls` (`kit/layers.json`, D-491, D-1694), so the close goes through a queued task, as `jobs`' `PURGE_DUE_KIND` does. (1) The new `app/jobs/src/line_close.rs` (exported through the shared `jobs::api`): `LINE_CLOSE_KIND` (`"calls.close_line"`) and `queue_line_close(db, job, reason, now)`, which reads the job's number and enqueues one task with the payload `{job, number, reason}` (`reason` one of `cancelled`, `complaint`, `no_show`) under the per-move dedupe key `calls.close_line.<job>.<job version after the move>` (`core.task.dedupe_key` stays taken once a task is done, `app/core/src/tasks.rs:180`, so a per-job key would silently drop a later move's close; `close_line` is idempotent anyway), on the caller's connection, so it commits or rolls back with the status move. It is called right after a cancel or check-in move applied (`Guarded::Applied`; `intake`'s `cancel` helper drops the move's result today, `app/intake/src/closing.rs:152` to `:155`, so it branches on it), inside the same transaction: by `intake`'s `cancel` (`app/intake/src/closing.rs:146` to `:156`), which both the text cancel and the homeowner's page cancel (`close_from_page`, `:242` to `:261`) use, and its INT-038 cancel (`app/intake/src/conversation.rs:358` to `:369` `cancel_job`) with `cancelled`, on every applied cancel whatever the status it left (`close_line` answers `None` when the job has no line, and the key is per move), because a released job with an open line is not in Connected in production today (D-2015 (1)) but in the status `pick_move` leaves it in (Awaiting confirm, `app/picks/src/status.rs:163` to `:168`); by `jobs::followups::answer_check_in` (`app/jobs/src/followups.rs:205`, after `apply` applied at `:222` to `:229`, before the commit at `:230`) with `complaint` for PROBLEM, and with `no_show` for a NO that moves the job out of Connected (to Closed, or to Quotes ready for a day-3 NO under email contact, which records a no-show; `app/jobs/src/rules.rs:121` to `:126`); OTHER, DONE, ONGOING and the 21-day Connected timeout (`app/jobs/src/status.rs:130`) queue nothing, and their lines close in the 30-day sweep. Both the text and the portal check-in (`app/intake/src/check_in_replies.rs`, `app/portals/src/checkin.rs`) go through `answer_check_in`, so neither changes. (2) The new `app/calls/src/close_tasks.rs` (exported through the shared `calls::api`): `run_close_line` reads the payload and calls `close_line(db, (job, number), reason, now)` (`Cancelled`, `Complaint` or `NoShow`; an unknown reason is a handler error), which closes the line with its audit row and, for a cancel, queues `line_closed_cancelled` (en and es, `app/messaging/templates/en.json:422`, `es.json:514`) to the owner and the Confirm-and-billing members with no strike (CALL-010); `close_line` answers `None` for a line already closed (by the no-show path or a repeat), so the task is idempotent. `CLOSE_EXPIRED_KIND`, `run_close_expired_at` (calls `close_expired` at the worker clock's now, then enqueues the next run a day later under a run-time dedupe key) and `schedule_close_expired`. (3) The shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` registers `jobs::api::LINE_CLOSE_KIND` to `calls::api::run_close_line` and `CLOSE_EXPIRED_KIND` in `register_daily_sweeps` (`:1836`), on every path so `tests/integration/tests/task_registry.rs` finds both kinds; the shared `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs` seeds the sweep in `schedule_start` (`:106`). (3b) A line opened late must not outlive the job: `picks`' `retry_line` (`app/picks/src/settle.rs:175`, the `picks.line_retry` task) opens a line for a Paid or Free pick whose job never had one and never checks the job is still Connected, while a cancel, PROBLEM or NO leaves the pick Paid; so a close that ran before the retry found no line, and the retry would then open a live line to her phone for up to 30 days. This task now owns `settle.rs` (a money file under its 95% branch-coverage floor, `tests/coverage_floor.json:30`): `retry_line` opens nothing (and finishes) when `jobs::api::current` (`app/jobs/src/api.rs:70`) reads the job's status as final (`JobStatus::is_final`, `app/jobs/src/status.rs:233`: Cancelled, Closed, Done, Closed early, Not covered); it does not require Connected, because no production code moves a job to Payment pending or Connected yet (D-2015 (1), D-2930), so released jobs sit in Awaiting confirm and every existing line-retry test (`app/server/tests/release_recovery.rs:642` to `:669`, `:738` to `:770`; `tests/integration/tests/whos_calling.rs:223`) passes unchanged. The PROBLEM and NO closes are wired now but stay inert until the move to Connected is built (D-2015 (1), unowned; the overseer plans it separately), since no check-in is queued for a job that is not Connected (D-2930). (4) Tests in the new `tests/integration/tests/line_close_paths.rs` (TD-CALL-27), PostgreSQL, fake data and fake numbers only, driving the real paths, not `close_line` directly: a released job left in Awaiting confirm, where production leaves it, with an open line, cancelled by her text, closes the line and sends the `line_closed_cancelled` notice once the queued task runs; a released job that the confirm timer moved back to Quotes ready (`app/jobs/src/status.rs:122` to `:125`, the usual state of a released job when she cancels) with an open line, cancelled, does the same; a Connected job (moved there by hand, as no production move exists yet) with an open line; the homeowner's text cancel through `intake`, then the queued task run, closes the line with one `line_closed_cancelled` notice and no strike, and the business's call on the pool number then gets no `Connect` (`calls::api::answer_call` hangs up or asks for nothing to connect); the same for the homeowner's page cancel (`close_from_page`) and the INT-038 cancel; a check-in PROBLEM through `answer_check_in` closes it as a complaint with no notice; a check-in NO closes it as a no-show; OTHER and DONE leave it open; a line closed by the no-show path first makes the task a no-op; a rolled-back move queues nothing; a pick whose line retry is still queued when the job is cancelled opens no line when the retry runs, while a retry for a job in Awaiting confirm still opens its line; a cancel of a job that never had a line queues a task that closes nothing; two moves out of Connected on one job (a re-pick after a no-show) each queue their own close; the sweep closes a line assigned 30 days before and not one assigned 29 days 23 hours before, and queues its next run. Update `app/calls/NOTES.md` (its "Not here yet" line: the callers of `close_line` and the sweep are now built), `app/jobs/NOTES.md`, `app/intake/NOTES.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md`. tasks.title: recovery (tests): the backup tests' fake binaries can no longer fail with "Text file busy"
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4864 (Fable's diagnosis of T663's second failure). T663's attempt 2 passed review and a green merge-train run, then failed Coverage on an unrelated main test: `backup::tests::the_dump_sees_only_path_and_its_password` panicked at `app/recovery/src/backup.rs:726` with `Err(Dump)`. `fake_dump` (`:710` to `:714`) and `fake_tool` (`:422` to `:430`) write a shell script with `std::fs::write` and `set_permissions` and the test spawns it at once, while other tests in the same binary fork child processes (the `--version` probe at `:93`, `a_dump_dropped_at_its_deadline_is_killed`, the real `pg_dump` and `psql` in `td_ops_19` at `:544`); a fork made while the write descriptor is open leaves it in a child, so the exec fails with ETXTBSY ("Text file busy"), which `dump_encrypted` maps to `RecoveryError::Dump` (`:185` to `:187`). In `backup.rs` `mod tests`, add one helper `write_script(path, text)` that creates the executable through a child process (`Command::new("/bin/sh")` with the arguments `-c`, `printf %s "$2" > "$1" && chmod 755 "$1"`, `sh`, the path, the text, in that order: the literal `sh` fills `$0`, so the path is `$1` and the text `$2`; waited on, success asserted), so the test process never holds a write descriptor a concurrent fork could inherit; `fake_tool` and `fake_dump` both call it, and their `std::fs::write` and `set_permissions` go. A photo stored before step 9 (a picture text sent at the ZIP step or later) is never shown for confirmation then: it waits, and step 9 shows it for her YES or REMOVE in the order. The task's photo step drives step 9 on every outcome (stored, re-ask, HEIC, refused off Twilio's hosts, or failed after its retries, each with its text), so step 9 never waits on a task that has ended. (2) A new `app/intake/src/picture_text.rs` handles that task (registered in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs`): outside any held transaction it fetches each media through `take_picture_text` with `fetch_twilio_media` (SEC-041: Twilio's hosts only, size cap, timeout), stores it, deletes it at the provider only after the store committed, and then, under the homeowner lock, calls the dispatcher's photo step for that request; a rerun takes nothing twice (dedupe key per media SID). Step 11 then follows. (4) T672's `tests/integration/tests/intake_order_timing.rs` and T673's `intake_order_flow.rs` script replies from the trade questions to name and address; with the photo step between them they are extended here, add-only: a "no photo" reply (and in the flow test one confirmed picture text) is inserted where the order now asks, and the photo ask is added to the expected texts; no assertion is removed or loosened. tasks.title: Runner (harness): a merge-line task whose turn ran out goes to the back of the line instead of waiting forever
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4392 (merge-line starvation; evidence in D-4392). D-3418's merge line lets a turn holder that neither merges nor moves for `MERGE_LINE_TURN_LIMIT` (45 minutes) give up the line (`_turn_spent`), but nothing ever gives it a turn back: `_turn_spent` reads `merge_turn_since` and the branch's last new head, neither changes while it has no turn, so `_line_place` returns "late" forever, and a late task updates only in a cycle where no "line" task holds the turn (`_resolve_merges`' late loop, `runner/cycle.py:548`). With five to seven lanes handing in, some line task always holds it. T623 (PR #1007, handed in 03:46:51Z on November 18) took the turn at 05:22:40Z, got its update merge onto `main` 9aeca6f and green Ci, Twin and Ally, but `main` moved at 05:34Z and 06:00Z (plan merges) before auto-merge could land, no runner cycle ran from 05:27Z to 06:06Z, its turn ran out at 06:07:40Z, and from 06:10Z eleven update merges went to other tasks while T623, holding lane 7, got none. Fix: a spent turn sends the task to the back of the line instead of out of it (round robin), with no new `kit/state.json` key. (1) `_line_place`: "late" (taken last, updates only while the turn is free, exactly as today) now means only `_ruleset_red` (a ruleset-only check failed on its head); every task whose turn is spent is re-queued: "line". (A branch that got no new head in its turn is not kept late: the state cannot tell a branch that was current from one no runner cycle reached, as from 05:27Z to 06:06Z here, so that would bring the starvation back; D-4392 review r2.) (2) `_merge_line(state, now=None)`: with `now`, tasks are ordered by FIX-MAIN first, then by line time (a task without one last, as today; compared as parsed times, not strings), then by task id; a task's line time is `_handed_in_at` (as today), or, when `_turn_spent(task, now)`, the moment its turn ended (the later of `merge_turn_since`, its hand-in and its update merges' `at`, plus `MERGE_LINE_TURN_LIMIT`, capped at `merge_turn_since` plus `MERGE_LINE_TURN_CAP`), so it waits behind every task handed in or re-queued before that moment and ahead of every later one; with `now` None the order is today's hand-in order (`tests/test_runner_merge_line.py:166` calls it so). Every call in `runner/cycle.py` passes `now`, including the merge train's choice of the next line task B (T641), so the train follows the same order. (3) `_mark_turn`: the holder whose turn is spent takes a fresh turn (`merge_turn_since` = now, so `_turn_spent` is false again for a whole turn); a task that does not hold the turn and whose turn is spent keeps its `merge_turn_since` (that is its place in the line: clearing it would put it back at its hand-in time and let it preempt the holder next cycle); one not spent is cleared as today. (4) `_turn_spent` also ends a turn `MERGE_LINE_TURN_CAP` (new, 90 minutes, two limits) after `merge_turn_since` however often its branch got a new head, so a holder whose update keeps being overtaken by `main` cannot keep the turn forever either. Why it is enough (state it in the docstrings): one turn flag, so never two holders; a task re-queued at time r has ahead of it only tasks whose line time is before r, at most the other MERGE_PENDING tasks of that moment (new hand-ins and later re-queues go behind it), each of which holds at most once more for at most `MERGE_LINE_TURN_CAP` before it merges, leaves or is re-queued behind r; so with `main` green it holds the turn within (tasks ahead) x 90 minutes plus one cycle gap, and then gets an update merge (when behind) and a whole turn for its checks. D-3418's protection stays: a holder that never merges (a check that never runs, a ruleset check GitHub waits on) still gives up the line after the limit, and a ruleset-red task never holds the line. Trade-off, accepted: such a holder waits a full round and then holds again for up to the limit every round until its attempt ends or someone steps in, where today it lost the line once; stuck tasks (`_line_stuck`), the red-`main` guard, FIX-MAIN first, `UPDATE_KEYS`, auto-merge for out-of-turn current branches and `resolve_merged`'s early pass (T597) are unchanged. Keep every function under 50 lines. Tests, in the new `tests/test_runner_merge_line_rotation.py` (reuse `tests/test_runner_merge_line.py`'s helpers by import; that file and `tests/test_runner_merge_early.py` and `tests/test_failure_drills.py` pass unchanged; T700 also owns T641's `tests/test_runner_merge_train.py` with one narrow licence: a case that builds its late B from a spent turn (which this rule may re-queue into the line) may switch that B to a ruleset-red one, each such change logged in the decision entry; nothing else in that file changes): (a) the T623 reproduction: T623 handed in at minute 0 takes the turn and is updated; no cycle until minute 50 while `main` moves and four tasks hand in at minutes 10, 20, 30 and 40, all open and behind; then a cycle every 5 minutes, a new task handing in every 10 minutes and each holder leaving MERGE_PENDING (merged) 20 minutes after it took the turn: T623 is re-queued at minute 45, the four earlier tasks hold in turn, and T623's branch gets an update merge and the turn (`merge_turn_since` = that cycle) no later than the cycle after the fourth leaves, while every task handed in after minute 45 is still waiting; this case fails against `main`'s runner (T623 never updates); (b) in every cycle of (a), at most one MERGE_PENDING task has a `merge_turn_since` whose turn is not spent, and at most one line task's branch is updated; (c) a re-queued task keeps its `merge_turn_since` while it waits and never preempts the holder, whose `merge_turn_since` does not change across cycles; (d) a holder updated every 20 minutes keeps the turn at `MERGE_LINE_TURN_CAP` minus one minute and gives it up at the cap to the next in line; (e) a holder whose checks never run gives up the line at the limit, takes a fresh turn only after the tasks ahead of it have held, and gives it up again at the limit, whether or not its branch got a new head in its turn; (f) a spent task alone in the line takes a fresh turn and its update at once (as today's late task with a free turn); (g) a ruleset-red task with a spent turn is still late: it is never re-queued into the line and updates only while the turn is free; (h) FIX-MAIN still comes first and a red `main` still moves nothing else. `docs/architecture.md`'s "Merge line (D-3418)" bullet says so with D-4392.

tasks.title: Integration tests (harness): one shared log capture that a callsite cached as "never" cannot miss (D-4419)
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4419 (5): `td_lic_30_reads_write_nothing_and_log_no_value` (`tests/integration/tests/signup_own_record.rs:602`) failed once in `Ci` at its `assert!(!logged.is_empty(), "the unreadable read is logged")` (`:634`) with no code change, then passed. Each test file that checks log lines keeps its own `Subscriber` (`Lines`, `:628` to `:674`) and installs it for its own thread only with `tracing::subscriber::set_default` (`:613`). `tracing` caches each callsite's interest the first time any thread reaches it; when another test in the same binary reaches a callsite while no subscriber is in place, or while the interest is being rebuilt as a capture is installed, the callsite can keep a cached `Interest::never`, and the event never reaches the capture: a test that asserts a line is logged fails, and one that asserts no line holds a value passes without having seen the line. Build one capture for the `askhava-integration` test crate in the new `tests/integration/src/log_capture.rs` (`pub mod log_capture;` in `tests/integration/src/lib.rs`; `tracing` moves from `[dev-dependencies]` to `[dependencies]` in the shared `tests/integration/Cargo.toml`, no new crate, `Cargo.lock` unchanged): a process-global subscriber installed once per test binary (`std::sync::OnceLock`, `tracing::subscriber::set_global_default`, then `tracing::callsite::rebuild_interest_cache()`), whose `register_callsite` answers `Interest::always()` and `enabled` true, so no callsite is ever cached as never while it is in place, and which appends each event's and each new span's fields (as the files' `Line` visitors do: ` name=value` with the value's `Debug`) to the buffer of the capture started on the current thread, if any; `log_capture::start()` gives a guard holding that buffer (a `Vec<String>` behind `Arc<Mutex<_>>`) whose drop ends the capture, and a capture never sees another thread's events, as today. A unit test in `log_capture.rs` reaches a callsite first on another thread before any capture exists, then captures it on the test's thread. Move to it the three files whose tests assert that a log line is present, deleting their own `Subscriber`: `signup_own_record.rs` (TD-LIC-30, both captures, `:211` and `:613`), `tests/integration/tests/emergency_request_limits.rs` (`:275` to `:286`, "logged once", `error=\"Counter\"`) and `tests/integration/tests/safety_key_retry.rs` (`:228` to `:229`, "step failed"). Every assertion in the three files stays as it is, word for word: no assertion is removed, loosened or moved after a retry; only the capture's type and its start change. The other per-thread captures are not changed here: eight more `tests/integration/tests/` files assert only that no line holds a value, and those in other test crates (`app/server/tests/`, `tests/security/tests/`, `app/jobs/src/tests/transitions.rs`) cannot use this crate's helper. (2) In a new module `runner/wip.py` (`//!`-style module docstring per `docs/code-docs.md`): `WIP_REF` = `claude/wip/(T[0-9]+[A-Za-z]?)-a([0-9]+)` and `wip_ref(task_id, attempt)`; `blocked_paths(paths, protected, locked)`, the changed paths under any `kit/tasks.json` `protected_paths` entry (CLAUDE.md rule 7's list and more: `.github/`, `.claude/`, `runner/`, `stand_ins/`, `sources/`, the protected tests and scripts), or among `main`'s `check_plan_lock.locked_paths()` (which covers `scripts/*.py`, `scripts/*.sh`, `.gitattributes`, `kit/runner.json`, `kit/tasks.json` and the rest of the locked blueprint), or named `.gitattributes` anywhere, or `.gitleaks*`; so a retry never starts on an unreviewed `smoke.sh`, `prehandin.sh` or scanner change. `binary_paths(numstat)`: any path `git diff --numstat` reports as binary (`-`), an image included, is refused (a public repository: a photo or binary is never kept on a WIP ref). `scan(...)` returns '' only when all of these pass: no added line in `<main>..<head>` contains `gitleaks:allow`; `gitleaks git` over exactly that log range (`--log-opts`, `--no-banner --redact --exit-code 1`) AND `gitleaks dir` over the head tree; `scan_text` from `pii_scan.py` over each commit's changed files (as of that commit), over the head tree once (`pii_scan.py --root`), and over the commit messages (`git log --format=%B <main>..<head>`). Every scanner is main's copy, never the checkout's (at `--after` the checkout is the worker's branch, and `_pii_patterns` at `github_env.py:195` to `:198` loads `pii_scan.py` from its own path): `pii_scan.py`, `brand.py` and any gitleaks config are written from `git show <main>:<path>` into a temporary directory and run from there, as `prehandin()` writes main's gate (`github_env.py:2491` to `:2494`); trees are read with `git show`/`git ls-tree` or a `git worktree add --detach` checkout, never with `git archive`, which follows the head's `.gitattributes`. Exit 1 or any other non-zero code, a missing `gitleaks` binary, the time bound or any exception is a refusal with a one-line reason, never a pass (fail closed). tasks.title: Runner (harness): a retry after a review failure or a plan-fixed PLAN GAP continues the kept work once; workers check ownership first
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4720 (Nov 19, 2026; Fable's decision on Casey's token-efficiency ask). Part B of two, on T726's mechanics (`runner/wip.py`, `GitHubEnv.wip_check` with its scans of each commit, the head tree and the messages, `push_wip`, `wip_refs`, `delete_wip_ref`, `wip_continue`, `prepare_branch`'s `wip_continue`, `continued_from` and `wip_dropped`): the policy. From `claude/kit-state` history, about 120 failed attempts that pushed nothing cost about 520 to 580M worker tokens, and the attempt after such a failure used about 7 to 10M against about 1.1M after a pushed (check_failed) one; the expected saving is 350 to 550M. (1) A new session outcome `review_failed`: the attempt's reviewer, after step 4's findings round, still ends with `REVIEW-VERDICT: FINDINGS`; the session passes `--outcome review_failed --log <the findings>`. In `runner/cycle.py` it counts exactly as `tests_failed` (attempts, BLOCKED at the cap, `last_failure`, strikes), the only difference being (2). (2) WIP push: when an attempt ends `review_failed` with reviewer evidence, or `plan_gap`, with commits ahead of `main`, origin has no task branch (the hand-off's prepared `remote_sha` empty), `env.wip_continue()` is true, the attempt did not itself continue a WIP and the task's entry has no `wip_used`, and the log names neither test weakening nor protected-path tampering (a fixed, tested case-insensitive pattern list, e.g. `weaken`, `assertion removed`, `test removed`, `protected path`, `tamper`), the runner asks `env.wip_check(head)`; on '' it records `wip: {ref, sha, attempt, kind ("review" or "plan_gap"), at}` on the task through `update_state` FIRST and only then calls `env.push_wip(ref, sha)` (record before push, as D-515 orders the review record before the branch push), ref `claude/wip/<id>-a<attempt>`; a refusal or a failed push records `wip_skipped: <why>` in the attempt's history row and changes nothing else. Every other ending (timeout or a lease that ran out, `tests_failed`, prehandin or smoke red, review missing, path-check failure, usage limit, api error) pushes nothing, as today. An Env without these methods does nothing new. (3) Continue: at claim, before `_prepare_branch`, the task dict gets `wip_continue: {ref, sha}` only when the entry's `wip` exists, `wip_used` is unset, the flag is on and, for `kind` `plan_gap`, the entry's latest `requeues` item has `plan_fix` and an `at` later than the record's `at` (a requeue after `--plan-fix`, D-677); the claim then sets `wip_used: true`. The attempt's history row gets `continued_from` (from `prepared`) or `wip_dropped`; either way `wip` is dropped from the entry once the attempt is prepared, so a continued attempt that fails again starts the next one fresh. The reviewer is not told the branch continues earlier work or that a head was rejected, and reviews the whole diff against `main` as usual. (4) Cleanup: `wip` is dropped when the task is DONE or SKIPPED; each cycle, beside the stale-train pass (`cycle.py:635` to `:654`), a sweep lists `env.wip_refs()` FIRST, then re-reads the state (`env.read_state()`, fresh, after the listing) and deletes only refs that are not exactly some task's recorded `wip` (ref and sha) in that fresh state; because a lane records `wip` before it pushes, a ref pushed by any of the seven lanes after the listing is never deleted, and one pushed before it is already recorded, so DONE, SKIPPED, fresh-started, removed tasks and stray names are all cleared; a failed delete is retried on the next pass; it runs whether or not the flag is on. A WIP ref never gets a pull request, auto-merge or `_adopt_orphan_pr` (`cycle.py:1814`): those read only `claude/task/**` branches and recorded PRs. (5) Tokens: the history row's existing `usage` with `continued_from` lets the overseer compare continued and fresh retries; after 10 continued retries the overseer records the comparison in `docs/decisions.md` and sets `wip_continue` false if continuing is not clearly cheaper (D-4720). (6) Ownership check first: in `backup-runner.yml`'s session prompt (step 3, where the worker is briefed), tell the worker that its first step, before any edit, is to list every file it expects to create or change, compare the list with the prompt's owned and shared paths, and if any falls outside, stop and report `PLAN GAP: outside ownership: <path>, <path>` naming the exact paths; `runner/cycle.py` records those paths as `paths` in the task's `plan_gap` record. Step 4 adds `review_failed` as above and says never to pass the branch note or the last failure to a reviewer; step 3b passes a `continued_from` branch note word for word to the worker. (7) `kit/state_schema.json` describes the optional per-task `wip`, `wip_used` and `plan_gap.paths`, and history's `continued_from`, `wip_dropped`, `wip_skipped`; absent keys mean no WIP, and unknown keys are kept (D-121), so a state written by either runner reads under the other and no merge hold is needed; `python3 scripts/check_state.py` passes on states with and without them. (8) `tests/test_runner_wip.py`: protected-path refusal, scan hit and scanner error each push nothing and record `wip_skipped`; the record is written before the push; a timeout, a `tests_failed`, a smoke-red and a path-check ending push nothing; a sha mismatch or missing ref starts fresh and drops `wip`; once only (a continued attempt that fails again pushes nothing and the next starts fresh); a `plan_gap` WIP continues only on a requeue after `--plan-fix`, not after a plain `--requeue`; a log naming test weakening pushes nothing; no pull request, auto-merge or `_adopt_orphan_pr` adoption from a WIP ref; the sweep deletes the ref after DONE, after SKIPPED and for a stray name, and keeps a recorded one, including one recorded by another lane between the listing and the state read (the race case); `review_failed` counts like `tests_failed`; flag off: no push, no `wip_continue`, the sweep still runs; PLAN GAP paths land in `plan_gap.paths`.

tasks.title: messaging and privacy: opt-out listings are re-keyed to the active index key version, and a version is retired only once every listing under it is re-keyed
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4748 (Fable's decision (2), Nov 19, 2026; designs D-4418's open item; PRIV-024, CON-035, CON-013). PRIV-024 (`docs/spec/privacy.md:28`, reworded by D-4748) lets a `VAULT_INDEX_KEY` version be retired only once every opt-out listed under it is also listed under the active version. Today `record` (`app/messaging/src/optout.rs:332`) lists a number under the versions configured at that moment and nothing re-keys a listing, so T702's start check (`app/messaging/src/suppression_versions.rs:39`) keeps every held version configured for good and a leaked version can never be retired. This task, in the new `app/messaging/src/suppression_rekey.rs` (public calls re-exported through the shared `messaging::api`): (1) `rekey_suppression_batch(db, vault, limit) -> Result<usize, _>` takes up to `limit` numbers listed under an older version with no row under the active one, finds each one's kept vault phone (D-079 keeps it while the number is listed) through a new `privacy::api::phone_for_index(conn, vault, (version, digest))` in the new `app/privacy/src/suppression_phone.rs` (re-exported through the shared `privacy::api`; it matches the contact's stored homeowner-phone digest under that version, reads the phone under `Purpose::Rotation` (`app/privacy/src/models.rs:148`), audits the read as `rotate_batch` does (PRIV-003) and returns a `SecretString`, never logged or put in an error), and, holding T701's per-number lock (`lock_number`, `optout.rs:455`) in the same transaction, adds the missing rows under every configured version with the channel, method and time of the row it copies; it returns how many numbers moved and is run beside `rotate_batch` (`app/privacy/src/vault.rs:767`) until both return 0. A listing whose phone no contact holds is counted and left, never guessed. (2) `retire_index_version(db, vault, version)` refuses (naming counts and version numbers only, never a digest) when `version` is the active one or while any number listed under it lacks its row under the active version; otherwise it deletes the rows under `version` in one transaction with one audit row, after which the operator drops the version from `VAULT_INDEX_KEY` and T702's start check passes. T702's start check and its test are unchanged. (3) The order (add the new version, run both batches to 0, retire, then drop) goes in the `messaging` and `privacy` notes and `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/runbook.md` is not this task's file. Tests in the new `tests/integration/tests/suppression_rekey.rs`, PostgreSQL, fake 555-01xx numbers only: a v1-only opt-out gains its v2 rows and `send_checked` still refuses the number after v1 is retired and dropped; retiring refuses while one listing lacks its v2 row, and for the active version; an opt-out arriving during the run on a second connection leaves exactly one listing per version (the lock); no log line, error or audit row holds a phone or a digest. tasks.title: portals and payments: a $0 Confirm after a PaymentIntent was opened ends the intent and releases, and a refused paid event raises a High alert
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4763 (Fable's money audit of `main` 79e9b499, finding M1 major and m3 minor; FEE-010, FEE-013, FEE-016, PICK-022, SEC-049; D-3717, D-3719, D-3813, D-3824, D-2713). M1: the Confirm page opens a PaymentIntent when the waiver decided on the page read is none (`card_section`, `app/portals/src/confirm_pay.rs:1219` to `:1228`), but the press can then decide $0 (a free first win or a repeat customer that the page read did not see, `waiver_now`, `confirm_pay.rs:1242` to `:1252`; `decide_and_pay`, `:1492` to `:1494`; `decided`, `app/payments/src/free_wins.rs:166`; `is_repeat`, `:221`); `no_fee_release` (`app/payments/src/release_proof.rs:285`) refuses any pick with a `payments.pick_intent` row (`:298`, `NOT EXISTS`), so a $0 Confirm after an intent was opened never releases her details and the business is stuck. This task: (1) in the press transaction that records a $0 decision, `confirm_pay.rs` calls `payments::api::end_intent_unless_charging` (`app/payments/src/pick_fee.rs:222`) for the pick's open intent on `tx` before `press_move` (`confirm_pay.rs:1502`, `app/portals/src/confirm_moves.rs:174`, which commits `tx`) and makes no Stripe call for the ended intent, as that function's other callers make none (the intent is unconfirmed and holds no funds; a later success on it after a declined attempt is refunded under FEE-021, and one with no attempt at all raises m3's High alert below). When `end_intent_unless_charging` answers false, the whole press transaction, which has already written the $0 row (`decide_and_pay`, `confirm_pay.rs:1492` to `:1494`), is rolled back and the press answers with the attempt's state (`attempt_state`, `confirm_pay.rs:1028`), so a pick is never both charged and waived; (2) `no_fee_release` accepts a pick whose intents are all ended with no live or succeeded attempt (still refusing one with a live or succeeded attempt, so a pick is never both charged and free, FEE-016); (3) `held_release` (`release_proof.rs:247` to `:256`), which sends any pick with a `pick_intent` row down the paid path, falls to `held_no_fee` for a pick whose intents are all ended with no live or succeeded attempt, so a $0-after-intent release held in safe mode is released, not answered `NotPaid` and dropped by `run_held_release` (`app/server/src/release_hold.rs:86`); 'live or succeeded attempt' in (2) to (4) means an attempt in `sent`, `processing`, `succeeded`, `needs_action` or `unreachable`, the set `end_intent_unless_charging` reads (`pick_fee.rs:239`), so the done test `td_fee_72_an_ended_pick_queues_one_late_refund` (`app/payments/src/tests/held_release.rs`, an ended intent with a `sent` attempt) still takes the paid path, and an intent not yet ended is still refused by `no_fee_release` (done test `td_fee_57_a_pick_with_a_payment_intent_is_refused`, `tests/integration/tests/no_fee_release_binding.rs:130`); (4) `from_stored_success` (`release_proof.rs:331`), for a pick whose intents are all ended with no live or succeeded attempt, no refund and no dispute, answers `no_fee_release`'s result for the pick's own `pick_fee` pair when that clears, else `PickEnded` as today; a `Database` error stays `Database` (else `release_sink.rs:254` to `:258` would read it as `MovedOn` and drop the release for good), so `reclear_release` (`app/payments/src/reclear.rs:30` to `:43`), which falls to `no_fee_release` only on `WrongIntent`, releases a $0-after-intent pick on an emergency job whose release waited for the address instead of answering `PickEnded` (which `release_sink.rs:254` to `:258` reads as `MovedOn`); `reclear.rs` is not edited, and its done test `td_int_39_the_first_failing_check_wins` (`reclear.rs:236` to `:242`: an ended intent, a declined attempt and no $0 row answer `PickEnded`) stays green. m3: a verified `payment_intent.succeeded` that `paid_release` refuses as `WrongAmount`, `WrongPick`, `NotPaid` or `WrongIntent` is only info-logged (`app/payments/src/routes.rs:384` to `:388`); the route's `release` now raises one High alert through `ops::api::raise_alert_once` (IDs and the reason only, never an amount tied to a person or a card detail; deduplicated per pick and reason) only when the event's PaymentIntent id equals the pick's stored `payments.pick_intent.stripe_intent_id`: that is every `WrongAmount`, `WrongPick` and `NotPaid` (`check_intent` runs after the id match, `release_proof.rs:218` to `:225`) and the `WrongIntent` of `store_success` (`:482`, no attempt). A `WrongIntent` for an event naming another intent id (`:218` to `:220`) or a pick with no `pick_intent` row (`:424`) raises no alert and is info-logged as today (done test `td_fee_43_a_database_error_is_resent_and_handled`, `tests/integration/tests/stripe_webhook_dispatch.rs:426` to `:430`, not owned, stays green). `paid_release`'s signature and answers do not change and `ReleaseError` gains no variant; the route tells the cases apart by a crate-private read in `release_proof.rs`; a failed read or a failed alert write answers as a `Database` refusal (500, Stripe resends). A refusal from the `ReleaseSink` raises no m3 alert. Still answering Stripe 200 and resending nothing; `Stripe` and `Database` refusals are retried as today. Tests in the new `tests/integration/tests/zero_fee_after_intent.rs`, PostgreSQL and the Stripe stand-in, fake data only: a page read that opens an intent, then a press that decides $0 (a free first win recorded between the read and the press), ends the intent once (`ended_at` set, no further Stripe request for that intent) and releases her details exactly once; a press with a charge in flight does not take the $0 path and leaves no $0 ledger row; `no_fee_release` still refuses a pick with a succeeded attempt; each `payment_intent.succeeded` on the pick's own stored intent refused as `WrongAmount`, `WrongPick`, `NotPaid` or no-attempt `WrongIntent` raises one High alert and a replay raises none; one naming another intent id raises none; a $0-after-intent release held in safe mode is released by `held_release` through `held_no_fee`; a $0-after-intent release that waited for an address: this case is an in-crate test in `release_proof.rs`'s `mod tests` (owned) that calls `Releasable::from_stored_success` directly: an ended intent with no live or succeeded attempt and the pick's $0 ledger row clears with the no-fee basis; the same rows with a refund or a dispute answer `PickEnded`. Neither `reclear_release` nor `from_stored_success` is named in code in `zero_fee_after_intent.rs` or outside `app/payments/src/` (`reclear.rs:334` to `:359`). Plan change D-5158 (Fable, option (a)): D-4763's Stripe cancel is dropped. The same file must also show, for a `payment_intent.succeeded` on the ended intent after a $0 release: (a) after a declined press attempt, then the $0 press, the success queues one late-success refund task and raises one High alert (FEE-021, `late_success`, `app/payments/src/late.rs:70` to `:111`) and makes no second release; (b) with no attempt at all (`store_success`, `release_proof.rs:473` to `:482`, answers `WrongIntent` before `late_success` runs), it raises m3's High alert and makes no release. If cheap, it also shows that the press reply carries no `client_secret` once the press answers $0 (`press_reply`, `app/portals/src/confirm_pay.rs:333`, its `client_secret` filter at `:343`). Every Confirm route, waiver and release test passes unchanged; `app/payments/` keeps its 95% floor. Money: Opus worker, Opus money and security review, two review rounds. Update the `portals` and `payments` notes, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: messaging: a sole opt-out word counts with any spacing ("STOP ALL"), and decomposed accents fold
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4764 (Fable's texting audit of `main` a9e2cb79, findings T1 (major) and T4; CON-008, CON-010, CON-035; D-020, D-477). `detect_opt_out` (`app/messaging/src/rules.rs:503`) compares the folded text with each sole opt-out word, but `fold` (`:574`) keeps an inner space, so "STOP ALL", "stop all" or "Stop  all" (CON-008's stopall said as two words) and "opt  out" spaced oddly are not opt-outs; and `fold` maps only precomposed accents, so a phrase typed with decomposed accents (a base letter followed by a combining mark, U+0300 to U+036F, as some phones send it: "qu\u{0069}\u{0301}tenme de la lista") misses the Spanish CON-010 phrases. This task, in `app/messaging/src/rules.rs` only: (1) a text is a sole opt-out word when the folded text with every space removed equals a listed word (`PROVIDER_OPT_OUT_WORDS`, `APP_OPT_OUT_WORDS`) with its spaces removed, English and Spanish alike; the strict rule stays: only a text that is nothing but an opt-out word or phrase is one, so "stop please" and "please stop" are still not opt-outs (a spec question left for later, recorded in D-4764), and no ordinary word pair may collapse into a listed word (the test lists the word list's pairs and asserts none is a common two-word phrase); (2) `fold` drops combining marks (U+0300 to U+036F) after lower-casing, so a decomposed accent folds as its precomposed letter does; the phrase match (CON-010) and the word match both use it. Tests: new cases in `app/messaging/src/tests/optout_words.rs` (its existing cases unchanged): "STOP ALL", "stop all", "Stop  all", "opt out", "OPT-OUT", "PARAR" and "Baja." opt out; "stop please", "please stop", "can stop by at 3" do not; each Spanish CON-010 phrase typed with decomposed accents is detected; `app/messaging/src/tests/prop_optout_props.rs` passes unchanged. Every opt-out integration test passes unchanged. Consent: Opus worker (Fable once the runner's `models` map names it, D-4761), Opus security and compliance review. Update the `messaging` notes and `docs/decisions.md`.
tasks.acceptance: `app/messaging/src/tests/optout_words.rs` passes with its new cases and its existing cases unchanged; `prop_optout_props.rs` and every opt-out integration test pass unchanged; "stop please" is still not an opt-out.

tasks.title: privacy: the scrubber catches phones split by connector words, spaced dots, percent-encoded addresses and spaced keycap digits
tasks.goal: Plan change D-4765 (Fable's privacy audit of `main` 4ed3a4ff, finding P1; AI-020, AI-002, PRIV-005, AI-003; TD-AI-09). The scrubber's text feeds `quotes.job_description` (the job card a business sees before a paid pick) and the AI, and four contact shapes pass it: (1) connector words split a spelled or digit phone into runs under 7 digits, each kept (`mark_digit_runs` and `spoken_gap`, `app/privacy/src/scrub.rs:637` to `:664`): "nine two eight and five five five and zero one two three"; (2) a lone "." between a label and a top-level domain is not taken as a dot (`:666` to `:684`): "name at gmail . com"; (3) a percent-encoded address is checked undecoded (`:566` to `:594`): "name%40example.com"; (4) keycap-emoji digits with spaces between them. This task, in `scrub.rs` only: a connector word (`y`, `and`, `then`, `luego`) may sit inside a spelled or digit run only when digits lie on both sides of it and the joined run's total is a phone length (exactly 7, 10 or 11 digits), so ordinary text keeps its words ("2 and 3 bedrooms", "between 9 and 5", "de 2 y 3 recámaras", "the 1200 and 1300 block", "built between 2015 and 2018", "1500 and 2000 square feet", "$25 and $75"); the known residual ("150 and 2000" joins to 7 digits and is cut) is recorded in D-4765; a token's key is percent-decoded once before the contact checks (one pass, an invalid sequence left as typed, so the result is deterministic: "name%2540example.com" decodes to "name%40example.com" and is checked as that); a lone "." between a label and a top-level domain counts as a dot only when an `at`, `arroba` or `@` appears earlier in the same run, since the TLD list (`:341` to `:343`) holds common words such as `me`, `us` and `co` ("the AC died . me and my husband" and "se rompió . me urge" keep every word); spaced keycap digits join as digits do. Tests: new corpus cases in `app/privacy/src/tests/scrub.rs` for each shape, English and Spanish, with every kept case above (the connector cases, "the AC died . me and my husband", "se rompió . me urge") left unchanged and the "%2540" case giving its stated result; its existing cases and TD-AI-09's recall floor unchanged; `prop_scrub_props.rs` and `scrub_context.rs` pass unchanged. Privacy: Opus worker (Fable once the runner's `models` map names it, D-4761), Opus privacy and security review. Update the `privacy` notes and `docs/decisions.md`.
tasks.acceptance: `app/privacy/src/tests/scrub.rs` passes with the new corpus cases and its existing cases unchanged; every kept case in the goal is untouched (connector runs not of phone length, a lone "." with no earlier at or @); TD-AI-09's recall floor holds; the scrub property tests pass unchanged.

tasks.title: jobs, core and server: a dead Payment pending timer is revived, a task that died on its last try is reaped on a busy queue, and a slow queue read is not reported as the database being down
tasks.goal: Plan change D-5081 (external code review of Nov 20, 2026, finding s F32, F35 and F36; JOB-006, JOB-014, PRIV-007, OPS-004, OPS-007; D-2640, D-3144, D-4349). Three ways a stuck task is never found or is misreported. (1) F32: the daily backstop's `check_timer` (`app/jobs/src/timer_backstop.rs`) revives only a dead `jobs.timeout` task; a Payment pending job's wait is a `picks.payment_returned` task (`PAYMENT_RETURNED_KIND`, its key built in `payment_wait.rs`), and when that one is dead the job stays in Payment pending for good, never reaches a final status, and its PRIV-007 purge is never queued. `check_timer` now also runs `revive_dead` on that key when the job is in Payment pending and its own timer is alive, under the same `MOST_REVIVALS` cap, audit row and alert; `Revival::Missing` and `Revival::Alive` on that key do nothing (no task is queued: missing is the normal state before the timer fires); the key repeats `payment_wait.rs`'s format. (2) F35: `reap_expired` (`app/core/src/tasks.rs`) runs only on a poll that claimed nothing, so on a busy queue a task whose worker died on its last attempt is never dead-lettered, is invisible to the dead-letter alert, and `queue_health`'s oldest-waiting read (`app/core/src/queue_health.rs`), which has no `attempts < max_attempts` filter, counts it until `/healthz` answers 503. The reaper now runs on every poll that claimed fewer tasks than it asked for and at least once a minute whatever was claimed, and the oldest-waiting read leaves out a row no claim can take; `reap_expired`'s and `claim`'s signatures stay; `Worker` gains no field (it is built as a struct literal in `tests/integration/tests/task_queue.rs` and `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs`): the last-reap time is a local in `claim_loop` passed to `spawn_due`, and the minute is read from `self.clock`, so a test advances a `ManualClock`. (3) F36: `check` in `app/server/src/healthz.rs` reports a queue-read error or timeout as the database being down although its round trip has just passed; it now answers 503 as today, with `status` "down", `database` "up" and `worker` "unknown" (a new `HealthState` field, built only in `healthz.rs`; `healthy()` is false for it), the answer's keys unchanged. This task adds no migration: the two indexes for `queue_health`'s `max()` reads wait for a later plan change (see D-5081), and no row of `core.task` is deleted (a done row's dedupe key means once ever). Tests, fake data only: the new `tests/integration/tests/payment_returned_backstop.rs` (a dead `payment_returned` task on a Payment pending job is revived once and the job leaves Payment pending; after the cap, one High alert; one on a job that moved on is left alone) and `tests/integration/tests/stuck_task_health.rs` (a task at its last attempt with an expired lease, beside a steady supply of due tasks, is dead-lettered within a minute and counted by the dead-letter alert, and the probe never reports the worker down for it; a failed queue read answers 503 with database up and worker unknown). Every existing `timer_backstop`, task-queue and `healthz` test passes unchanged; if one pins the reaper to an empty poll, report it, do not change it. Plan change D-5163: `app/server/CLAUDE.md` is near the D-5080 threshold, so this task's notes go to `NOTES.md` only. Build notes go to the end of each crate's `NOTES.md`; update `docs/decisions.md`.
