(1) OPS-029 says every alert that does not push "waits in the owner portal and the weekly digest", and OPS-052 says the Low volume alert is "shown in the owner portal", but the portal's list is `pushed_alerts` alone (`app/ops/src/owner_alerts.rs`, read by `alert_rows` in `app/portals/src/owner_portal.rs`), so `ops.volume_low`, `ops.volume_high`, `ops.audit_chain_broken` and every other open alert with no push row appear nowhere in the portal; D-4434 (4) said they do. `owner_alerts.rs` gains a reader of open alerts that have no push row (kind, severity, raised time, subject ID; newest first; a fixed cap), exported by one line in the shared `api.rs`, and the owner home page lists them under their own heading below the pushed ones, each with its kind's plain name and time and no acknowledge button (acknowledging stays for pushed alerts); the page stays axe-clean and every value is escaped. (2) F34: `ops.volume_low` and `ops.volume_high` are raised through `raise_kind_once` and nothing ever resolves them, so after the first breach every later one is silent. The daily check in `app/ops/src/volume_check.rs` now resolves, as the system actor, each open volume alert whose level no longer holds, with its own statements in `volume_check.rs`, written as the private `acknowledge_one` in `alerts.rs` does (the alert's `resolved_at`, one `ops.alert_ack` row by `system`, one `ops.alert_acknowledged` audit row), in one transaction: below 70% both; from 70% to 85% the High one (the Low one is raised or stays); above 85% the Low one stays open beside the High one. `alerts.rs` is not edited. (3) F33: `verify_audit_chain` in `app/server/src/offdb_stream.rs` turns every storage read error into a broken chain (`.ok()`), so a storage outage raises a High `ops.audit_chain_broken` each night. Only a not-found answer or a mismatch is a broken chain; any other adapter error is a storage error: the task fails and retries and no alert is raised; the alert itself is raised once while one is open. Tests in the new `tests/integration/tests/alert_lifecycle.rs`, PostgreSQL, fake data only: 72% then 60% raises Low and resolves it; 72%, 60%, 72% raises a second Low; 90% then 75% resolves High and leaves or raises Low; a storage fake answering an unknown outcome raises no alert and fails the task, one answering not found raises one alert, and a second night adds none; the owner home page lists an open non-pushed alert without an acknowledge button and still lists a pushed one with its button. The page's `PAGE_STATES` entry in the shared `tests/a11y/page_states.ts` gains the state with a non-pushed alert. Every existing alert, volume and audit-stream test passes unchanged. tasks.title: payments and portals: the scorecard's refund and dispute rates are read against their own charges, and a GO line worse than its STOP is refused at start-up
tasks.goal: Plan change D-5081 (external code review of Nov 20, 2026, finding s F37 and F38; OPS-039). (1) `ledger_totals` in `app/payments/src/scorecard_inputs.rs` counts refunds, disputes and charges each by their own record time inside the window, and `money_figs` in `app/portals/src/scorecard.rs` divides one by the other, so a week with two refunds of earlier charges and one new charge reads "200.0% (2 of 1)" and a week with refunds and no charge reads "No data yet". The rates are now a cohort: of the charges recorded in the window, how many have a refund and how many a dispute recorded by now, so no rate passes 100%; a window with no charge shows "No data yet" for the rate and, beside it, the plain count of refunds and disputes recorded in the window, so they are never hidden. Say in the decision entry and on the page's note that a recent window's rate can still rise. (2) `ScorecardLines::from_pairs` in `app/portals/src/scorecard_lines.rs` checks only that each key is present, so a swapped GO and STOP pair turns an amber or red figure green. It now refuses, with a new error naming the key, a line whose GO is worse than its STOP for that line's direction (equal values pass); start-up refuses as it does for a missing key, and the shipped defaults pass. Tests in the new `tests/integration/tests/scorecard_rates.rs`, PostgreSQL, fake data only: a refund in week 2 of a week-1 charge counts against week 1 and not week 2; no figure is over 100%; a week with refunds and no charge shows the count and no rate; unit cases in-crate for each direction of a swapped line, an equal pair and the shipped defaults. `tests/integration/tests/scorecard.rs` passes unchanged; if one of its cases pins the old division, report it, do not change it. `scorecard_inputs.rs` is money code under the `payments` 95% branch floor. Build notes go to the end of each crate's `NOTES.md`; update `docs/decisions.md`.
tasks.acceptance: `tests/integration/tests/scorecard_rates.rs` and the new in-crate cases pass; no scorecard figure can pass 100%; a swapped line refuses start-up and the shipped defaults start; `tests/integration/tests/scorecard.rs` passes unchanged; `app/payments/` stays at or above its branch floor.

tasks.title: payments: a dispute with no usable evidence date is still recorded and still blocks refunds
tasks.goal: Plan change D-5081 (external code review of Nov 20, 2026, finding F26; FEE-026, FEE-027; D-2073 (1)). A `charge.dispute.created` whose `evidence_details.due_by` is null is read as unreadable (`app/payments/src/routes.rs`): one High alert with no subject, no `payments.dispute` row and no ledger entry, so FEE-026's refund block never applies and an automatic refund can go out on a disputed charge; D-2073 (1) said Casey records such a dispute by hand, but no screen or caller exists for that. A `due_by` of 0 or below is stored as 1970 and its tasks fire at once. The new `migrations/0219_payments_dispute_due_optional.sql` drops `NOT NULL` from `payments.dispute.due_at`. The webhook route now treats a null, zero, negative or already-past `due_by` as no date and still records the dispute: the dispute row, the ledger entry and the dispute alert are written exactly as for a dated one, so refunds on that pick are blocked and flagged, and only the submit task and the due reminders, which need a date, are skipped; the alert says the evidence date is missing and names the pick, so Casey can act in Stripe. `record_dispute`'s existing signature stays for dated disputes; the undated case is a new entry beside it in `app/payments/src/disputes.rs`, so no done test changes except TD-FEE-43's `td_fee_43_an_unreadable_event_alerts_casey_once`, by logged spec change (D-5164): its unreadable dispute becomes one with no `payment_intent`; the odd refund status, the alert count 2, the no-dispute-row and High assertions stay. Every reader of `payments.dispute.due_at` handles a missing date: the ones in these two files (in `disputes.rs`, `mark_auto_submit` (`:213` to `:224`) neither sets `auto_submit` nor queues a submit task for an undated dispute and answers as for one it did not mark, and `list_disputes` (`:414`) reads `(due_at IS NULL OR due_at >= $1)` so an undated open dispute stays in the digest), `DisputeView.due_at` (now `Option<Timestamp>`, `models.rs`), `dispute_row` in `app/portals/src/owner_portal.rs` (an undated dispute shows `date not given by Stripe` as `due` and, unless submitted, the standing 'You need to counter or accept this one in Stripe.', never the 2-days line; no template change), and `place_dispute_holds` in `app/payments/src/purge.rs`, which this task also owns for that read alone: an undated dispute's PRIV-007 hold counts from `opened_at` in place of the missing date, and the decision entry and `docs/for-casey-review.md` say so. Tests in the new `tests/integration/tests/dispute_no_due_date.rs`, PostgreSQL with the Stripe stand-in's signing, fake data only, the event bodies built in the test: `due_by` null makes one dispute row with no date and one ledger entry, and a later refund on that pick is blocked and flagged; `due_by` 0 and a past date do the same and queue no task due in the past; an undated dispute still places its retention hold; a dated dispute behaves as today; an undated open dispute is listed by `list_disputes` and gets no submit task from `mark_auto_submit`; a negative `due_by` is undated; a null `due_by` raises no `UNREADABLE_EVENT_ALERT`; `disputes_of` returns `None` for the date; the owner refund page line for an undated dispute; and the null, zero, negative and past `due_by` paths and the undated `purge.rs:41` read each get a case (95% branch floor). Every existing dispute and refund test passes unchanged except that one TD-FEE-43 case. It is money code under the `payments` 95% branch floor. The worker updates `td_fee_43_an_unreadable_event_alerts_casey_once`'s doc comment ("a dispute with no evidence due date") to match its new body. This task does not touch `kit/plan.lock`. Build notes go to the end of `app/payments/NOTES.md`; update `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.
